### 型付き struct コンストラクタが UInt64 等のフィールド値型を保存する ✅ (Issue #4990)

- `struct FooUInt64Field; x::UInt64; end` に `FooUInt64Field(UInt64(2))`
  を渡すと、フィールドが `Int64` として保存され
  `f.x === UInt64(2)` が `false` になっていた。
- 根本原因: コンパイル時の `julia_type_to_value_type` が
  全ての符号付き / 符号なし整数幅を `ValueType::I64` に潰すため、
  `compile_struct_constructor` の `compile_expr_as(arg, I64)` が
  `DynamicToI64` を emit し、`UInt64` 値を `Int64` に変換していた。
- 修正:
  - `compile/context.rs` に `field_julia_types_by_type_id` を追加し、
    `ValueType` ではなく精密な `JuliaType`(`field_julia_types`)から
    宣言フィールド幅を取得できるようにした。
  - `compile/expr/struct_.rs` で、宣言フィールド型が幅を保持できない
    プリミティブ(`Int8/16/32/128`, `UInt8/16/32/64/128`,
    `Float16/Float32`)の場合はコンパイル時の lossy な coercion を
    スキップし、引数を素のまま compile する。
  - `vm/exec/struct_ops.rs` に `coerce_fields_to_declared_types` を
    追加し、`NewStruct` / `NewStructSplat` と
    `vm/exec/call_function_variable.rs::try_construct_default_datatype`
    の実行時に、精密な `field_julia_types` を使って
    Julia のデフォルト / `new` コンストラクタの `convert(fieldtype, x)`
    相当の coercion を適用する。
  - `Any` / 抽象 / struct / コレクション / 非数値値のフィールドは
    一切変換しない(Julia と同じく `convert` が挿入されない箇所)。
- テスト: `fixtures/struct/struct_typed_uint64_field_4990.jl`(parity OK)、
  および `struct_ops` の coercion ユニットテスト3件。

### Module 等価比較とBase 反射関数値ルックアップ ✅ (Issues #4959, #4960-#4966)

- #4959: `Base == Base` / `Base != Core` の Module 等価比較が
  `Cannot convert Module to I64` でコンパイル失敗していた。
  `compile_binary_op` の `==`/`!=` で Module オペランドを検出したら
  `BuiltinId::Egal` (恒等) へルーティングして I64 coercion を回避。
  VM 側 `Egal` / `Isequal` に `(Value::Module, Value::Module) => 名前一致`
  の arm を追加。`Base === Base` / `Base !== Core` も対応。
- #4960-#4966: `Base.return_types`, `infer_return_type`, `code_typed`,
  `code_lowered`, `widen`, `promote_type`, `promote_rule`, `convert`,
  `oftype` の関数値ルックアップが `Base has no function named X` で失敗。
  `compile_module_function_ref` の `Base.` 分岐に
  `is_base_reflection_function_value` allowlist を追加し、該当名は
  bare identifier 経路 (`Expr::Var`) へ委譲して非修飾 `<fn>` と同じ
  callable 関数値を生成。
- 新規 fixture: `reflection/module_equality_4959.jl` (7 tests),
  `reflection/base_function_value_lookup_4960.jl` (14 tests)。
  いずれも upstream Julia 1.12 と pass/fail parity 一致。

### ntuple(f, Val(N)) が Val{N} 長さラッパーから数値パラメータ N を抽出 ✅ (Issue #4975)

- `ntuple(identity, Val(3))` のように `Val(N)` を `ntuple` の長さ
  引数に直接渡すと、`Val{3}` 構造体が `n` の位置に来て
  `LoadSlotI64`/`pop_i64` が `expected I64, got StructRef` で失敗していた。
- 上流 Julia は `ntuple(f, ::Val{N})` を提供しており
  `(1, 2, 3)` を返す。
- 修正: `vm/exec/hof.rs` の `NtupleFunc` / `NtupleRuntime` で長さ
  オペランドを取り出す際に新ヘルパ `pop_ntuple_length` を使用。
  値が `Val{N}` 構造体 (`Value::Struct` / `Value::StructRef`) の場合は
  `struct_name` (`Val{3}` など) から数値パラメータ `N` をパースして
  `i64` を返す。それ以外は従来どおり `pop_i64` で数値強制し、
  非整数引数は同じ型エラーを報告する。
- 回帰テスト: `subset_julia_vm/tests/fixtures/types/ntuple_val_length_4975.jl`
  (`Val(N)` / `Val{N}()` / lambda / 名前付き関数 / クロージャ / 0・1 要素)。
  sjulia と上流 Julia でパリティ確認済み (8 passed)。
- 既知の制約: `eval(Meta.parse("f(Val{Int16(-2)}())"))` のような
  動的 eval 経由の値パラメータ構築 (Issue #4976) は別問題で未対応。
  ランタイム eval インタプリタ (`vm/builtins_macro/eval.rs`) が
  ユーザ関数/コンストラクタの実ディスパッチを持たないため、
  `Val` コンストラクタや curly-callee 呼び出しを評価できない。

### :(x.y = z) 代入のドット付き LHS が Expr(:., :x, QuoteNode(:y)) に lower される ✅ (Issue #4993)

- PR #4992 (Issue #4901) で `NodeKind::CallExpression` arm の
  callee を `cst_to_expr_constructor` で再帰させる修正を入れた
  ポストモーテム中に、構造的に同じバグが
  `NodeKind::Assignment` arm にも残っていることを発見。
  `:(x.y = z)` の LHS が flat な `Symbol("x.y")` に潰されていた。
- 上流 Julia:
  ```julia
  julia> typeof(:(x.y = z).args[1])
  Expr        # Expr(:., :x, QuoteNode(:y))
  ```
- 修正: `subset_julia_vm/src/lowering/expr/quote/cst_to_constructor.rs`
  の `NodeKind::Assignment` arm で、LHS が `FieldExpression` の
  場合のみ `cst_to_expr_constructor` で再帰させる。それ以外の
  ケース (Identifier、`$tmp` のような `UnaryExpression` 補間)
  は既存の `walker.text(target)` パスを維持。後者を雑に再帰させると
  `gensym_in_macro.jl` の `$tmp = $a` パターンが
  `handlers.rs::extract_symbol_from_constructor` で
  `expected SymbolNew expression` エラーになる
  (Var ノードは現状ハンドラーが扱えない)。
- 新規 fixture `macros/quote_assign_dotted_lhs_4993.jl` で
  `:(x.y = z)`, `:(Mod.field = 42)`, `:(x = 1)` の 3 ケースを
  pin。`scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh` で上流と一致確認。
- 129/129 fixture chunks pass、clippy 0 warnings。

### :(M.f(x)) 呼び出しのドット付き callee が Expr(:., :M, QuoteNode(:f)) に lower される ✅ (Issue #4901)

- Surfaced from the fixture for Issue #4899 (PR #4903, field-access
  quote). 単独の `:(a.b)` は PR #4903 で正しい
  `Expr(:., :a, QuoteNode(:b))` 形になっていたが、ドット名が
  call の callee である `:(Base.foo(x))` では別の lowering 経路
  (`NodeKind::CallExpression` arm) が callee を flat な
  `Symbol("Base.foo")` に潰してしまっていた。
- 上流 Julia の出力:
  ```julia
  julia> ex = :(Base.foo(x));
  julia> typeof(ex.args[1])
  Expr
  julia> ex.args[1]
  :(Base.foo)   # Expr(:., :Base, QuoteNode(:foo))
  ```
  sjulia は `Symbol("Base.foo")` を返していた。
- 修正: `subset_julia_vm/src/lowering/expr/quote/cst_to_constructor.rs`
  の `NodeKind::CallExpression` arm を、callee の素のテキストを
  Symbol で包む代わりに `cst_to_expr_constructor` で再帰させる。
  これによって `FieldExpression` callee は PR #4903 で追加した
  arm を通り、正しい `Expr(:., obj, QuoteNode(:f))` 形になる。
  Identifier / Operator callee はそれぞれ自身の arm が既に
  `Symbol(text)` を出すので、`:(f(x))` 等の単純 case は変わらない。
- 新規 fixture `macros/quote_call_dotted_callee_4901.jl` で
  `:(Base.foo(x))`, `:(foo(x))`, `:(Foo.Bar.baz(x))`,
  `:(Base.foo(x, y))` を pinning。`scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`
  で上流と pass/fail 一致を確認。
- 1931/1931 lib tests pass、129/129 fixture chunks pass、
  clippy 0 warnings。

### パラメトリック構造体インスタンス化の reflection parity ✅ (Issue #3909)

- `fieldnames` / `fieldcount` / `fieldtypes` / `supertype` を `Box{Int64}`
  のようなパラメトリック構造体インスタンス化で本家と一致 (`vm/type_objects.rs`)。
  `RuntimeTypeRegistry` がベース名 (`Box`) でパラメトリックスキーマを解決し、
  `field_types` は宣言型パラメータを具体型引数で置換 (ネスト / 繰り返し型変数を
  含む)、`supertype` は self-reference バグを修正 (親無し→`Any`、`AbsB{T}`→
  `AbsB{Int64}`)。`CoreType` は意味表現のまま、identity/layout/置換は registry
  が所有する #3909 方針に整合。
- fixture `reflection/parametric_instantiation_reflection_3909.jl` (22 アサーション、
  parity 一致) + Rust 単体テスト 4 件。未対応: 組込み `DenseVector`/`DenseArray`
  階層、`Vector{Int}.parameters` の `N` (#4722)、パラメトリック親への subtype。

## 最新対応 (2026-05-28)

### :0xFF / :0b1010 preserve hex/binary literal types ✅ (Issue #4927)

- Surfaced from PR #4926 (Issue #4923): `:0xFF` evaluated to
  `Int64(255)` instead of `UInt8(0xFF)`. Bare `0xFF` correctly
  produces `UInt8`, so the type loss was specifically on the
  colon-prefix-of-literal path.
- Root cause: the `cst_to_expr_constructor::IntegerLiteral` arm
  called `parse_int` (untyped), which discarded the hex / binary /
  octal width tag. The bare-literal lowering uses
  `lower_integer_literal` which goes through `parse_int_typed` and
  wraps in a `UInt8` / `UInt16` / … constructor for typed kinds.
- Fix: change the visibility of `lower_integer_literal` to
  `pub(super)` and reuse it from
  `subset_julia_vm/src/lowering/expr/quote/cst_to_constructor.rs`'s
  `NodeKind::IntegerLiteral` arm. The now-unused `parse_int`
  helper is gated to `#[cfg(test)]` since its tests still
  reference the untyped variant.
- New fixture `macros/colon_hex_type_4927.jl` pins `:0xFF`,
  `:0x100`, `:0x10000`, `:0b1010`, `:0b1_0000_0000` with `===`
  (which checks both value AND type), plus a decimal regression
  guard (`:42 === 42`, `typeof(:42) === Int64`).
- 2712/2712 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Colon-prefix on literal: :42 / :"hi" / :'A' / :3.14 ✅ (Issue #4923)

- Surfaced from PR #4921 (Issue #4920): the parser rejected
  `:42` (and other `:literal` forms) so the natural test case
  `:(:42) → QuoteNode(42)` could not be expressed. Upstream Julia
  treats `:literal` as a quote of a self-quoting value — at the
  top level it evaluates to the literal itself
  (`typeof(:42) === Int64`); inside an outer quote `:(:42)` it
  becomes `QuoteNode(42)`.
- Fix (two parts):
  1. In `subset_julia_vm_parser/src/parser/expressions/primary.rs`,
     add an arm in `parse_colon_prefix` for numeric / char /
     string literal tokens that produces a `QuoteExpression` CST
     node with the literal as a child (with-children form).
  2. In `subset_julia_vm/src/lowering/expr/quote/cst_to_constructor.rs`,
     restructure `lower_quote_expr` to branch on
     `children.is_empty()` instead of the text-shape heuristic so
     the with-children path returns the inner literal's
     constructor directly. Also add a `NodeKind::CharacterLiteral`
     arm to `cst_to_expr_constructor` (was missing).
- The nested case `:(:42)` continues to produce `QuoteNode(42)`
  via the `NodeKind::QuoteExpression` recursion arm from
  PR #4914 / #4921.
- New fixture `macros/colon_literal_4923.jl` covers `:42`,
  `:0xFF`, `:0b1010`, `:3.14`, `:"hello"`, `:'A'`, tight binding
  (`:1 + 2 == 3`), and the nested-case regression guard.
- 2712/2712 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Meta-quote of complex Expr lowers to Expr(:quote, ...) ✅ (Issue #4920)

- Refinement of PR #4914 (#4911). Pre-#4920 the with-children form
  of meta-quote always emitted `QuoteNode(...)`. Upstream Julia
  branches on the inner kind: atom → `QuoteNode`, complex Expr →
  `Expr(:quote, …)`. Macros that pattern-match on `Expr(:quote, …)`
  needed the upstream shape.
- Fix: in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/lowering/expr/quote/cst_to_constructor.rs`,
  the `NodeKind::QuoteExpression` arm now inspects the inner CST
  kind. Atom variants (`Identifier`, `Operator`,
  `IntegerLiteral`, `FloatLiteral`, `StringLiteral`,
  `CharacterLiteral`, `BooleanLiteral`, and `QuoteExpression`
  itself for triple-quote leaves) emit `QuoteNode(inner)`. Every
  other variant emits `Expr(:quote, inner)`.
- New fixture `macros/quote_metaquote_expr_4920.jl` pins
  atom-inner meta-quote (regression guard from #4911), Expr-inner
  with binary op `:(:(x+y))`, call `:(:(f(a,b)))`, and tuple
  `:(:((a, b, c)))`.
- 2712/2712 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### QuoteNode === QuoteNode is reflexive (partial #4915) ✅

- Surfaced from PR #4914 (Issue #4911, meta-quote): `===` on two
  `QuoteNode` values fell through the `Egal` builtin's main
  `match (&left, &right)` block to `_ => false`, so
  `QuoteNode(:x) === QuoteNode(:x)` returned `false` even when both
  operands wrapped the same Symbol.
- Fix: in `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/builtins_equality.rs`, add a
  `(Value::QuoteNode(a), Value::QuoteNode(b))` arm right after the
  existing `Expr` arm. Compares the wrapped inner values
  structurally via Debug representation, matching the policy
  already used for `Expr` and `Tuple`.
- New fixture `macros/quotenode_egal_4915.jl` pins reflexivity,
  value equality, inequality, and interop with the meta-quote
  lowering from PR #4914 (`:(:foo) === QuoteNode(:foo)`).
- Scope: `===` only. The companion `==` operator still errors
  with `Compilation error: "Cannot convert QuoteNode to I64"` at
  compile time — the dispatch tries to coerce QuoteNode operands
  to integers before reaching any runtime equality arm.
  Compile-time fix is the remaining piece of #4915.
- 2712/2712 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Meta-quote :(:foo) lowers to QuoteNode(:foo) ✅ (Issue #4911)

- Third gap closed from the #4893 audit matrix (after #4899's
  field access and #4904's splat). `:(:foo)` — a Symbol literal
  nested inside an outer quote — previously raised
  `UnsupportedExpression("quote for quote_expression not yet supported")`.
- Fix: in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/lowering/expr/quote/cst_to_constructor.rs`,
  add a `NodeKind::QuoteExpression` arm that handles both forms —
  the leaf `:foo` (parses the Symbol name from the leaf text) and
  the with-children `:(expr)` form (recurses then wraps in
  `QuoteNode`). The accurate-upstream behaviour of producing
  `Expr(:quote, …)` for non-atom inner expressions is approximated
  as `QuoteNode(quoted_inner)` and tracked for follow-up.
- New fixture `macros/quote_metaquote_4911.jl` pins leaf-form
  meta-quote for plain Symbols (`:(:foo)`, `:(:bar)`),
  operator-name Symbols (`:(:%)`, `:(:+)`), and verifies the
  returned QuoteNode is `isa QuoteNode` with the same `typeof()`
  as a user-constructed `QuoteNode(:foo)`. Equality via `==` is
  not asserted because sjulia currently errors with `Cannot
  convert QuoteNode to I64` on QuoteNode equality dispatch —
  separate follow-up.
- Matrix fixture `quote_lowering_matrix_4893.jl` updated to move
  meta-quote out of "Known gaps" — three remaining variants there
  now (let, comprehension, matrix).
- 2712/2712 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Parse :. and :... as Symbol literals ✅ (Issue #4908)

- Parser rejected `:.` (Symbol `"."`) and `:...` (Symbol `"..."`)
  with `ParseFailed`. These are the canonical Symbol forms of the
  field-access and splat Expr heads — needed for asserting them
  cleanly in tests instead of falling back to `Symbol(name)`. Both
  fixture PRs #4903 (field access, #4899) and #4906 (splat,
  #4904) had to use the `Symbol(name)` workaround.
- Root cause: `Token::Dot` and `Token::Ellipsis` are deliberately
  excluded from `Token::is_operator()` (they have grammatical
  meaning as field-access and splat markers), so they fell through
  the `parse_colon_prefix` arms in
  `subset_julia_vm_parser/src/parser/expressions/primary.rs` to
  the standalone-colon catch-all.
- Fix: add an explicit `Some(Token::Dot) | Some(Token::Ellipsis)`
  arm right after the `is_operator()` arm — same shape (produces a
  `NodeKind::QuoteExpression` leaf with the operator's text).
- New fixture `macros/symbol_dot_literal_4908.jl` pins `:.` /
  `:...` parse and equal their `Symbol(name)` equivalents, plus
  interop with quoted Expr heads (`:(a.b).head === :.`), plus a
  regression guard so other operator-name Symbol literals (`:+`,
  `:-`, `:*`, `:(==)`, `:%`) stay intact.
- 2712/2712 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Quoted splat :(f(args...)) lowers to Expr(:..., :args) ✅ (Issue #4904)

- Second gap closed from the #4893 audit matrix (after #4899's
  field access). `:(f(args...))` previously raised
  `UnsupportedExpression("quote for splat_expression not yet supported")`.
- Fix: in `subset_julia_vm/src/lowering/expr/quote/cst_to_constructor.rs`,
  add a `NodeKind::SplatExpression` arm that emits the canonical
  `Expr(:..., inner)` — head is the three-dot Symbol literally
  named `"..."`, single child is the recursively-quoted operand.
- New fixture `macros/quote_splat_4904.jl` covers trailing
  `f(args...)`, mid-list `g(a, xs..., b)`, single-splat
  `h(xs...)`, and splat of an arbitrary `(a + b)...` expression.
  Matrix fixture `quote_lowering_matrix_4893.jl` updated to move
  splat out of "Known gaps" — four remaining variants there now
  (let, meta-quote, comprehension, matrix).
- 2712/2712 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Quoted field access :(a.b) lowers to Expr(:., :a, QuoteNode(:b)) ✅ (Issue #4899)

- First gap closed from the audit fixture in PR #4898 (Issue
  #4893): `:(a.b)` previously raised
  `UnsupportedExpression("quote for field_expression not yet
  supported")`. Upstream Julia lowers field access to
  `Expr(:., obj, QuoteNode(:field))` — note the second arg is a
  `QuoteNode` wrapping the field-name Symbol, not a bare Symbol.
- Fix: in `subset_julia_vm/src/lowering/expr/quote/cst_to_constructor.rs`,
  add a `NodeKind::FieldExpression` arm that emits the canonical
  three-arg `Expr(:., obj, QuoteNode(:field))`. Two named children:
  the object (recursively quoted) and the field-name identifier.
- Discovered while writing the fixture: a related gap on the
  call-with-dotted-callee form (`:(M.f(x))` produces a flat
  `:M.f` Symbol instead of an `Expr(:., :M, QuoteNode(:f))`).
  That lives in the `CallExpression`-quote arm, not the
  `FieldExpression` one. Tracked separately in #4901.
- New fixture `macros/quote_field_access_4899.jl` pins bare field
  access, module-qualified access, and nested `x.y.z` chains. Also
  moves the field-access entry out of `quote_lowering_matrix_4893.jl`'s
  "Known gaps" list — five remaining variants there now.
- 2712/2712 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Quote-lowering coverage matrix (regression guard) ✅ (Issue #4893)

- Prevention follow-up to PRs #4888 (#4872) and #4892 (#4890): the
  quote-lowering pass in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/lowering/expr/quote/cst_to_constructor.rs`
  used to surface each unsupported `NodeKind` variant only when a
  user tripped over it. This PR adds a matrix-style regression
  guard that pins every variant currently supported (literal,
  identifier, operator, tuple/vect/curly aggregates, call, binary
  op, control flow, assignment/ternary/range, try-catch) so any
  future change immediately reveals regression — and documents the
  six remaining `NodeKind` variants that still fall to the
  catch-all (field access, let, meta-quote, comprehension, matrix,
  splat) as inline comments so the next contributor sees the audit
  results at-a-glance.
- Discovered as a side effect of writing the audit:
  Issue #4895 — `:(nothing)` / `:(missing)` quote to the literal
  values rather than upstream's `:nothing` / `:missing` Symbols.
  The trivial one-line fix breaks the Pure-Julia `@test` macro
  (which terminates its `quote ... end` block with a bare
  `nothing` to make the macro return nothing), so the gap is
  documented at the special-case arm and tracked in #4895 pending
  macro-expansion-scope binding support.
- 2712/2712 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Quoted vector literals and parametric types lower correctly ✅ (Issue #4890)

- Follow-up to PR #4888 (Issue #4872, quoted operator). Once the
  operator-quote slice was fixed, the next two `NodeKind` variants
  in the original reproducer
  (`:(Base.infer_exception_type(%, Tuple{Int64,Int64}))`) hit the
  same catch-all fall-through:
  - `:([1, 2, 3])` → `UnsupportedExpression("quote for vector_expression not yet supported")`
  - `:(Tuple{Int, Int})` → `... "quote for parametrized_type_expression not yet supported"`
- Fix: add top-level arms in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/lowering/expr/quote/cst_to_constructor.rs`:
  - `NodeKind::VectorExpression` → `Expr(:vect, elements...)`
  - `NodeKind::ParametrizedTypeExpression` → `Expr(:curly, base, params...)`
  Both mirror the existing `NodeKind::TupleExpression` shape and the
  head Symbol matches upstream Julia's `base/expr.jl` lowering
  convention.
- New fixture `macros/quote_vector_parametric_4890.jl` covers
  vector-literal head/args, parametric-type head/args (including
  multi-parameter `Dict{String, Int}`), the combined #4872+#4890
  reproducer, and a `TupleExpression`-quote regression guard.
- 2712/2712 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Quoted bare operators lower to Symbol ✅ (Issue #4872)

- A bare operator inside a quoted expression — `:(%)`, `:(+)`,
  `:(*)`, `:(==)`, or an operator used as a value like
  `:(reduce(+, xs))` — was rejected during lowering with
  `UnsupportedExpression("quote for operator not yet supported")`.
  Upstream Julia treats a quoted operator as a `Symbol`, identical
  to a quoted identifier.
- Fix: in `subset_julia_vm/src/lowering/expr/quote/cst_to_constructor.rs`,
  add a top-level `NodeKind::Operator` arm right after the existing
  `NodeKind::Identifier` arm. The operator's text becomes
  `Symbol(text)` via the same `BuiltinOp::SymbolNew` builtin the
  identifier path already uses.
- New fixture `macros/quoted_operator_4872.jl` covers `:(%)`,
  `:(+)`, `:(*)`, `:(/)`, `:(-)`, `:(==)`, `:(<)`, `:(>)`, `:(<=)`,
  `:(>=)` each equaling the shorthand Symbol form, plus a
  regression guard so the existing quoted-identifier path stays
  intact. The remaining `parametrized_type_expression` and
  `vector_expression` quote gaps surfaced by the original
  reproducer are out of scope here and tracked separately.
- 2712/2712 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### BigInt/BigFloat === is reflexive ✅ (Issue #4883)

- `x === x` returned `false` for any `BigInt` (or `BigFloat`) bound
  to the same local, breaking reflexivity of `===`. Surfaced while
  writing the carrier-matrix testset for #4878 — `x[1] === x`
  failed only for `x = big(7)` in a 7-value sweep.
- Root cause: the `Egal` builtin in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/builtins_equality.rs` had no
  `(Value::BigInt, Value::BigInt)` arm (nor `BigFloat`), so the
  comparison fell through to the `_ => false` catch-all.
- Fix: add value-equality arms for both `BigInt` and `BigFloat`.
  Upstream Julia has reference-identity semantics for these mutable
  struct types; sjulia stores them as value types, so the fix
  trades full reference-identity for value-equality. Documented
  tradeoff: `x === x` is now correct (the common case), but two
  distinct `big(7)` instances also compare `===` as true (upstream
  returns false). Matches the policy every other `Number` arm in
  this match already uses.
- New fixture `arithmetic/bigint_egal_4883.jl` only asserts cases
  where both sjulia and upstream agree (reflexivity for the same
  binding, alias preservation via `y = x`), plus a Number-primitive
  regression guard so the new arms don't shadow the existing ones.
- 2712/2712 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### ndims(::Char) returns 0 like other scalar carriers ✅ (Issue #4878)

- First payoff of the prevention refactor in #4875 / PR #4877: while
  auditing the other scalar-aware builtins, `ndims('A')` was found
  to still raise `Type error: ndims: expected array or number, got
  Char('A')` — exactly the same shape as the `length(::Char)` gap
  fixed earlier today in #4871. The `Char` (and `BigInt`/`BigFloat`)
  carriers were missing from `vm/builtins_arrays.rs::Ndims`'s
  inline scalar arm.
- Fix: replace the inline
  `matches!(... I8 | I16 | ...)` allow-list with a delegation to
  the shared `is_scalar_carrier` predicate. Mirrors what `Length`
  and `IndexLoad` already do, so the `Number ∪ AbstractChar`
  boundary stays in lock-step across the triple (`length`,

- New fixture `arithmetic/ndims_char_4878.jl` covers `ndims` for

### Centralize scalar 0-dim carrier predicate ✅ (Issue #4875)

- Prevention follow-up to two same-class bugs landed earlier today
  (#4814 scalar `getindex` → PR #4870; #4871 `length(::Char)` →
  PR #4873). Both bugs were the same shape: each builtin maintained
  its own *implicit* list of which `Value` variants count as a
  scalar 0-dim collection, and the lists drifted.
- Fix: extract a shared
  `is_scalar_carrier(v: &Value) -> bool` predicate in a new module
  `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/value/predicates.rs` that returns `true`
  for every `Number` and `AbstractChar` subtype (matching upstream
  Julia's hierarchy). Replace the local `is_scalar_indexable_value`
  helper from #4870 in `vm/exec/array_index.rs` and the inline
  `matches!(... I8 | I16 | ...)` arm from #4873 in
  `vm/builtins_collections.rs::Length` with calls to the shared
  predicate.
- Pure refactor — no behavior change observable to user code. The
  three unit tests inside `predicates.rs` pin: (a) every numeric
  and `Char` carrier is a scalar; (b) `Symbol`/`Nothing`/`Missing`
  are not (upstream raises `MethodError` on `:foo[1]`); (c) `String`
  is not (`AbstractString` has its own collection semantics).
- 2712/2712 tests pass (3 new unit tests for the predicate), clippy
  0 warnings.

### length(::Char) / length(::BigInt/BigFloat) return 1 ✅ (Issue #4871)

### Scalar getindex (x[1] == x) for Number / AbstractChar ✅ (Issue #4814)

- `x[1]` for a scalar raised `Type error: indexing not supported for
  I64(N)` instead of upstream Julia's `x[1] === x` 0-dim-collection
  semantics. The most visible downstream impact was
  `vcat(scalar, vec, ...)` — a common idiom — whose Pure-Julia body
  indexes each arg via `args[i][j]`. The array-literal splat lowering

- Fix: in `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/exec/array_index.rs::IndexLoad`,
  the fallthrough `other =>` arm now first checks

  and `AbstractChar` subtypes (I8…I128, U8…U128, BigInt, F16/F32/F64,
  BigFloat, Bool, Char) — exactly what upstream Julia indexes — and
  returns `other` for `x[1]` or raises `BoundsError` otherwise.
  `Symbol`/`Nothing`/`Missing` are deliberately excluded (upstream
  also raises `MethodError` on `:foo[1]`).

### @show emits values in show-form, matching upstream lowering ✅ (Issue #4865)

- `@show "positive"` produced `x = positive` (no quotes) and
  `@show :foo` produced `y = foo` (no leading colon), because the
  `_do_show` helper in `base/macros.jl` routed the value through
  `println(... value)` — which uses print-form. Ints and floats
  already matched because their `print` and `show` forms agree.
- Fix: align `_do_show` with upstream Julia's `@show` lowering in
  `julia/base/show.jl:1283-1291`, which expands to
  `println(EXPR_STR * " = ", repr(value))`. `repr(value)` produces
  the show-form String once; `println` then emits it verbatim
  (println uses print-form for String args, so the embedded quotes
  / colon survive).
- New fixture `show_macro_form_4865.jl` pins both halves: `@show`
  preserves the value's identity (regression guard for the existing
  return-value contract) and `repr(value)` produces the canonical
  show-form text for the cases the bug affected (String, Symbol,
  Char, Tuple, Vector, primitives, Nothing, Missing). `repr` is
  what `_do_show` now feeds into `println`, so anchoring on it pins
  the user-visible `... = VALUE` line.
- 2709/2709 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Multi-line ternary parses newline after `?` and inner `:` ✅ (Issue #4862)

- The parser rejected a newline immediately after `?` in a ternary
  expression with `ParseFailed("unexpected token '\n' ..., expected
  expression")`. Upstream Julia treats `?` as a line-continuation
  token. Surfaced while writing the fixture for #4856 — having to
  convert a multi-line `?:` to `if/else` was an unnecessary
  workaround.
- Root cause: the binary-operator continuation loop in
  `subset_julia_vm_parser/src/parser/expressions/mod.rs` already lists
  `?` in its accept-continuation comment, but the ternary dispatch
  path (mod.rs ~L48) bypasses that loop and goes straight to
  `parse_ternary`, which was not eating newlines on its own.
- Fix: in `subset_julia_vm_parser/src/parser/expressions/types.rs`,
  added `while self.check(&Token::Newline) { self.advance(); }`
  blocks right after consuming `Token::Question` and after the inner
  `Token::Colon`, so both `cond ?\n then : else` and
  `cond ? then :\n else` shapes parse — symmetric with the existing
  binary-operator continuation policy.
- New fixture `multiline_newline_4862.jl` pins six cases: newline
  after `?`, newline after `:`, both, nested multi-line, multi-line
  inside a function body, plus a single-line regression guard.
- 2709/2709 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Nested immutable field reads preserve declared union type ✅ (Issue #4856)

- `x.inner.value` and `getfield(getfield(x, :inner), :value)` (and the
  equivalent triple-nested chains) widened to `Any` instead of
  preserving `InnerProbe.value`'s declared `Union{Int64, Nothing}`
  type. Single-level reads (Issue #4270) already worked.
- Root cause: `StructField::as_julia_type()` only returns `Some` for
  `TypeExpr::Concrete`, so a user-struct-typed field like
  `inner::InnerProbe` (parsed as `TypeExpr::Named`) fell through to
  `ValueType::Any`. The lattice struct table therefore stored
  `OuterProbe.inner` as `Any`, and the abstract-interp engine could
  not chain into `InnerProbe.value`'s declared union type — the
  nested struct identity was lost on the way into the engine.
- Fix: in `subset_julia_vm/src/compile/mod.rs`, fall back to
  `type_expr_to_string + JuliaType::from_name_or_struct` for any
  typed field (not just `Union`-typed). Struct-typed fields now land
  as `ValueType::Struct(type_id)` whenever the field's struct is
  already registered in `struct_table` (defined earlier in source
  order); both the `fields` (`ValueType`) and
  `field_julia_types` (`JuliaType`) projections use the same
  fallback so the two stay in lock-step.
- New fixture `nested_field_union_4856.jl` pins the canonical
  pattern: nested field guard, nested getfield-chain guard,
  single-level struct-typed field, triple-nested chain, plus a
  behavioral check on actual struct values.
- 2709/2709 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Tuple{Vararg{T,N}} dispatch binds T and N ✅ (Issue #4841)

- `v(xs::Tuple{Vararg{T,N}}) where {T,N} = (T, N)` and similar
  signatures previously failed at compile time with
  `Dispatch(NoMethodFound)` because `Vararg{T,N}` was not recognized
  by `JuliaType::from_name`. It fell through to
  `JuliaType::Struct("Vararg{T,N}")` inside a one-element `TupleOf`,
  so the element-wise tuple matcher refused any multi-element call
  site.
- Fix: in `subset_julia_vm/src/types/julia_type/parsing.rs`, the
  `Tuple{...}` arm now detects a single inner `Vararg{element,length}`
  param and canonicalizes the type to the equivalent
  `NTuple{length, element}` form. Upstream Julia treats these as the
  same type (NTuple is `Tuple{Vararg{T,N}}` with the arg order
  swapped), so reusing the existing NTuple infrastructure — dispatch
  matching, val-parameter detection in `compile/mod.rs ~L1733`, and
  runtime length/type binding in `vm/mod.rs ~L2600` — covers both
  spellings without duplicating logic.
- Scope: two-argument `Vararg{T,N}`. The unbounded one-arg form
  `Vararg{T}` (e.g. `Tuple{Vararg{T}}`) is left untranslated since it
  carries no length parameter and would require a distinct code path;
  it remains a pre-existing limitation tracked separately.
- New fixture `vararg_tuple_value_param_4841.jl` pins the canonical
  binding pattern (`T`, `N`, both-typevar, concrete-N, concrete-T)
  plus a regression guard so the `NTuple{N,T}` spelling keeps
  working.
- 2709/2709 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### log(-1) emits Union{DomainError, InexactError} ✅ (Issue #4700 follow-up)

- Same-day follow-up to PR #4838: wired the new

- Refactored the previous shared `log | log10 |

### ExceptionType gains Union variant ✅ (Issue #4700)

- The `ExceptionType` lattice could only represent
  `Bottom` / `Known(name)` / `Any` — no way to express
  a union of multiple exception types like upstream's
  `Base.infer_exception_type(() -> log(-1))` →
  `Union{DomainError, InexactError}`. PR #4699
  documented this as a known gap when adding
  const-value refinement for `log`/`sqrt`.
- Fix: added a
  `Union(BTreeSet<&'static str>)` variant to
  `ExceptionType`. Implemented an `ExceptionType::merge`
  helper that performs lattice union with proper
  canonicalization:
  - `Any` is absorbing,
  - `Bottom` is identity,
  - same `Known` stays `Known`,
  - distinct `Known` promote to `Union`,
  - `Known + Union` / `Union + Union` extend the set,
  - 0-element sets collapse to `Bottom`, 1-element to
    `Known`.
- Coverage: 8 unit tests in a new
  `exception_union_4700` module covering identity,
  absorbing, same-Known, distinct-Known, Union+Known
  extend, Union-already-contains-Known idempotent,
  Union+Union extend, and insertion-order
  independence.
- Scope: lattice infrastructure only. Wiring this
  through `typed_exception_type_for_expr` to actually
  emit `Union{DomainError, InexactError}` for
  `log(-1)` is a separate follow-up under #4274 /
  #4699.
- 2708/2708 tests pass (2700 existing + 8 new),
  clippy 0 warnings.

### Multi-comp returns 2D Matrix ✅ (Issue #4779)

- `[expr for i in R1, j in R2]` returned a flat 1D
  `Vector{T}` of length `length(R1) * length(R2)`
  instead of upstream's 2D `Matrix{T}` of shape
  `(length(R1), length(R2))`. The iteration order was
  already column-major (outermost loop = last
  iteration), so the flat element order was correct;
  only the dimension/shape was missing.
- Fix: at the end of
  `compile_multi_comprehension`, for n>=2 iterations,
  load each `len_var` onto the stack and emit
  `Instr::CallBuiltin(BuiltinId::Reshape, 1 + n)`.
  The flat column-major element layout becomes a
  proper multi-dimensional Array. Extends to 3+
  iterations (`[expr for i in R1, j in R2, k in R3]`
  → `Array{T, 3}` shape `(R1, R2, R3)`).
- Known related issue (separate, out of scope):
  multi-op body inference (`i+j+k`) falls through to
  the F64 default and produces an `Array{Float64, N}`
  even when the body is Int-valued at runtime.
  Single-var body (`i`) infers correctly.
- Coverage: 2D Int / 2D Float, iteration-order
  row/col position checks, 3D Array, 1D
  single-iterator comprehension regression guard.
- New fixture `comprehension_multi_2d_matrix_4779`
  (5 testsets, 18 assertions), parity-verified against
  upstream julia via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 2700/2700 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Nested try-as-expression propagates inner value ✅ (Issue #4833)

- Follow-up to #4784 / PR #4832 filed and fixed in the
  same session.
  `r = try; try; 1; catch; 2; end; catch; 3; end`
  raised `UndefVarError: __sjvm_try_result_<N>` at
  runtime because the inner try was the last statement
  of the outer try body. The `assign_last_value` helper
  only converted `Stmt::Expr` last-statements into
  `Stmt::Assign` into the outer result variable;
  `Stmt::Try` fell through unchanged, leaving the
  outer result var unassigned.
- Fix: made `assign_last_value` recursive — when the
  last statement of a branch is itself a `Stmt::Try`,
  recursively rewrite its branches so the inner's last
  expression flows back to the SAME outer result
  variable. Other non-expression statements
  (Stmt::Return, etc.) still fall through unchanged.
- Coverage: inner success propagates, inner caught
  propagates, inner re-raises so outer catches, triple
  nested, nested-try as RHS in arithmetic, simple
  (non-nested) try-as-expr regression guard.
- New fixture `nested_try_catch_expression_4833`
  (6 testsets, 6 assertions), parity-verified against
  upstream julia.
- 2700/2700 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### try/catch/end works as a first-class expression ✅ (Issue #4784)

- `result = try ... catch ... end` (assignment RHS) and
  similar use inside larger expressions (`1 + (try ...
  catch; 0 end)`, function returns) failed at parse with
  `ParseFailed("expected expression")`. Upstream Julia
  treats try/catch as a first-class expression whose
  value is the last expression in whichever branch ran.
- Two-stage fix:
  1. **Parser**: added `Token::KwTry` to the
     primary-expression dispatch in
     `parser/expressions/primary.rs`, mirroring how
     `KwIf` and `KwLet` are accepted as expressions.
  2. **Lowering**: added a `NodeKind::TryStatement` arm
     to `lower_expr` (and the context-aware variant)
     that rewrites the last `Stmt::Expr` of each branch
     (try / catch / else) into an `Stmt::Assign` to a
     fresh `__sjvm_try_result_<span>` variable, and
     wraps the modified try-statement plus a final
     read of that variable in an `Expr::LetBlock`. The
     LetBlock's "last statement is the block's value"
     semantics then yield the right answer.
- Known limitation (separate follow-up): nested
  try-as-expression where the inner try is the last
  expression of an outer try body doesn't propagate the
  inner value back to the outer rewrite — the inner is
  treated as a statement inside the outer's try_block.
  Out of scope for the first slice.
- Coverage (fixture try_catch_expression_4784,
  parity-verified against upstream julia): success
  path, exception path, named catch var, inside
  arithmetic (success + exception), and the bare
  statement-form regression guard.
- 2700/2700 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### typeof('a':'e') is StepRange{Char, Int64} ✅ (Issue #4830)

- Follow-up to #4795 final slice (PR #4829). The

  paths so they classify Char ranges as
  `StepRange{Char, Int64}` regardless of step value:
  1. `vm/value/value_enum.rs::runtime_type` (typeof
     root)
  2. `vm/type_ops/introspection.rs::value_type`
     (runtime typeof)
  3. `vm/exec/call_dynamic.rs::is_native_range_candidate_mismatch`
     (method dispatch matching)
  Also updated compile-time
  `compile/expr/infer/julia_type.rs::Expr::Range` to
  return `StepRange` when start is Char-typed.
- Coverage: typeof / isa StepRange / isa UnitRange /
  isa AbstractRange / repr matches show / direct show
  via IOBuffer / numeric typeof regression / numeric
  isa regression.
- New fixture `numeric_char_range_typeof_4830`
  (7 testsets, 11 assertions), parity-verified against
  upstream julia via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 2700/2700 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Multi-line trailing-comma literal parses ✅ (Issue #4776)

- Multi-line tuple/array/call literals with a trailing
  comma — `(1,\n 2,\n 3,\n)`, `[\n 1,\n 2,\n]`,
  `f(\n a,\n b,\n)` — failed at parse with
  "unexpected token ')' expected expression". The
  single-line trailing-comma form `(1, 2, 3,)` worked.
- Three parser bugs contributed:
  1. Tuple parser: trailing-comma RParen check ran
     before the newline-skip that follows the comma,
     so the parser tried to parse_expression on the
     closing paren and errored.
  2. Vector parser: did not skip newlines after the
     opening `[` (the tuple entry point already did),
     so `[\n 1, ...]` failed at `[\n`.
  3. None of tuple / vector / call parsers skipped
     newlines before `expect(RParen)` /
     `expect(RBracket)`, so the no-trailing-comma
     multi-line shape `(1,\n 2,\n 3\n)` failed at
     `3\n`.
- Fix: unified the three parser paths to skip newlines
  (a) inside the loop before the trailing-comma
  closing-bracket check, (b) right after the opening
  bracket, and (c) right before the final
  closing-bracket expectation. Three small edits across
  `parser/collections.rs` and
  `parser/expressions/calls.rs`.
- Coverage: tuple / vector / call / named-tuple
  multi-line trailing-comma form; no-trailing-comma
  multi-line form (unblocked as a side effect);
  single-element multi-line `[42,]` and `(42,)`;
  single-line trailing-comma regression guard;
  multi-line call with mixed arg types.
- New fixture `parse_multiline_trailing_comma_4776`
  (9 testsets, 11 assertions), parity-verified against
  upstream julia via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 2700/2700 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### print(buf, ::LinRange) / string(::LinRange) match show-form ✅ (Issue #4761)

- `print(buf::IOBuffer, r::LinRange)`, `string(r)`,
  `print(stdout, r)`, and `println(stdout, r)` leaked the
  raw 4-field struct dump
  `LinRange{Float64}(0.0, 1.0, 5, 4)` (the trailing `4` is
  the internal `lendiv` helper field) instead of matching
  the user-facing `show(io, ::LinRange)` form
  `LinRange{Float64}(0.0, 1.0, 5)`.
- Root cause: `vm/formatting.rs::format_struct_instance`
  has special-case arms for Rational, Pair, and the
  Array wrapper, but no arm for LinRange, so the generic
  `StructName(field1, ...)` fallback dumped all four
  fields including the internal `lendiv`.
- Fix: added a LinRange special-case arm that projects
  the 3 user-facing fields (start, stop, len) in the
  same shape as `_show_linrange_dynamic` in
  `base/io.jl`. The `print(r)` (no IO) path already
  worked because `PrintAnyNoNewline` dispatches to the
  registered user `show` method via `show_methods`; this
  fix closes the IOBuffer / stdout / stderr / `string`
  paths that bypass that dispatch.
- Scope: LinRange specifically. The broader bug
  (`print(io, x)` / `string(x)` for any struct with a
  user `show` method does not dispatch to that method)
  needs new VM infrastructure for invoking user show
  from inside the IOPrint / StringNew builtins — tracked
  as a follow-up.
- New fixture `io_linrange_print_string_4761`
  (7 testsets, 8 assertions) covers print(buf, ...),
  string(...), println(buf, ...), various endpoints, a
  direct regression guard against the `lendiv` leak, and
  a Pair-invariant regression guard. Parity-verified
  against upstream julia.
- 2700/2700 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### for-loop over Char range binds Char ✅ (Issue #4796)

- Follow-up to #4795. `for c in 'a':'c'` bound the loop
  variable as the underlying Int64 codepoint (`97`, `98`,
  `99`), with `typeof(c) === Int64` instead of `Char`. The
  first slice of #4795 fixed Range[i] / collect / first /
  last for Char ranges, but the for-loop iteration path used
  the I64-specialized fast path in
  `compile/stmt.rs::Stmt::For` and never reached
  `RangeValue::typed_element`.
- Fix: include `ValueType::Char` in the `needs_typed_range`
  check that rewrites `Stmt::For` to `Stmt::ForEach` over
  `Expr::Range` — same treatment small-int ranges
  (Int8/Int16/...) already got for the same reason in #3550.
  Char ranges now route through the generic
  Pure-Julia `iterate(::Range)` path, which materializes each
  step via `typed_element` and produces `Value::Char`.
- Coverage: basic `for c in 'a':'c'`, reverse step
  `'e':-1:'a'`, single-element `'x':'x'`, empty `'z':'a'`,
  iteration through a stored range variable, plus an
  Int-range fast-path regression guard.
- New fixture `numeric_char_range_for_loop_4796`
  (7 testsets, 8 assertions), parity-verified against
  upstream julia via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 2700/2700 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Comprehension Any-body no longer coerces to Float64 ✅ (Issue #4822)

- `[convert(Any, x) for x in [1, 2, 3]]` returned
  `Vector{Float64}` with `[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]` — Int values
  were silently coerced to Float.
- Root cause: `compile/expr/collection.rs::compile_comprehension`
  had a fallback at the end of its element-type chain
  that defaulted to `ArrayElementType::F64` for non-Tuple
  Any body types. A relic from a numeric-heavy era; with
  richer inference today it silently corrupted
  non-numeric Any-body results.
- Fix: change the fallback to `ArrayElementType::Any` so
  Any-body comprehensions produce `Vector{Any}` carrying
  source values verbatim. Upstream Julia often infers
  tighter (e.g. `Vector{Int64}`); `Vector{Any}` is the
  safe lossless default and matches upstream's behavior
  when its own inference cannot do better.
- 2700/2700 tests pass — the F64 fallback was not
  load-bearing in any existing fixture or unit test, so
  the change is contained.
- New fixture `comprehension_any_body_fallback_4822`
  (4 testsets, 10 assertions) covers Int and String
  source under `convert(Any, ...)` body, a Float
  comprehension regression guard, and an untyped Int
  identity regression guard. Parity-verified against
  upstream julia.
- clippy 0 warnings.

### Typed-Any comprehension `Any[expr for x in iter]` works ✅ (Issue #4819)

- `Any[x for x in [1, 2, 3]]` raised
  `ErrorException: Unknown function: Any` at runtime.
- Root cause: the typed-comprehension lowering helper
  `wrap_comprehension_body_with_call` unconditionally
  wrapped the body in a `T(x)` call. For ordinary types
  `T(x)` is the conversion constructor and works; for
  `T == "Any"` there is no `Any(x)` constructor in
  upstream Julia, so the synthesized call errored at
  runtime.
- Fix: special-case `function == "Any"` in the wrap
  helper to wrap the entire (untyped) comprehension in a
  `Vector{Any}(...)` Call instead of wrapping the body.
  The `Vector{Any}` compile intercept added in #4818
  (PR #4820) then routes through the Pure-Julia helper
  `_vector_any_collect`, producing a `Vector{Any}` with
  each element boxed.
- Non-Any typed comprehensions (`Float64[x for x in r]`
  etc.) keep their existing `T(x)`-body wrap behavior
  (no regression).
- Multi-iter `Any[expr for i in R1, j in R2]` now
  correctly resolves eltype to `Any` but the result is
  still flattened to `Vector{Any}` instead of
  `Matrix{Any}` — that's the orthogonal multi-comp shape
  bug tracked as #4779.
- New fixture `comprehension_typed_any_4819` (7
  testsets, 16 assertions) covers Int / Float / Range
  sources, non-identity body expressions, filter
  clauses, empty results, and a `Float64[...]`
  regression guard. Parity-verified against upstream
  julia via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 2700/2700 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Vector{Any}(arr) materializes a Vector{Any} ✅ (Issue #4818)

- Sibling bug to #4811/#4816. `Vector{Any}([1, 2, 3])`
  returned the source vector unchanged, leaving the result
  typed `Vector{Int64}` instead of `Vector{Any}`.
- Root cause: same compile-time intercept in
  `compile_array_constructor`. PR #4817 (#4816) added
  typed-comprehension synthesis but deliberately gated it on
  `!matches!(elem_type, ArrayElementType::Any)` because
  `Any[x for x in arr]` lowers to a body wrapped in `Any(x)`,
  which is not a defined Julia constructor (typed-Any
  comprehension itself is broken — filed as #4819).
- Fix: added a Pure-Julia helper `_vector_any_collect(arr)`
  in `base/array.jl` that allocates `Vector{Any}(undef, n)`
  and copies each source element via plain indexed store
  (the `Vector{Any}` backing boxes each value to `Any` as a
  side effect). The compile intercept routes
  `Vector{Any}(arr)` to a synthesized call to this helper.
- Gating: `type_args[0].to_string() == "Any"` literal check
  ensures unknown type variables (where-clause / TypeVar
  names that also fall through to `ArrayElementType::Any`)
  do not fire this branch and keep the existing no-op path.
- Coverage: `Vector{Any}(Vector{Int})`,
  `Vector{Any}(Vector{Float64})`, same-eltype
  `Vector{Any}(Vector{Any})` copy, `Vector{Any}()` empty
  constructor, `Vector{Any}(undef, n)` undef pattern, and
  non-Any same-eltype fast-path regression guard.
- New fixture `array_typed_vector_any_conversion_4818`
  (6 testsets, 18 assertions), parity-verified against
  upstream julia via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 2700/2700 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Vector{T}(::Vector{S}) typed constructor converts eltype ✅ (Issue #4816)

- Sibling bug to #4811. `Vector{Float64}([1, 2, 3])` returned
  the source vector unchanged instead of materializing a new
  `Vector{Float64}` with each element converted via `T(x)`.
  Result was `Vector{Int64}` carrying the source eltype.
- Root cause: same compile-time intercept in
  `compile_array_constructor` as #4811, but for an Array arg
  instead of a Range. PR #4815 (#4811) handled the Range case;
  the Array case still fell through to
  `self.compile_expr(&args[0])` — a no-op shallow copy that
  silently kept the source eltype.
- Fix: extended #4815's typed-comprehension synthesis to also
  fire on Array args. When `!matches!(elem_type, Any)` and the
  source eltype differs from `T` (or is unknown), emit
  `T[T(x) for x in arr]` via the existing typed-comprehension
  compile path. When the source eltype matches `T` exactly,
  preserve the existing no-op fast path to avoid penalizing
  the common-eltype case.
- Coverage: `Vector{Float64}(Vector{Int})`,
  `Vector{Int64}(Vector{Float64})`,
  `Vector{Float32}(Vector{Float64})`, `Array{T}` alias,
  same-eltype no-op fast path, `Vector{T}()` empty constructor,
  and `Vector(arr)` (no-type-args) regression guards.
- New fixture `array_typed_vector_array_conversion_4816`
  (8 testsets, 19 assertions), parity-verified against upstream
  julia via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 2700/2700 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Vector{T}(::AbstractRange) typed constructor materializes ✅ (Issue #4811)

- Follow-up to #4810. `Vector{Float64}(1:3)` returned the
  range unchanged (`1:3`) instead of materializing to
  `Vector{Float64}`. The Pure-Julia
  `Vector{T}(r::AbstractRange)` method existed in
  `base/array.jl` but was unreachable because the
  compile-time intercept at `compile_array_constructor`
  short-circuited before dynamic dispatch.
- Fix: in `compile_array_constructor`, the typed 1-arg
  range case now synthesizes the upstream Julia form
  `T[x for x in r]` (a typed comprehension whose body
  applies `T(...)` per element) and compiles it via the
  existing typed-comprehension path. Self-contained at
  the intercept site; no method-dispatch plumbing
  required. The Pure-Julia method is retained for
  dynamic-dispatch callers.
- Coverage: `UnitRange{Int}` → Float64/Float32,
  `StepRangeLen{Float}` → Int64, `StepRange{Int}` →
  Float64, `StepRangeLen{Float}` → Float64, the
  `Array{T}(range)` alias, plus regression guards for
  the no-type-args `Vector(range)` path (#4810) and
  `Vector{T}(::Array)` non-range path.
- New fixture `array_typed_vector_range_constructor_4811`
  (8 testsets, 16 assertions), parity-verified against
  upstream julia via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 2700/2700 tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Array literal splat `[a, v..., b]` lowering ✅ (Issue #4793)

- `[10, v..., 20]` (with `v = [1, 2, 3]`) failed at lowering
  with `UnsupportedExpression("splat_expression")`. Splat
  already worked in tuple literals and function calls; only
  array literals were missing.
- Fix:
  `lowering/expr/collection.rs::lower_vector_expr_impl` now
  detects `NodeKind::SplatExpression` children. When any
  splat is present, the vector literal is rewritten into a
  `vcat(...)` call: splat operands pass through unchanged,
  non-splat operands are wrapped in a 1-element
  `ArrayLiteral([elem])`. `vcat(args...)` (the existing
  varargs body in `base/array.jl`) flattens them with
  `promote_type` semantics, matching Julia's `[a, v..., b]`
  output exactly (element values and element type).
- Coverage: vector splat (middle/start/end/lone/multiple),
  scalar interleave, tuple splat, range splat, empty splat,
  Float promotion. Verified with
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh` against upstream julia.
- New fixture `array_literal_splat_4793` (10 testsets, 11
  assertions). 2700/2700 fixture and unit tests pass, clippy
  0 warnings.

### Vector(::AbstractRange) materializes (first slice) ✅ (Issue #4810)

- `Vector(1:3)` returned the range unchanged
  (`UnitRange{Int64}`) instead of materializing to a
  `Vector{Int64}`. Same for any range arg.
- Root cause: `compile_array_constructor` in
  `compile/expr/collection.rs` had a placeholder "compile the
  arg and return it" for the single-arg `Vector(arr)` form —
  fine as a no-op for actual arrays but wrong for ranges,
  where Julia's constructor materializes via `collect`.
- Fix:
  - In `compile_array_constructor`: when the single arg infers
    as a Range (`JuliaType::UnitRange` / `StepRange` /
    `AbstractRange` or `ValueType::Range`) AND no type args
    were given, emit
    `Instr::CallBuiltin(BuiltinId::RangeCollect, 1)` instead
    of the no-op placeholder.
  - Added `Vector(r::AbstractRange) = collect(r)` and
    `Vector{T}(r::AbstractRange) where {T}` (manual loop —
    splat in array literal `T[r...]` isn't supported yet,
    #4793) in `subset_julia_vm/src/julia/base/array.jl` for the
    Pure-Julia dispatch path.
- New fixture `array_vector_range_constructor_4810` (6
  assertions, three testsets) covers `Vector(1:3)`,
  `Vector(1:0.5:3)` (Float), and `Vector(::Array)` regression
  guard.
- Scope: first slice (no-type-args form). The typed form
  `Vector{Float64}(1:3)` still hits the compile intercept
  before reaching the Pure-Julia method; tracked as #4811.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Float16 print uses scientific notation (closes #4802 / #4804 fix family) ✅ (Issue #4807)

- Third member of the #4802 / #4804 fix family: Float16 print
  didn't switch to scientific notation for large magnitudes.
  Surfaced by the parity probe extension from PR #4806/#4808
  (the Float16 cell exposed the divergence).
- Fix: `format_float16_julia`
  - Lowered the whole-number fixed-form upper bound from `1e5`
    to `1e3` to match Julia's F16 switchover threshold (narrower
    than F32/F64 because F16's max magnitude is only ~6.5e4).
  - Added a scientific arm for `|x|` outside `[1e-4, 1e3)` that
    uses a round-trip mantissa search via Rust's `{:.*e}` to
    find the shortest faithful form (F16 has only ~3.3 decimal
    digits of precision so the loop exits in 0–4 iterations).
- New fixture `numeric_float16_scientific_4807` (14 assertions,
  four testsets) covers small/large F16 scientific, the
  threshold boundary (`999.0` vs `1000.0` → `1.0e3`),
  normal-range regression, and special values.
- Parity probe now down from 4 → 3 divergences (the F16 cell
  passes; remaining 3 are #4779 multi-variable comprehension
  shape).
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Float32 print also uses scientific notation (follow-up to #4802) ✅ (Issue #4804)

- `format_float32_julia` had the same fall-through to Rust's
  default `Display` as `format_float_julia` did before PR #4803.
  `Float32(1.5e-10)` printed as `0.00000000015` instead of
  `1.5e-10`. PR #4803 (#4802) only touched the Float64 helper.
- Fix:
  - Lowered the whole-number fixed-form upper bound in
    `format_float32_julia` from `1e7` to `1e6` (matching the
    Float64 threshold).
  - Routed magnitudes outside `[1e-4, 1e6)` through a new
    `format_float32_scientific_julia` helper that calls Rust's
    `{:e}` on the f32 directly (not after `as f64` cast), so
    the printed mantissa reflects f32's shortest round-trip
    rather than the wider f64 form. Both scientific helpers
    now share a `julia_scientific_postprocess` helper for the
    `1e10` → `1.0e10` `.0` insertion.
- New fixture `numeric_float32_scientific_4804` (18 assertions,
  five testsets) covers the scientific notation for small/large
  Float32 magnitudes, regression guards for the normal range,
  threshold boundary checks, and special values.
- Float16 still uses its own round-tripping algorithm; not
  affected by this fix (the F16 magnitude range is narrower so
  the issue surfaces less often).
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Float64 print uses scientific notation matching Julia ✅ (Issue #4802)

- `print` / `string` / `repr` of `Float64` never used scientific
  notation in sjulia. Upstream switches to scientific for very
  small / very large magnitudes (e.g. `1.5e-10`, `1.0e308`);
  sjulia printed full decimal form, producing 300+ digit output
  for `floatmin(Float64)` / `floatmax(Float64)`.
- Concrete divergences (now fixed): `1.5e-10` (was
  `0.00000000015`), `1.5e20` (was 21-digit decimal),
  `floatmin(Float64)` (was 308-digit decimal), `floatmax(Float64)`
  (was 308-digit decimal), `2.5e15` (was `2500000000000000`).
- Fix:
  - Lowered the whole-number fixed-form upper bound in
    `format_float_julia` from `1e15` to `1e6` so values like
    `1.0e6` correctly route to scientific.
  - Added a scientific arm: if `|x|` is outside `[1e-4, 1e6)`
    (and non-zero), route through new
    `format_float_scientific_julia` helper. The helper uses
    Rust's `{:e}` then post-processes whole-mantissa cases
    (`1e10` → `1.0e10`) to match Julia's required `.0`
    convention.
- New fixture `numeric_float_scientific_4802` (22 assertions,
  five testsets) covers the scientific notation for very small
  and very large magnitudes, regression guards for the normal
  fixed-point range (`0.0`, `0.5`, `3.14`, `150000.0`,
  `0.0001`), threshold boundary checks (`1e-4` vs `1e-5`,
  `1e5` vs `1e6`), and special values (`NaN`, `Inf`, `-Inf`,
  `-0.0`).
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green;
  parity probe still 3 known divergences (all #4779), no new
  ones introduced.

### Feature-branch guard for /auto-work workflow ✅ (Issue #4798)

- Prevention for the direct-to-main commit pattern: during the
  #4795 work in this session, the agent forgot to create a
  feature branch first and committed on local `main`. Recovered
  before push (via `git branch fix/4795-... && git reset --hard
  origin/main && git checkout fix/4795-...`) so no remote damage,
  but the workflow rule violation surfaced the gap.
- Added `scripts/branch_guard.sh` — fails fast when the current
  git branch is `main` or `master`, with recovery instructions
  in the error message. Install as a `.git/hooks/pre-commit`
  hook to make the next direct-to-main commit impossible at
  the git layer:
  ```
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexec bash scripts/branch_guard.sh --quiet\n' > .git/hooks/pre-commit
  chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
  ```
- Naming: intentionally NOT `check_*.sh` because it's a
  developer-side guard, not a CI gate (same convention as
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh` and
  `scripts/probe_base_api_parity.sh`).
- Added "Feature-branch guard for `/auto-work`" bullet to
  `docs/vm/CODE_AUDITS.md` documenting the script, the hook
  install one-liner, and the recovery sequence.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, shellcheck clean, audits green.

### Char range 'a':'e' (first slice — construction/[i]/collect) ✅ (Issue #4795)

- `'a':'e'` (Char range, upstream `StepRange{Char, Int}`) used to
  crash on construction because `Instr::MakeRangeLazy` called
  `pop_f64_or_i64` which rejects `Value::Char` operands.
- Fix slice:
  - Added `RangeElementType::Char` variant to
    `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/value/range.rs`. `typed_element`
    converts the stored Unicode codepoint back to a `Char` via
    `char::from_u32` (with U+FFFD fallback for safety).
  - Added `Vm::pop_f64_or_i64_or_char` helper in `vm/mod.rs`;
    `Instr::MakeRangeLazy` uses it and tags the resulting
    `RangeValue` with `RangeElementType::Char` when any operand
    is a Char.
  - `RangeValue::collect` Char arm builds a `Vector{Char}` via
    `char::from_u32` per element.
  - `Range[i]` (the array_index Range path) routes Char ranges
    through `typed_element` instead of the Int64-narrowing
    branch, returning Char values from indexing.
  - `eltype(::Range{Char})` arm + iterator element-type arm
    added so reflection sees Char.
- New fixture `numeric_char_range_4795` (10 assertions, five
  testsets) covers `length`, `[i]`, `collect`, `first`, `last`
  for `'a':'e'`, plus numeric range regression guards.
- Scope: this is the first slice. The for-loop iteration path
  (`for c in 'a':'e'`) still binds the loop variable as `Int64`
  because the specialized for-range instruction bypasses
  `typed_element` — tracked as a follow-up under #4796.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Float64 whole-number range preserves Float at first/[i] ✅ (Issue #4760)

- `0.0:1.0:5.0` (and other Float64 ranges with whole-number
  endpoints) silently narrowed `first` / `last` / `step` / `[i]`
  to `Int64`. `repr(0.0:1.0:5.0)` returned `"0:1:5"` (dropping
  the `.0`), so eval-roundtrips landed in `UnitRange{Int}`
  instead of `StepRangeLen{Float64}`. Same type-preservation
  family as #4745 (negative zero).
- Root cause: the range `getindex` heuristic at
  `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/exec/array_index.rs` narrowed any
  computed element with `fract() == 0.0` to `Int64`,
  regardless of the range's `is_float` flag. Both `first(r)`
  (via Pure-Julia `first(arr) = arr[1]`) and direct `r[i]`
  routed through this path.
- Fix: the narrowing branch now also requires `!range.is_float`.
  Non-float ranges keep their existing behavior (so
  `(1:5)[1] === Int64(1)` still holds); float ranges route
  through `range.typed_element(element)` which preserves the
  Float64 element type.
- New fixture `numeric_range_index_float_4760` (17 assertions,
  five testsets) covers `repr` / `first` / `last` / `step` /
  `[i]` / `collect` for whole-number Float64 ranges, with
  regression guards for the Int range path and the
  non-whole-step Float range path.
- Added a regression guard probe to
  `scripts/probe_base_api_parity.sh` (probes 59 total, still
  3 known divergences all #4779).
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### abs(typemin(IntN)) for narrow signed integers no longer crashes ✅ (Issue #4789)

- `abs(typemin(IntN))` for N < 64 (Int8/Int16/Int32) crashed with
  `Type error: Cannot negate "I8(-128)"` instead of returning
  `typemin(IntN)` itself. Upstream Julia silently returns the same
  value because two's-complement arithmetic wraps:
  `-typemin(IntN) == typemin(IntN)` for any signed N-bit integer.
- Root cause: Pure-Julia `abs(x::Int64) = flipsign(x, x)` handled
  the Int64 case correctly, but narrow signed integers fell
  through to the generic `abs(x) = -x if signbit(x) else x` in
  `julia/base/number.jl`, which routed through `dynamic_neg` whose
  narrow-integer arms were missing.
- Fix: `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/dynamic_ops/mod.rs::dynamic_neg`
  now uses `wrapping_neg` for all signed integer widths
  (I8/I16/I32/I64/I128), matching upstream's two's-complement
  semantics. Float/Bool/BigInt/BigFloat arms unchanged.
- New fixture `numeric_abs_typemin_narrow_4789` (17 assertions,
  four testsets) covers `abs(typemin(IntN))` for N ∈ {8,16,32,64,
  128}, normal narrow-integer abs (regression guards), the
  underlying `-typemin(IntN)` primitive, and Float/Bool negation
  regression guards.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### bswap respects element bit width (follow-up to #4785) ✅ (Issue #4787)

- Same root cause family as #4785: `bswap` for non-Int64 integer
  types returned wrong results because the compile path coerced
  the argument to I64 and the runtime arm byte-swapped all 8
  bytes regardless of original width. PR #4786 fixed
  count_zeros / leading_* / bitreverse but `bswap` was left
  behind.
- Fix:
  - `subset_julia_vm/src/compile/expr/builtin_math.rs` —
    `"bswap"` arm uses plain `compile_expr` and returns the
    expr's actual type rather than forcing I64.
  - `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/builtins_math.rs` — `BuiltinId::Bswap`
    arm pops a `Value`, match-dispatches over every integer
    variant (I8/16/32/64/128, U8/16/32/64/128), and pushes the
    original variant back.
- New fixture `numeric_bswap_width_4787` (12 assertions, four
  testsets) covers `bswap(UInt8/16/32/64)` (Int8/16/32 too),
  Int64 regression guard, and type preservation
  (`typeof(bswap(UInt16(...)))` === `UInt16`).
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Bit ops respect element bit width for non-Int64 integer types ✅ (Issue #4785)

- `count_zeros`, `leading_zeros`, `leading_ones` (and `bitreverse`)
  for non-Int64 integer types returned wrong results because the
  compile path coerced the argument to I64 via
  `compile_expr_as(..., ValueType::I64)`. The runtime arm then
  operated on a 64-bit value, inflating zero counts due to
  implicit zero-extension. Example:
  `count_zeros(UInt8(0xf0))` returned 60 (should be 4) — the upper
  56 zero bits of the zero-extended Int64 leaked into the count.
- `count_ones`, `trailing_zeros`, `trailing_ones` already worked
  coincidentally because they count from the LSB and the
  upper-zero-extension doesn't affect them — but they shared the
  same root cause and would have misbehaved on signed-negative
  inputs (sign extension fills upper bits with ones).
- Fix:
  - `subset_julia_vm/src/compile/expr/builtin_math.rs` — bit-op
    arms no longer pre-coerce via `compile_expr_as(...)`. They
    use plain `compile_expr` so the runtime sees the original
    integer variant.
  - `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/builtins_math.rs` — all 7 bit-op
    runtime arms (`CountOnes`, `CountZeros`, `LeadingZeros`,
    `LeadingOnes`, `TrailingZeros`, `TrailingOnes`, `Bitreverse`)
    pop a `Value` and match-dispatch over every integer variant
    (I8/I16/I32/I64/I128, U8/U16/U32/U64/U128, plus Bool for
    count_ones/zeros).
  - `bitreverse` now preserves the element type (UInt8 →
    UInt8, was previously coerced to Int64).
- New fixture `numeric_bit_ops_width_4785` (24 assertions, five
  testsets) covers count_zeros/leading_zeros/leading_ones for
  UInt8/16/32, Int8, signed-Int64 regression guards, and the
  bitreverse type-preservation case.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green;
  parity probe still reports 3 known divergences (all #4779), no
  new ones introduced.

### Base API parity sweep probe script ✅ (Issue #4782)

  diverging Base function shapes that were only discovered by

  or new Base wrapper changes).
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, shellcheck on new script clean,
  audits green.

### Symbol(parts...) multi-arg constructor ✅ (Issue #4780)

- `Symbol(parts...)` with multiple arguments failed at compile
  time with `Compilation error: Symbol requires exactly 1
  argument: Symbol(name)`. Upstream Julia's
  `Base.Symbol(args...) = Symbol(string(args...))` concatenates
  all parts via `string` then forms a single Symbol — common
  idiom for programmatically-built symbols like
  `Symbol("col_", i)` to build per-column accessor symbols.
- Fix:
  - `subset_julia_vm/src/compile/expr/builtin.rs` —
    `BuiltinOp::SymbolNew` arm accepts `args.len() >= 1` and
    emits the full argc.
  - `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/builtins_macro/mod.rs` —
    `BuiltinId::SymbolNew` arm pops `argc` values, formats each
    via `format_value_print`, concatenates, and forms the
    Symbol. The 1-arg fast path stays in `vm/exec/call.rs`.
- New fixture `meta_symbol_multi_arg_4780` (7 assertions, five
  testsets) covers single-arg (regression guard), `Symbol("col_", 1)`
  / `Symbol("my", "_", "var")` / `Symbol(:prefix, "_", :suffix)`
  / five-part `Symbol("a", "b", "c", "d", "e")`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### NamedTuple / Tuple field show form (and single-element trailing comma) ✅ (Issue #4777)

- `string(::NamedTuple)` / `string(::Tuple)` / `print(buf, ::Tuple)`
  recursed into field/element values via the print form (bare) so
  String/Char values lost their quotes — `(x = 1, y = hi, z = c)`
  vs upstream `(x = 1, y = "hi", z = 'c')`. Sibling of the
  already-fixed #4764 (struct field show form) — same root cause
  family but for the NamedTuple- and Tuple-specific format arms
  in `format_value_slow`.
- Also: single-element Tuple format produced `(1)` instead of the
  upstream-required `(1,)` disambiguation form.
- Fix: NamedTuple and Tuple value mapping in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/formatting.rs` now uses
  `format_value_show_field` (which quotes `Value::Str` and
  `Value::Char`), and the Tuple arm adds the trailing-comma case
  for single-element tuples.
- New fixture `io_namedtuple_tuple_show_form_4777` (8 assertions,
  five testsets) asserts:
  - NamedTuple/Tuple string/print quoting for String + Char
  - Single-element Tuple `(1,)` / `("hi",)` trailing comma
  - Empty Tuple `()` (no spurious comma)
  - Pure-numeric Tuple `(1, 2, 3)` unchanged
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Matrix fixture for Container<user_struct> StructRef leak + Dict/Set fixes ✅ (Issue #4774)

- Prevention sibling for the fix family #4761 / #4763 / #4772 /
  #4773. Existing matrix fixtures (#4757, #4766) covered (entry
  point) × (top-level value class) but did NOT cover
  (container shape × heap-allocated element). The PR #4771 /
  #4773 round-trip showed the gap is real.
- While writing the new matrix, two more leaks surfaced that the
  existing matrix didn't catch:
  - `Dict("k" => user_struct)` leaked `StructRef(heap_idx=N)`
    because `resolve_struct_refs_for_format` had no `Dict` arm.
  - `Set([1, 2, 3])` leaked `Set([I64(1), I64(2), I64(3)])`
    because the Set arm of `format_value_slow` used Rust
    `format!("{:?}", e)` for elements instead of the proper
    `format_dict_key` (which is what the Dict arm uses).
- Fix:
  - Add a `Value::Dict` recursion arm to
    `resolve_struct_refs_for_format` that rebuilds the Dict via
    `DictValue::with_type_params_opt` + per-entry `insert` so
    each value goes through the resolver.
  - Route `format_value_slow`'s Set arm through
    `format_dict_key` to eliminate the Rust Debug leak for set
    elements (parallels the Dict-key fix from #4735).
- New fixture `io_no_leak_container_struct_matrix_4774` (54
  assertions, 8 testsets) covers 7 container shapes (Vector,
  Tuple, NamedTuple, Dict<value=struct>, Pair<struct,Int>,
  Ref<struct>, Set<primitive>) × 6 display entry points
  (`string`, `repr`, `print(buf, x)`, multi-arg
  `print(buf, lit, x, lit)`, `sprint(io -> print(io, x))`,
  interpolation `"$x"`) with negative assertions for `StructRef(`,
  `heap_idx=`, `I64(`, `I32(`, `I128(`, `U64(`, `F64(`, `Str(`,
  `Char(`, `Symbol(` tokens.
- Updated `docs/vm/CODE_AUDITS.md`'s "StructRef heap resolution"
  bullet to explicitly list the recursion-covered carriers
  (`Memory`, `NativeArray`, `Dict` added since the original
  bullet) and call out the requirement to extend the matrix
  fixtures when adding a new carrier.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Vector{user_struct} StructRef leak inside compact form (regression) ✅ (Issue #4772)

- Regression from PR #4771 (#4770 fix). The new compact `[a, b, c]`
  form for `print(::Vector)` walked native-array elements via
  `format_value` without first resolving `Value::StructRef(idx)`
  against the struct heap, so a Vector of heap-allocated structs
  (any user struct, Pair, etc.) leaked `StructRef(heap_idx=N)`
  inside the compact form.
- Fix: extend `resolve_struct_refs_for_format` in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/formatting.rs` to recurse into both
  `Value::Memory` and `Value::NativeArray`, replacing the carrier
  with a fresh `Any`-typed copy whose elements are pre-resolved.
  The widening is throw-away (only used by the formatting copy of
  the value tree); original carriers are not mutated.
- New fixture `io_vector_struct_no_leak_4772` (20 assertions,
  three testsets) asserts that `string` / `repr` / `print(buf, x)`
  on Vector{user_struct}, Vector{Pair}, and Any-typed Vector with
  mixed struct elements no longer contain `StructRef` /
  `heap_idx=` tokens, and that the element values DO appear (so
  resolution actually fired rather than just hiding the leak).
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### print(::Vector) / string(::Vector) compact form ✅ (Issue #4770)

- `print(v)` / `println(v)` / `string(v)` for any `Vector{T}` /
  `Matrix{T}` (e.g. from `[1, 2, 3]`, `sort([3, 1, 2])`,
  `filter(iseven, 1:6)`) leaked the internal Pure-Julia Array
  wrapper struct form:
  `Array{Int64}(3-element Memory{Int64}:\n 2\n 4\n 6, (3))` —
  exposing the `Memory{T}` carrier and shape tuple instead of the
  canonical `[2, 4, 6]`. Sibling of the already-fixed #4731 (which
  fixed `repr(::Vector)`); same family but for the print path.
- Fix: add an Array-wrapper arm to `format_struct_instance` in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/formatting.rs` that walks the `_mem`
  Memory carrier and emits the compact `[a, b, c]` (1D) /
  `[a b; c d]` (2D, column-major) / `T[]` (empty 0/1D) /
  `Matrix{T}(undef, r, c)` (empty 2D) form. Elements render
  through `format_value_show_field`, so String elements are
  quoted (matching upstream and #4764). Mirrors the Pure-Julia
  `_show_vector_compact` / `_show_matrix_compact` helpers.
- New fixture `io_print_vector_compact_4770` (9 assertions, five
  testsets) asserts `string` / `print(buf, ...)` produce the
  compact form for `Vector{Int}`, `Vector{String}`, typed empty
  vectors, matrices, and sort/filter results.
- This closes the easy slice of #4770 (1D/2D arrays). Higher-rank
  arrays (`ndims >= 3`) still fall through to the generic
  struct-field-dump arm; that case is uncommon for `print` usage
  and is left for follow-up.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Generic show(io, x) fallback for user-defined structs ✅ (Issue #4768)

- `repr(user_struct_instance)` crashed with "indexing not supported
  for I64(N)" for any user-defined struct. The Pure-Julia
  `repr` impl calls `show(io, x)`, but there was no fallback
  `show(io::IO, x)` Any-typed method — only built-in types
  (Bool, Int*, Float*, String, Symbol, Tuple, Pair, Dict, ...)
  had explicit show methods. Dispatch silently fell through to a
  built-in arm that tried `x[1]`. Surfaced after #4761 / #4764
  made struct display matter.

  (Dict/Set/Missing/StepRangeLen show crashes that landed on
  `show(IO, CartesianIndex)`), but for user-defined structs.
- Fix: add a generic `show(io::IO, x)` method in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/julia/base/io.jl` that prints
  `typeof(x)(field1, field2, ...)` using `fieldnames(typeof(x))`
  + `getfield(x, name)` + recursive `show` per field. Specific
  arms for built-in types still win via most-specific-method
  dispatch.
- New fixture `io_show_fallback_user_struct_4768` (13 assertions,
  three testsets) asserts `repr` works for 1/2/3-field structs,
  built-in specific arms still produce the expected forms
  (Pair/Tuple/Array/String/Symbol/Float/Bool/Nothing/Missing),
  and `show(buf, ::user_struct)` writes the expected form into
  an IOBuffer.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Matrix-fixture and audit policy for StructRef leak prevention at IOBuffer entry points ✅ (Issue #4766)

- Prevention for the fix family #4761 / #4763. The original matrix
  fixture `io_no_rust_debug_leak_4757` only covered the `string`

  multi-arg print paths (`print(buf, x)`, `write(buf, x)`,

  Value-to-string and Rust Debug catch-all bullets, with the
  explicit list of currently-covered call sites and the

- This is the easy half of #4766 (the matrix sibling). The

### struct field formatting uses show form (quoted strings/chars) ✅ (Issue #4764)

- `print(io, struct)` / `string(struct)` recursed into fields using
  the print form (bare) instead of the show form, so String / Char
  fields lost their quotes (`Foo(42, hi)` vs upstream
  `Foo(42, "hi")`). Surfaced after #4761 made the StructRef leak
  visible.
- Fix: added `format_value_show_field` in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/formatting.rs` that quotes `Value::Str`
  with `"..."` (escape table mirrors `escape_for_repr_str` in
  `builtins_strings.rs`), single-quotes `Value::Char` with
  `'...'`, and falls through to `format_value` for all other
  variants. `format_struct_instance` now maps fields through this
  helper for both the generic struct arm and the special-cased
  `Pair` arm.
- New fixture `io_struct_field_show_form_4764` (6 assertions, five
  testsets) asserts `string` / `print(buf, ...)` produce the
  quoted-field form for String / Char field types and that
  numeric fields are unchanged.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### print(io, struct) Rust Debug leak (StructRef heap_idx) ✅ (Issue #4761)

- `print(buf::IOBuffer, x)`, `print(stdout, x)` (the multi-arg
  IOPrint path), and `write(buf, x)` leaked the Rust debug repr
  `StructRef(heap_idx=N)` whenever `x` was a heap-allocated struct
  (`Pair(1, 2)`, user struct, etc.). The single-arg `print(x)` arm
  (`BuiltinId::Print`) already resolved StructRef via
  `resolve_struct_refs_for_format` before formatting, but the
  multi-arg IOPrint and IOWrite arms did not.
- Fix: resolve every `Value::StructRef` in the printed args against
  `self.struct_heap` before calling `format_value_print` in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/builtins_io.rs`'s `BuiltinId::IOPrint`
  (sprint / stdout / stderr / IOBuffer / non-IO arms) and
  `BuiltinId::IOWrite`. Mirrors the existing `BuiltinId::Print`
  pattern.
- New fixture `io_print_iobuffer_structref_4761` (8 assertions,
  three testsets) asserts `print(buf, Pair(...))`,
  `print(buf, user_struct)`, and multi-arg `print(buf, ..., x, ...)`
  no longer contain `StructRef` / `heap_idx` tokens and match the
  expected Julia form.
- This is the "easy slice" of #4761. The harder slice (route
  `print(buf, ...)` and `string(...)` through user-defined Pure
  Julia `show(io, ::T)` method lookup so e.g.
  `print(buf, LinRange(...))` calls the user's show method instead
  of dumping the 4 internal struct fields) remains open on #4761.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### show/repr for StepRangeLen with float step and LinRange ✅ (Issue #4759)

- `repr(1:0.5:3)` (and `show(io, ::StepRangeLen{Float64})` more
  generally) crashed with `GetField(0): expected struct, got Range
  in show(IO, CartesianIndex)` because the Pure-Julia
  `first/last/step(::StepRangeLen)` methods access struct fields,
  but VM-native `Value::Range` is reported as `StepRangeLen` yet is
  not backed by struct fields. Same crash family as the recent
  Dict/Set/Missing show fixes (#4737/#4739/#4743) but for ranges.

  in `subset_julia_vm/src/julia/base/io.jl`, forwarding to an
  untyped helper (`_show_steprangelen_dynamic(io, r)`) that lacks
  the `::StepRangeLen` parameter annotation — this forces
  `first/last/step(r)` inside the helper to be dynamically
  dispatched, which routes through the VM Range builtins for
  VM-native ranges while still working for real struct values.
- New fixture `io_show_steprangelen_4759` (9 assertions, three
  testsets) covers `repr` / `show` / `string` for VM-native
  `StepRangeLen{Float64}` ranges and `repr` / `show` for
  `LinRange`. Tests use non-whole-number floats to avoid #4760
  (whole-number Float64 ranges narrow to Int64) and exclude
  `print(buf, ::LinRange)` / `string(::LinRange)` to avoid #4761
  (struct print/string bypass show methods).

### Stop ExprValue Display from leaking Rust Debug for non-I64/F64 children ✅ (Issue #4755)

- `Meta.parse("-9223372036854775808")` (working after PR #4754
  / Issue #4753) displayed as `Expr(:call, :-, I128(9223372036854775808))`
  — leaking the Rust `Debug` repr `I128(...)` into user output.
- `vm/value/container.rs`'s `impl Display for ExprValue`'s child
  arg match had explicit arms only for `I64` / `F64` / `Symbol` /
  `Str` / `Expr`; everything else fell into `_ => write!("{:?}")`.
  Extended with explicit arms for `I8`/`I16`/`I32`/`I128`,
  `U8`/`U16`/`U32`/`U64`/`U128`, `Bool`, `F16`/`F32`, `Char`,
  `Nothing`, `Missing`. The catch-all Debug fallback remains for
  values that have no parseable Julia literal form.
- New fixture `io_expr_display_no_debug_leak_4755` (6 assertions)
  asserts that `string(Meta.parse(...))` output never contains
  Rust Debug tokens like `I128(`, `Str(`, `Char(`. The fixture is
  runtime-agnostic — upstream Julia's `:(...)` form also never
  contains those tokens — so it passes under both interpreters.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.
- Remaining: sjulia's Expr display still uses the
  `Expr(:call, :+, :x, 1)` constructor form rather than upstream's
  `:(x + 1)` infix-quote form. Broader display-form parity is a
  separate follow-up.

### Meta.parse promotes overflowing integer literals to Int128/BigInt ✅ (Issue #4753)

- `Meta.parse("-9223372036854775808")` (i.e. `repr(typemin(Int64))`)
  failed at runtime with `Invalid integer: 9223372036854775808`.
  sjulia parsed the magnitude as a positive i64 *before* applying
  the unary `-`, and `Int64::MAX + 1` doesn't fit i64.
- Two-part fix:
  1. `vm/builtins_macro/parse.rs` `IntegerLiteral` arm falls
     back i64 → i128 → BigInt (for decimal literals only — hex /
     oct / bin keep the existing i64 path). The magnitude
     `9223372036854775808` now parses as `Value::I128`.
  2. `vm/builtins_macro/eval.rs` `eval_call` unary `-` arm handles
     `Value::I128` (and `Value::F32` while we're there). When the
     negation result fits `i64::try_from`, narrow back to
     `Value::I64` so the typing matches upstream
     (`typeof(-Int128(9223372036854775808)) === Int64`).
- New fixture `io_meta_parse_typemin_4753` (9 assertions) covers
  `typemin(Int64)` round-trip, overflow promotion to Int128/BigInt,
  and regular small negative literals (regression guard). All pass
  under both sjulia and upstream Julia 1.12 via
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.
- Remaining out-of-scope cosmetic: the `Expr` display still leaks
  `I128(...)` Rust Debug repr (`Expr(:call, :-, I128(...))` instead
  of `:(-9223372036854775808)`); separate display-leak family
  tracked elsewhere.

  four testsets) asserts the exact `repr(x)` output for:
