    `Float32` with `f0` suffix (PR #4748), `Float16` wrapper
  - escaped strings and chars (PR #4750)
  - `Symbol`, `Bool`, `Nothing`, `Missing` (PR #4744)
  - `Pair` (PR #4726), `Vector{Int}`/`Vector{Float64}`/`Vector{String}`,
    typed-empty `Int64[]` (PR #4734), `Tuple`
- Originally framed as a `eval(Meta.parse(repr(x))) ≡ x` round-trip
  invariant, but sjulia's `Meta.parse` / `eval` has its own gaps
  (`=>` not callable in eval context, `Float32` literal parser
  doesn't read `1.5f0`, `Inf` / `NaN` / `nothing` / `missing`
  not resolved as identifiers in eval scope). Switched to a
  literal-equality form that's strictly stronger for repr's actual
  contract and not blocked by those independent gaps.
- Verified 32/32 under both sjulia and upstream Julia 1.12 via
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### repr / show for String and Char now escape special characters ✅ (Issue #4749)

- `repr("a\nb")` wrote a raw newline between `a` and `b` instead of
  the literal escape sequence `\n`, so the output failed to
  round-trip through `Meta.parse`. Same for `"\"\""`, `"\\"`, and
  `repr('\n')` / `repr('\\')` / `repr('\'')`.
- Two-layer fix:
  1. `vm/builtins_strings.rs` `BuiltinId::Repr` now wraps
     `Value::Str` and `Value::Char` arms with new
     `escape_for_repr_str` / `escape_for_repr_char` helpers that
     mirror upstream `Base.escape_string` (escapes `\\`, `"`,
     `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\0`, plus `'` for chars).
  2. Pure Julia `show(io::IO, x::String)` in `julia/base/io.jl`
     now delegates to `escape_string` (already defined in
     `base/strings/util.jl`). `show(io::IO, x::Char)` rewritten
     with an inline match on the same escape table.
- `print` and `string` paths keep the raw form
  (`string("a\nb") == "a\nb"`); only show / repr escape.
- New fixture `io_repr_string_char_escape_4749` (14 assertions)
  covers String/Char escaping plus the print/string parity. All
  pass under both sjulia and upstream Julia 1.12 via
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

## 最新対応 (2026-05-27)

### repr(Float32) keeps f0 suffix, repr(Float16) keeps wrapper ✅ (Issue #4747)

- `repr(Float32(1.5))` returned `"1.5"` and `repr(Float16(1.5))`
  returned `"1.5"`, both dropping the typed-literal information so
  an `eval(Meta.parse(...))` round-trip landed at `Float64`.
- Updated `show(io::IO, x::Float32)` to `print(io, x, "f0")` and
  `show(io::IO, x::Float16)` to `print(io, "Float16(", x, ")")`
  in `julia/base/io.jl`. `print` and `string` still call
  `format_float32_julia` / `format_float16_julia` directly, so
  bare-form output (`"1.5"`) is preserved for the print path,
  matching upstream's print vs show distinction.
- New fixture `io_typed_float_repr_4747` (9 assertions) covers
  Float32/Float16 repr (suffix/wrapper) and Float64 (unchanged), plus
  the print/string bare-form parity. Parity-verified via
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Preserve sign of -0.0 in float display ✅ (Issue #4745)

- `repr(-0.0)`, `string(-0.0)`, `"$(-0.0)"`, and `print(io, -0.0)`
  all returned `"0.0"` instead of upstream Julia's `"-0.0"`. Root
  cause: `format_float_julia`'s whole-number arm computes
  `format!("{}.0", x as i64)`, and `(-0.0_f64) as i64 == 0`, so the
  negative-zero sign was lost.
- Added a `is_sign_negative() && x == 0.0` guard to both
  `format_float_julia` (Float64) and `format_float32_julia`
  (Float32), mirroring the existing guard in
  `format_float16_julia`. The guard fires before the lossy i64
  cast and returns `"-0.0"` directly.
- New fixture `io_neg_zero_sign_4745` (11 assertions) covers
  `repr` / `string` / interpolation / `print` / `show` for `-0.0`
  plus a `signbit`/`iszero`/equality cross-check that the
  underlying IEEE 754 value semantics are unchanged. Parity-verified
  via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### show(io, ::Missing) added — repr(missing) no longer crashes ✅ (Issue #4743)

- `repr(missing)` crashed with the same `show(IO, CartesianIndex)`
  mis-dispatch family as Dict (#4737) and Set (#4739) because there
  was no Pure Julia `show(io, ::Missing)` method.
- Added `show(io::IO, ::Missing) = print(io, "missing")` to
  `julia/base/io.jl` next to the existing `show(io, ::Nothing)`.
  One-liner addition matching the convention.
- New fixture `io_repr_missing_4743` (6 assertions) covers
  repr/string/interpolation/show for Missing and a Nothing parity
  pair to make sure both stay aligned.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Separate print vs show for Symbol — print writes bare name ✅ (Issue #4741)

- `print(io, :foo)` / `println(io, :foo)` / `"$(:foo)"` all wrote
  `:foo` (the show-form) instead of the bare `foo` upstream Julia
  produces. Root cause: `format_value` is shared between print and
  show codepaths and unconditionally produces `:foo` for Symbols.
- New helper `vm/formatting.rs::format_value_print(v)` strips the
  leading `:` for top-level `Value::Symbol` and delegates everything
  else to `format_value`. Symbols inside containers (e.g.
  `Dict(:k => 1)`) intentionally keep the `:` per upstream convention,
  so recursion stops at the top level.
- Routed every print-side call site through the new helper:
  - `vm/exec/print.rs` `Instr::PrintAny` / `PrintAnyNoNewline`
  - `vm/builtins_io.rs` `BuiltinId::Print` / `Println` / `IOPrint`
    (all five IOPrint dispatch arms — sprint_state / Stdout /
    Stderr / IOBuffer / non-IO fallback), and `IOWrite`
  - `vm/exec/string_ops.rs` `Instr::ToString` / `StringConcat`
- Because print is now bare for Symbol, `show(io::IO, x::Symbol)`
  in `julia/base/io.jl` could no longer rely on
  `print(io, x)` accidentally producing `:foo`. Switched its body
  to `print(io, ":", x)` so the show-form keeps the `:`.
- New fixture `io_print_symbol_bare_4741` (7 assertions) covers
  print/println/interpolation/string/show for Symbol. Parity-checked
  via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### show(io, ::AbstractSet) and NamedTuple bare-name display ✅ (Issue #4739 first slice)

- `repr(Set([1, 2, 3]))` crashed with the same `show(IO, CartesianIndex)`
  mis-dispatch family that Dict had (Issue #4737) — Set also lacked a

    via recursive `show(io, x)` for each element.

### show(io, ::AbstractDict) added — repr(Dict) no longer crashes ✅ (Issue #4737)

- `repr(Dict("a" => 1, "b" => 2))` crashed with

  Pure Julia base lacked a `show(io, d::AbstractDict)` method, so

### Dict String key/value Debug-leak in format_dict_value ✅ (Issue #4735)

- `string(Dict("a" => 1))` returned `"Dict(Str(\"a\") => 1)"`,
  leaking the Rust `Debug` repr of `DictKey::Str(...)` because
  `format_dict_value` formatted each key with `format!("{:?}", k)`.
  String *values* inside a Dict also rendered without quotes
  (`Dict(1 => "one")` → `"Dict(1 => one)"`) because `format_value`'s
  print contract drops the quote convention upstream uses inside
  container display.

  helpers:
  1. `format_dict_key(k)` formats `DictKey` in Julia convention —
     `"<s>"` for `Str`, `:<s>` for `Symbol`, plain digits for signed
     ints, zero-padded `0x...` for `UInt*`, and the existing
     `format_float*_julia` helpers for `F16`/`F32`/`F64` bit-packed
     keys.
  2. `format_dict_value_field(v)` matches `Value::Str` to the
     quoted `"<s>"` form (show convention) while delegating
     everything else to `format_value` (print convention) — the
     scope of "switch to show inside containers" stays small.

  exercises String/Symbol/Int keys and String values. Parity-verified
  via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.

  `Dict{T1,T2}` type-parameter prefix and converts `Bool` values to

### repr([1,2,3]) IOBuffer leak + show(::Array) compact form ✅ (Issue #4731)

- `repr([1, 2, 3])` returned
  `"IOBuffer(...)\n3-element Vector{Int64}: 1\n 2\n 3\n"`. Two
  overlapping bugs:
  1. Pure Julia `_show_vector(io, v)` calls `println(io)` to add a
     trailing newline. `println(io::IO)` was dispatching through the
     stdout path (because the `io` parameter inferred as `Any`),
     formatting the IO value itself as `"IOBuffer(...)"` and dumping
     that to stdout.
  2. `show(io::IO, ::Array)` was writing the multi-line
     `MIME"text/plain"` form ("n-element Vector{T}: ...") instead of
     the compact 2-arg `show(io, x)` form ("[a, b, c]") that
     upstream Julia uses for `repr`.
- Fixes:
  1. `compile/expr/builtin_io.rs` extends the `println(...)` compile
     path: when the first arg is `ValueType::IO` *or*
     `ValueType::Any`, route through the `IOPrint` builtin which
     dispatches on the runtime kind. This catches the common case
     where an `io` parameter is untyped (`Any`) but actually holds
     an `IOBuffer` at runtime.
  2. `vm/builtins_io.rs` `BuiltinId::Println` gains an early
     `Value::IO` dispatch as a runtime safety net for any path that
     escapes the compile-time check.
  3. `julia/base/io.jl` adds `_show_vector_compact` and
     `_show_matrix_compact` helpers and switches
     `show(io::IO, ::Array)` to call them. The original
     `_show_vector` / `_show_matrix` are retained for the
     `MIME"text/plain"` REPL display form.
- New fixture `io_repr_array_compact_4731` (10 assertions) verifies
  `repr`, `string`, and `println(io)` parity. Parity-checked against
  upstream Julia 1.12 via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.
- Remaining: `repr(Int[])` returns `"[]"` in sjulia but `"Int64[]"`
  upstream. Tracked separately.

### string(Pair) no longer leaks Rust `StructRef(heap_idx=N)` debug repr ✅ (Issue #4725)

- `string(Pair(1, 2))` returned `"StructRef(heap_idx=12)"`, and
  every code path that interpolated a heap-allocated `Pair` leaked
  the Rust `StructRef` `Debug` formatting into user output.
- Root cause: `vm/formatting.rs`'s `format_value` is heap-less, so
  `Value::StructRef` fell through to `format!("StructRef(heap_idx={})", idx)`.

  which recursively walks composite carriers (`Tuple`, `NamedTuple`,

  `format_struct_instance` gained a `Pair` arm (alongside the
  existing `Rational` arm) that renders `"left => right"` instead of
  the constructor-call form.

  `BuiltinId::Repr` now pass each argument through
  `resolve_struct_refs_for_format` before formatting, so
  `string(Pair(1,2))`, `repr(Pair(1,2))`, and `string((1, p))` all
  match upstream.
- New fixture `strings_string_pair_no_structref_leak_4725` (5 cases)
  exercises the fix under both interpreters via
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 127/127 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings. Out-of-scope sub-bugs
  (string interpolation `"$p"` and `string(Pair("a", 42))` show-vs-print
  for string fields) are tracked separately.

- 1920/1920 lib tests pass (was 1918, +2 new), clippy 0 warnings.

  remaining tasks (sweep TypeVar/UnionAll/TypeOf for the same
  pattern, add a subtype-rules doc) stay open.

### Dispatcher no longer treats Array as matching AbstractString/AbstractDict ✅ (Issue #4708)

- After PR #4707 added per-type `summary` overloads, defining
  `f(::AbstractString)`, `f(::AbstractDict)`, and `f(::AbstractArray)`
  side by side triggered `AmbiguousMethod` for `f([1,2,3])` —
  the `JuliaType::AbstractUser` parent-`Any` fallback in
  `is_subtype_of` made `JuliaType::Array.is_subtype_of(Any)` return
  true and therefore claimed `Array <: AbstractDict` /
  `Array <: AbstractString` were both true.
- Fix in `types/julia_type/comparison.rs`'s `AbstractUser` arm:
  when the AbstractUser's declared parent is `Any`, skip the
  recursive parent fallback. Instead, defer to CoreType when the
  abstract name resolves to a builtin abstract
  (`CoreType::Abstract(_)`), so `Dict <: AbstractDict` and
  `Set <: AbstractSet` keep working. Non-`Any` parents (e.g.
  `AbstractArray`) retain the existing fallback so hierarchies
  like `AbstractVector <: AbstractArray` still resolve.
- The dispatcher's struct-ancestry tie-breaker in
  `compile/method_table.rs` continues to filter Struct args against
  the parent map, so existing Matrix/Vector dispatch tests
  (`matmul_matrix_matrix_abstract_dispatch_4020`,
  `nullspace_logdet_adjoint`) keep selecting the correct overload.
- New fixture `dispatch_abstract_dict_array_disambiguation_4708`
  (10 cases) reproduces the original bug and asserts the fix
  preserves Dict/Set/Array dispatch semantics. The same assertions
  pass under upstream Julia 1.12.

### Base.summary parity for AbstractString and AbstractDict ✅ (Issue #4706)

- Upstream Julia returns `"5-codeunit String"` for `summary("hello")`
  and `"Dict{String, Int64} with 1 entry"` for
  `summary(Dict("a" => 1))`. sjulia fell back to the generic
  `string(typeof(x))` for both, dropping the length / entry-count
  prefix.
- Updated `subset_julia_vm/src/julia/base/io.jl`'s generic
  `summary(x)` to internally `isa`-dispatch on `AbstractString` and
  `AbstractDict`, producing `"N-codeunit String"` (or `"empty
  String"`) and `"Dict{...} with N entry/entries"` respectively. The
  rest of the body unchanged (the `AbstractArray` overload is
  untouched).
- Tried separate `summary(::AbstractString)` / `summary(::AbstractDict)`
  overloads first; that triggered a sjulia dispatcher
  `AmbiguousMethod` error for `summary([1,2,3])` even though `Array`
  is not a subtype of `AbstractString`/`AbstractDict`. Filed as a
  follow-up dispatcher bug; the internal-`isa` form is the
  pragmatic workaround.
- `io_summary` fixture expanded to 15 cases (was 12) covering
  empty/non-empty strings, 0/1/2-entry Dicts, and the original
  Tuple / Array / Symbol / Bool / Nothing assertions. All 15 pass
  under both sjulia and upstream Julia 1.12.

### INTENTIONAL_NOOP markers for essentials.jl no-op helpers ✅ (Issue #4703 first slice)

- First slice of the Pure Julia base/ silent-stub audit (Issue #4703).
  After `Base.isvarargtype` (#4701) and `Base.unwrap_unionall` (#3909
  / PR #4693) both turned out to be untyped-arg trivial-body stubs
  that silently returned wrong values, we are establishing a marker
  convention for the *legitimate* intentional no-ops in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/julia/base/essentials.jl` so a follow-up CI
  audit can distinguish them from new silent stubs.
- `donotdelete(x) → nothing` and `compilerbarrier(setting, x) → x`
  carry new `# INTENTIONAL_NOOP (Issue #4703):` markers explaining
  why a pass-through body is the correct sjulia semantics — both
  upstream uses are optimizer hints that the sjulia interpreter does
  not perform, so the marker also doubles as a hint to future authors
  that the body intentionally does not change.
- The accompanying audit script
  (`scripts/check_julia_base_stubs.sh`) and CI workflow registration
  are deferred to a follow-up PR because updating
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml` requires the GitHub `workflow` OAuth
  scope, which the current automation token does not have.

### Base.isvarargtype / Base.isvatuple replace stub implementations ✅ (Issue #4701)

- `subset_julia_vm/src/julia/base/essentials.jl`'s `isvarargtype(t)`
  always returned `false` and `isvatuple(t)` returned `t === Tuple`,
  so `Base.isvarargtype(Vararg{Int})` and
  `Base.isvatuple(Tuple{Int, Vararg{Int}})` both returned wrong values.
- Replaced with upstream-equivalent Pure Julia implementations:
  `isvarargtype(t) = isa(t, DataType) && nameof(t) === :Vararg` and an
  `isvatuple` that unwraps UnionAlls then checks the last `.parameters`
  entry. This is now tractable thanks to `Base.unwrap_unionall`
  (PR #4693), the registry-backed `.parameters` projection (PR #4693 /
  PR #4695), and TypeVar preservation in parametric application
  (PR #4697).
- New fixture `reflection_isvarargtype_4701` (12 cases) exercises both
  helpers across `Vararg{Int}`, `Vararg{Float64}`, plain DataTypes, and
  tuple types with and without a trailing Vararg. The same assertions
  pass under upstream Julia 1.12.

### Const-positive refinement for sqrt/log DomainError inference ✅ (Issue #4274)

- Previously every call to `sqrt`, `log`, `log10`, `log2` reported
  `ExceptionType::Known("DomainError")` and `nothrow=false` regardless
  of the argument. Upstream Julia combines constprop with the same
  call:`Base.infer_exception_type(() -> sqrt(4))` returns `Union{}`
  (nothrow). `Base.infer_exception_type(() -> sqrt(-1))` stays
  `DomainError`.
- `typed_exception_type_for_expr` is now generalised beyond the
  numeric-division slice. When the single argument is a
  `LatticeType::Const(Int64(n))` with `n >= 0`, or
  `Const(Float64(f))` with non-NaN `f >= 0.0`, the call is refined to
  `nothrow=true` / `ExceptionType::Bottom`. Known-negative constants
  keep the conservative `DomainError` exception type but tighten
  effects to `effect_free_may_throw`.
- The pre-existing
  `test_issue_3714_inferred_expr_tracks_call_exception_effects`
  assumed `sqrt(1)` would throw DomainError. It is updated to cover
  const-negative (`sqrt(-1)` → DomainError), const-positive
  (`sqrt(4)` → Bottom), float const (`sqrt(2.5)` → Bottom), and the
  same const refinement for `log` / `log10` / `log2`.
- Verified against upstream: `() -> sqrt(4)` and `() -> log(2)` both
  yield `Union{}`; `sqrt(-1)` yields `DomainError`.
- Remaining gap: `log(-1)` is `Union{DomainError, InexactError}`
  upstream. Our `ExceptionType` cannot yet represent a union of
  exception types, so we conservatively return `DomainError` — left
  on the broader #4274 backlog.

### Runtime TypeVar preserved in Vector{T}/Dict{K,V}/struct{T} ✅ (Issue #4696)

- `T = TypeVar(:T)` followed by `Vector{T}` previously erased `T` to
  `Any`, so `Vector{T}.parameters[1]` returned `Any` instead of `T`.
  The `ConstructParametricType` instruction stringified its type
  arguments and dropped `Value::RuntimeTypeVar` into the generic
  `"Any"` fallback arm.
- `vm/exec/struct_ops.rs` now writes the TypeVar's name into the
  parametric string for the generic path and also accepts
  `Value::RuntimeTypeVar` via `tv.projection()` for the special-case
  `num_type_args == 1` constructors (`Vector` / `Matrix` / `Type`).
- The change unblocks the semantic round-trip with
  `UnionAll(var, body)` (Issue #4694): `UnionAll(S, Vector{S})` now
  produces a real `Vector{S} where S` instead of `Vector{Any} where S`,
  so `Base.rewrap_unionall` and friends compose correctly.
- New fixture `reflection_parametric_runtime_typevar_4696` (13 cases)
  asserts kind+name preservation for `Vector`, `Matrix`, `Dict`, and
  user-defined parametric structs. The same assertions pass under
  upstream Julia 1.12.
- Remaining gap: TypeVar **identity** (`===`) between the original
  fresh `RuntimeTypeVar` and the projected parameter is still not
  preserved. Tracked under the broader runtime type-object identity
  work in Issue #3909.

### UnionAll(var, body) constructor + Base.rewrap_unionall ✅ (Issue #4694)

- `UnionAll(TypeVar(:T), Vector{Int64})` previously failed with
  "Function 'UnionAll' not found", which blocked Pure Julia
  reflection helpers like `Base.rewrap_unionall` and
  `Base.rename_unionall`. This is the natural follow-up to PR #4693
  (Issue #3909) which added `Base.unwrap_unionall`.
- New `BuiltinId::UnionAll` registered in `builtins.rs`. The handler
  in `vm/builtins_types.rs` pops `(var, body)`, accepts both
  `Value::RuntimeTypeVar` and registry-projected
  `Value::DataType(JuliaType::TypeVar(...))` for `var`, and returns
  a fresh `JuliaType::UnionAll { var, bound, body }`.
- Matches upstream `jl_type_unionall`'s "smart wrap" semantics: when
  the body does not reference the bound variable, return the body
  unchanged. Two new helpers (`julia_type_references_typevar` and
  `parametric_struct_mentions_typevar`) walk the JuliaType structure
  and also scan string-encoded names like `"Vector{T}"` for the var
  via word-boundary matching. This keeps
  `UnionAll(T, Vector{Int64}) === Vector{Int64}` and
  `Base.rewrap_unionall(Int64, Vector) === Int64` in agreement with
  upstream Julia.
- `julia/base/essentials.jl` now defines
  `rewrap_unionall(t, u) = isa(u, UnionAll) ? UnionAll(u.var, rewrap_unionall(t, u.body)) : t`,
  closing the round-trip with `Base.unwrap_unionall`.
- New fixture `reflection_unionall_constructor_4694` (9 cases)
  exercises the smart wrap and round-trip. The same assertions also
  pass under upstream Julia 1.12.

### isa kind agrees with typeof for runtime type objects + Base.unwrap_unionall ✅ (Issue #3909)

- `typeof(Vector) === UnionAll` was returning true but `isa(Vector, UnionAll)`
  returned false (and `isa(Vector, DataType)` returned true) because
  `Value::DataType(_)` always projected to `JuliaType::DataType` through
  `runtime_type()`, bypassing the kind classification owned by
  `RuntimeTypeRegistry`.
- `vm/builtins_types.rs`'s `BuiltinId::Isa` now routes `Value::DataType(jt)`
  through `RuntimeTypeRegistry::new_with_struct_defs(...).object(jt)
  .runtime_type_projection()`, which yields the registry's kind projection
  (`JuliaType::DataType`, `Struct("UnionAll")`, `Struct("TypeVar")`).
- `types/julia_type/comparison.rs`'s `JuliaType::Type` arm now also accepts
  `Struct("UnionAll")` so `isa(Vector, Type)` keeps returning true.
- `vm/exec/struct_ops.rs`'s `Instr::GetFieldByName` gained a
  `Value::DataType(jt)` block mirroring the static `ValueType::DataType`
  path in `compile/expr/struct_.rs`. Pure Julia helpers can now access
  `.parameters`, `.var`, `.body`, `.name`, `.lb`, `.ub` on a type-object
  value even when inference could not narrow the carrier to
  `ValueType::DataType` (e.g. parameters typed `Any`).
- `julia/base/essentials.jl`'s `unwrap_unionall(t)` was a stub returning
  `t` unchanged. Reimplemented as
  `while isa(t, UnionAll); t = t.body; end; return t`, matching upstream
  Julia's `Base.unwrap_unionall`.
- New fixture `reflection_isa_typeof_kind_consistency_3909` (24 cases)
  covers isa kind agreement and `Base.unwrap_unionall`. Verified the same
  assertions pass under upstream Julia.

### specializer widens slot type on incompatible reassignment ✅ (Issue #4688)

- `FunctionSpecializer::Stmt::Assign` previously overwrote
  `self.locals[var]` with each assignment's concrete type. For patterns
  like `x = "init"; for i in 1:n; x = 42; end; x` the body's `x = 42`
  latched `locals[x] = I64`, so the final read of `x` compiled to
  `LoadI64` (slot-rewritten to `LoadSlotI64`). When the loop ran zero
  iterations the slot still held the surviving `Str("init")` from the
  pre-loop store, and `LoadSlotI64` crashed with
  `expected numeric in x, got Str("init")`.
- `Stmt::Assign` now widens the *recorded* slot type to `ValueType::Any`
  whenever the previous binding had a different concrete type. The
  store itself still uses the value's concrete type (`StoreI64`,
  `StoreStr`, etc.) because the runtime slot is `Option<Value>` and can
  hold any tag. The widening only affects later `LoadXxx` emissions,
  which become `LoadAny` / `LoadSlot` (untyped) and read whichever
  concrete tag survived to that program point.
- The generic compiler (`compile/stmt.rs`'s `Stmt::Assign`) already
  handled the same case via `mixed_type_vars` populated by inference
  (Issues #3535 / #3536). This change brings the specializer to parity
  without copying the full mixed-type-vars infrastructure: the
  one-step type-changed guard is enough because the specializer
  visits each assignment in source order.
- Added `type_inference_slot_widening_4688` (10 cases) covering
  int/str/float overwrite inside a parametric for-loop and a partial
  `if` rebind. All match upstream Julia.

### specializer patches break/continue in for/while/foreach ✅ (Issue #4684)

- `FunctionSpecializer` (`vm/specialize/stmt.rs`)'s `compile_for`,
  `compile_while`, and `compile_foreach` never patched the placeholder
  `Jump(0)` instructions emitted by `Stmt::Break` and `Stmt::Continue`
  inside the loop body. After the call site relocated specialized
  bytecode by `entry_point` (`vm/exec/call.rs`), each unpatched
  `Jump(0)` became `Jump(entry_point)` — an unconditional jump back to
  the start of the specialized function — and any parametric-range
  for-loop with a top-level `break` would loop forever (the original
  Issue #4684 reproduction never returned).
- Each loop compiler now saves the enclosing loop's pending
  `break_positions` / `continue_positions` via `std::mem::take`,
  compiles the body, patches every entry the body accumulated to the
  correct target (loop exit for break, `continue_target` for `for` /
  `foreach`, `loop_start` for `while`), and restores the outer loop's
  pending lists so nested loops route their own break/continue
  correctly.
- Added `control_flow_for_break_dynamic_range_4684` covering
  top-level break, break with assignment, break with String overwrite,
  `continue`, conditional break inside an `if`, and a nested-loop
  inner-break — 15 assertions matching upstream Julia. Issue #4680's
  fixture (`type_inference_for_break_const_range_4680.jl`) intentionally
  omitted the dynamic `1:n` runtime call because of this hang; that
  case is now safe to exercise on sjulia (left as a future follow-up
  PR alongside the fixture extension).

### call-site `==` against Union-typed function return defers to runtime dispatch ✅ (Issue #4686)

- Root cause of Issue #4682 (closed by PR #4685's regression fixture
  after the constant-range narrowing in PR #4683 sidestepped it). The
  `Str-vs-non-Str` shortcut in `compile/expr/binary/mod.rs`
  constant-folded `==` to `false` whenever exactly one side had
  `ValueType::Str` and the other was neither `Str` nor `Any`. The
  shortcut did not account for `ValueType::Union(_)`: a slot inferred
  as `Union{Int64, String}` can hold a `String` at runtime that should
  compare equal to the literal on the other side, but the compiler
  emitted `PushBool(false)` and silently miscompiled `f() == "s"`.
- Extended `left_is_runtime_unknown` / `right_is_runtime_unknown` to
  match `ValueType::Any | ValueType::Union(_)` so Union-typed operands
  fall through to the runtime-dispatch path already shared with `Any`
  (`has_any` at the end of the function). For Unions that don't
  include `Str` (e.g. `Union{Int64, Float64} == "s"`) the runtime path
  still returns `false`, just via dispatch instead of constant folding
  — correctness is preserved, the only cost is a slightly later
  decision point.
- Added `comparison_union_eq_string_4686` exercising the
  Union-returning for-loop call site, the reverse polarity (`"s" ==
  f()`), the via-binding path, the Int-arm runtime value, and an
  if-Union end-to-end flow. Skipped the `Union{Int64, String}` slot
  with a String runtime value in the loop-zero-iteration case because
  it trips a separate `LoadSlotI64` slot-allocator bug not in scope
  for this PR.

### for-loop + break over non-empty constant range narrows post-loop env ✅ (Issue #4680)

- Follow-up to PR #4678 / PR #4681 (Issues #4267, #4679). Upstream Julia
  models `for var in start:end` over a provably-non-empty constant
  range with a top-level `break` as exiting only via the break edge —
  the pre-loop env never falls through because the loop is guaranteed
  to run at least once, and the end-of-iteration env is unreachable
  past the break. sjulia previously merged the pre-loop env into the
  post-loop env, producing wider `Union{...}` returns (e.g. the issue's
  `for i in 1:3; x = "s"; break; end` returning `Union{Int64, String}`
  instead of `String`).
- Added `InferenceEngine::range_provably_non_empty`, a constant-bounds
  oracle over the `start`/`end`/optional `step` lattice values. It
  recognizes `Const(Int64)` triples and applies the sign-of-step rule
  (`step > 0 ⇒ start ≤ end`, `step < 0 ⇒ start ≥ end`, `step = 0 ⇒
  empty`), and bails out for dynamic bounds, non-integer types, and
  other unknown shapes. Float ranges are intentionally left out of this
  slice because of their rounding edge cases.
- `Stmt::For` now computes `range_non_empty` up front and inspects the
  body for a top-level `Stmt::Break` (`body_has_direct_break`). When
  both hold the post-loop env is replaced with the joined break-exit
  env — mirroring the statically-true `while` slice. When the break is
  nested in an `if`/`try` the end-of-range exit edge is still
  reachable, so the legacy pre-loop merge is preserved. This matches
  upstream Julia's behavior of keeping the `Union{...}` for the
  conditional-break case.
- Added `type_inference_for_break_const_range_4680` exercising the
  basic `1:3` repro, `1:2:6`/`5:-1:1` step variants, a pre-existing
  `String` overwrite, a nested-break case, and a dynamic `1:n` contrast
  that should keep the wider `Union{Int64, String}` to lock in the
  precision difference. Both runtime (`===`) and `Base.return_types` /
  `Base.infer_return_type` are checked. The existing
  `type_inference_while_true_break_4267` and
  `type_inference_for_range_loop_var_type` fixtures continue to pass,
  per the issue's acceptance criteria.
- Discovered while implementing this slice (both surface separately,
  not blocked on #4680):
  - `for_v() == "s"` at the call site returns `false` even though
    `typeof(for_v()) === String` and `for_v() === "s"` is `true` —
    likely a codegen path for static dispatch of `==` after a
    for-loop. Filed as Issue #4682.
  - `for i in 1:n; ...; break; end` (parametric range, top-level
    break) hangs sjulia at runtime even though inference returns the
    correct `Union{Int64, String}`. The fixture uses constant ranges
    for runtime checks and only asserts inference for the dynamic
    `1:n` case to avoid this hang.

### `while true` no-exit collapses post-loop env to `Union{}` ✅ (Issue #4679)

- Follow-up to PR #4678 (Issue #4267 break-env slice). Upstream Julia
  models a statically-true `while` whose body has no `break`,
  `return`, or `throw` as never falling through and surfaces the
  post-loop env as `Union{}` (Bottom), so the enclosing function
  return type collapses to `Union{}`. sjulia previously kept the body
  fixpoint output, producing a sound-but-wider `Int64`/etc.
- Added a `StmtResult::Diverges` variant. `Stmt::While` now emits it
  when `condition_always_true` is true, the break-env stack slot is
  empty, and no explicit `return` was accumulated. `infer_block_branch`
  treats this as a non-falling statement: it drops `last_stmt_type` to
  `LatticeType::Bottom`, sets `may_fallthrough = false`, and stops
  iterating since subsequent statements are unreachable in the
  abstract domain. `infer_block_explicit_return_only` and
  `infer_block_partial_struct_return` route `Diverges` the same way.
- `lattice_to_parametric_julia_type` now preserves
  `LatticeType::Bottom` as `JuliaType::Bottom`. The legacy
  `LatticeType::Bottom → ValueType::Any` fallback in
  `lattice_to_value_type` would otherwise widen `Union{}` back to
  `Any` when reflection's `m.return_type` snapshot is materialized
  via `value_type_to_julia_type`.
- Added `type_inference_while_true_no_exit_4679` exercising the basic
  no-break loop, dead-code-after-loop, `Const(true)` variable
  condition, nested outer-no-break/inner-break, and pure literal
  `while true` cases — runtime, `Base.return_types`, and
  `Base.infer_return_type` all match upstream Julia returning
  `Union{}`. Existing `type_inference_while_true_break_4267` and
  `type_inference_while_exit_narrowing_4267` continue to pass.
- Base call sites in `base/dict.jl` and `base/reflection.jl` use
  `while true` with `return` exits inside the body, so
  `accumulated_return` is `Some(_)` and the new `Diverges` branch is
  not taken there — `MaybeReturn` semantics preserved.

### statically-true while + break exit narrowing ✅ (Issue #4267)

- Added a per-loop break-env stack on `InferenceEngine`. `Stmt::Break` now
  snapshots the current path-sensitive env into the innermost loop's slot;
  `while`/`for`/`foreach` push and pop the slot so nested loops dispatch
  breaks to the correct target.
- `Stmt::While` detects statically-true conditions (literal `Bool(true)`
  or a variable bound to `Const(true)`). For those loops the post-loop
  env is the joined break-exit env when at least one break was seen, since
  the condition-false exit edge is unreachable.
- When the always-true loop has no break, the body fixpoint output is
  retained as a sound over-approximation of the infinite-loop case
  (upstream Julia marks this as `Union{}`; sjulia still keeps that as
  follow-up work).
- Existing `Stmt::While` handling for non-statically-true conditions is
  unchanged — pre-loop merge and exit narrowing still apply, so the
  Issue #3517 / #4267 first-slice cases continue to pass.
- Added `type_inference_while_true_break_4267`, covering single break,
  const-true condition, break-in-if, overwriting break, and nested
  while-true via runtime, `Base.infer_return_type`, and `Base.return_types`
  parity against upstream Julia.
- Keeping #4267 open for the broader goal: routing production inference
  through lowered CFG blocks, block input/output state, statement side
  tables, and Phi/SSA value typing.

### Plots function/x argument normalization ✅ (Issue #4448)

- Added bundled `Plots` methods for `plot(f::Function, x)`,
  `plot!(f::Function, x)`, `scatter(f::Function, x)`, and
  `scatter!(f::Function, x)`, forwarding to the corresponding `(x, f)` forms.
- Materialized `x` with `collect(x)` before `map(f, x)` so range inputs produce
  vector-backed `Series.x` and `Series.y`, matching the upstream recipe path.
- Extended `packages_plots_function_xy_4452` with the reported
  `plot(-0.1:0.01:1, cos); scatter!(-0.1:0.01:1, sin)` case and swapped
  `plot(cos, xs)` / `scatter(sin, xs)` coverage.

### generic DataType getfield parameters ✅ (Issue #4673)

- `getfield(::DataType, :parameters)` now uses the runtime type object registry
  instead of treating DataType as an unsupported non-struct field receiver.
- Generic `where T` methods can project type parameters through
  `getfield(T, :parameters)[1]`, matching upstream Julia.
- Extended `reflection_type_parameters`.

### logical Array wrapper equality ✅ (Issues #4653, #4675)

- Equality now compares array wrappers by logical shape and logical element
  values instead of raw backing Memory length.
- `Array` / `Vector` / `Matrix` wrapper aliases are accepted by the shared
  linalg ArrayValue conversion helper, including nested wrapper `_mem` storage.
- Added `array_matrix_equality_4653` and restored direct String vector equality
  in `views_selectdim_dropdims_string_fallback_4591`.

### range adjoint assigned-local size dispatch ✅ (Issue #4572)

- `adjoint` / `transpose` inference for range-like structs now returns an array
  storage type rather than preserving `LinRange` / `StepRangeLen`.
- Assigned range-adjoint rows now dispatch `size(a)` through the Array method
  after `a = adjoint(LinRange(...))`.
- Extended fixture `array_range_adjoint_similar_allocation_4018`.

### anonymous function bindings inside array/tuple literals ✅ (Issue #4650)

- Propagated lambda-context lowering through collection and tuple literal
  children so nested `->` expressions are lifted and registered before use.
- `Any[(..., () -> ...)]` can now store a callable tuple element and later call
  it after tuple destructuring without `UndefVarError`.
- Added fixture `closures_any_tuple_array_lambda_4650`.

### getfield(Main, ::Symbol) module binding lookup ✅ (Issue #4621)

- `getfield(::Module, ::Symbol)` now resolves module bindings for `Main`
  instead of rejecting module receivers in the reflection builtin path.
- `Main` lookup checks the global frame first and then function table bindings,
  so `getfield(Main, :reduce)` returns the same function object as `reduce`.
- Added fixture `reflection_getfield_module_binding_4621`.

### parenthesized callable `!` broadcast lowering ✅ (Issue #4640)

- `(!).(xs)` now lowers through the Pure Julia broadcast materialization path
  instead of failing as an unsupported call target.
- Direct callable `(!)(false)` and `typeof((!))` remain covered as first-class
  operator function references.
- Extended fixture `broadcast_unary_dot_not_4626`.

### multiline tuple literal parsing ✅ (Issue #4654)

- Tuple / parenthesized expression parsing now treats newlines after `(` and
  tuple elements as intra-expression whitespace.
- Multiline tuple literals now parse after assignment and in `for ... in (...)`
  clauses.
- Added fixture `tuple_multiline_tuple_literal_4654`.

### Value::Array enum variant retirement ✅ (Issue #4568)

### scalar narrow-number flatten collect ✅ (Issue #4666)

- `collect(Base.Iterators.flatten((Int8(1), Int16(2))))` now returns
  `Vector{Signed}`, matching upstream Julia instead of erroring on scalar
  `Int8` iteration.
- VM scalar `Number` iteration now covers the native narrow signed/unsigned
  integer and float carriers in addition to the existing `Int64`/`Float64`
  paths.
- Added fixture `iteration_flatten_narrow_scalar_collect_4666`.

### number eltype dynamic dispatch ✅ (Issue #4665)

- `eltype(x)` inside a generic function now returns the upstream scalar number
  element type instead of `Any`.
- The `Eltype` builtin fallback now returns `runtime_type()` for native scalar
  number carriers, matching upstream's number eltype protocol when sjulia routes
  generic calls through builtin fallback.
- Added fixture `types_eltype_number_dynamic_dispatch_4665`.

### scalar flatten collect ✅ (Issue #4664)

- `collect(Base.Iterators.flatten((1, 2)))` now returns `Vector{Int64}`,
  matching upstream Julia instead of widening to `Vector{Any}`.
- Scalar `Number` inner values in `Flatten` now contribute `typeof(inner)` to
  runtime eltype derivation, preserving homogeneous Float64 and mixed
  Int64/Float64 scalar flatten results as well.
- Added fixture `iteration_flatten_scalar_collect_4664`.
- The broader dynamic `eltype(x::Number)` dispatch gap found while fixing this
  slice is tracked and fixed as bug #4665.

### flatten mixed eltype collect ✅ (Issue #4663)

- `collect(Base.Iterators.flatten((Int8[...], Int16[...])))` now returns
  `Vector{Signed}`, matching upstream Julia instead of widening to
  `Vector{Any}`.
- `Flatten` now reports `HasEltype()` and derives its runtime eltype from the
  joined inner iterable eltypes, covering `Signed`, `Unsigned`, `Integer`, and
  `AbstractFloat` representative cases.
- Added fixture `iteration_flatten_mixed_eltype_collect_4663`.
- The separate scalar `flatten((1, 2))` widening observed during probing is
  tracked as bug #4664.

### tuple collect abstract numeric eltype ✅ (Issue #4662)

- `collect((Int8(1), Int16(2)))` now returns `Vector{Signed}`, matching
  upstream Julia instead of widening the allocation to `Vector{Real}`.
- `Vector{Number}` / `Vector{Real}` / `Vector{Integer}` / `Vector{Signed}` /
  `Vector{Unsigned}` / `Vector{AbstractFloat}` typed undef allocation now keeps
  the requested abstract numeric element type.
- Added fixture `array_tuple_collect_abstract_numeric_eltype_4662`.

### indexin Union result type ✅ (Issue #4657)

- `indexin(a, b)` now returns `Vector{Union{Nothing, Int64}}` for array-key
  inputs, matching upstream Julia instead of widening to `Vector{Any}`.
- `Vector{Union{Nothing, Int64}}(undef, n)`,
  `_array_undef_from_dims(Union{Nothing, Int64}, dims)`, and
  `similar(Array{Union{Nothing, Int64}}, dims)` preserve their Union element
  tags through Memory-first allocation.
- Callable-value dispatch now applies the same non-exact `Type{Any}` demotion
  as typed-dispatch, so generic `::Type{T} where T` methods bind Union type
  objects instead of falling into `::Type{Any}` specializations.
- Added Pure Julia `convert(::Type{Union{Nothing, Int64}}, ...)` coverage needed
  by Array `setindex!`, and fixture `array_indexin_union_result_4657`.

### typed Set construction and Set/Vector set algebra ✅ (Issue #4018)

- `typeof(Set(Int8[...]))` / `eltype(Set(Int8[...]))` now report
  `Set{Int8}` / `Int8` from the homogeneous stored keys instead of fixed
  `Set{Any}`, and `Set(Float32[...])` accepts Float32 keys without invalid-key
  errors (Issue #4609).
- `Set{Int8}()` now preserves the explicit element type through `typeof`,
  `eltype`, `collect`, and `empty!` even before any element is inserted.
- Pure Julia `union` / `intersect` / `setdiff` / `symdiff` on `Set` now keep
  the returned set value from `push!` / `delete!`, preserving non-empty results
  and their element type projection.
- Mixed `Set`/`Vector` representative paths now match upstream result shape:
  Set-first forms return `Set{Int8}`, while Vector-first forms return
  `Vector{Int8}`.
- `JuliaType::Set` now represents the bare `Set` family name for dispatch, so
  `Set{T} <: Set` and `empty!(s::Set)` match upstream behavior.
- Local `Set` bindings now use `StoreSet`, and direct `push!(s, x)`,
  `delete!(s, x)`, and `empty!(s)` compile to in-place Set storage updates.
- 作業中に見つけた typed Set widening bug は Issue #4658 として報告済みで、
  fixture `collections_set_typed_operations_4658` を追加した。typed Set metadata
  で露見した bare `Set` subtype / dispatch bug は Issue #4660 として報告済み。
  空 `Set{T}()` の element type drop は Issue #4661 として報告済みで、
  fixture `collections_set_typed_empty_constructor_4661` を追加した。

### empty integer division binary map typed allocation ✅ (Issue #4019)

- `map(/, A::Vector{<:Integer}, B::Vector{<:Integer})` と
  `map(/, Bool[], Bool[])` の empty-input result allocation を
  `Vector{Float64}` に固定する singleton-function specializations を追加した。
- これにより non-empty path と同じく upstream Julia の division result eltype に
  合わせ、`similar(A, 0)` による input-eltype fallback を避ける。
- 作業中に見つけた `map(/, Int8[], Int8[])` の empty result eltype bug は
  Issue #4659 として報告済みで、fixture
  `hof_map_binary_type_preservation_4610` を拡張した。

### permutedims no-perm typed allocation ✅ (Issue #4018)

- `permutedims(arr)` without an explicit permutation now uses
  `similar(arr, ...)` result allocation for vector row conversion and 2D
  transpose.
- This removes the previous `Any[]` fallback for element types outside the
  hand-written special-case list; `Int8` and `Float32` inputs now preserve
  `Matrix{Int8}` / `Matrix{Float32}` result eltypes.
- 作業中に見つけた no-perm `permutedims` widening bug は Issue #4656 として
  報告済みで、fixture `array_permutedims_type_preservation` を拡張した。

### hcat/vcat mixed eltype promotion ✅ (Issue #4018)

- `hcat` / `vcat` mixed vector result allocation を `promote_type` +
  `_array_undef_from_dims` へ移し、upstream Julia と同じ promoted result
  eltype を使うようにした。
- `Int8` + `Int16` は `Matrix{Int16}` / `Vector{Int16}`、`Int8` +
  `Float32` は `Matrix{Float32}` / `Vector{Float32}`、`String` + `Any` は
  `Matrix{Any}` / `Vector{Any}` として materialize する。
- 作業中に見つけた mixed concat の result eltype bug は Issue #4655 として
  報告済みで、fixture `array_concat_mixed_type_preservation_4655` を追加した。

### stack mixed eltype promotion ✅ (Issue #4018)

- `stack(arrays)` の mixed-eltype result allocation を `Matrix{Any}` fallback
  から `promote_type` + `_array_undef_from_dims` に移し、upstream Julia と同じ
  promoted result eltype を使うようにした。
- `Int8` + `Int16` は `Matrix{Int16}`、`Int8` + `Float32` は
  `Matrix{Float32}`、`String` + `Any` は `Matrix{Any}` として materialize する。
- 作業中に見つけた mixed stack の `Matrix{Any}` widening bug は Issue #4652、
  typed/boxed matrix equality gap は Issue #4653 として報告済み。

### cat mixed eltype promotion ✅ (Issue #4018)

- `cat(A, B; dims)` の mixed-eltype result allocation を
  `promote_type(eltype(A), eltype(B))` と `_array_undef_from_dims` に寄せ、
  upstream Julia と同じ promoted result eltype を使うようにした。
- `Int8` + `Int16` は `Vector{Int16}`、`Int8` + `Float32` は
  `Vector{Float32}`、`String` + `Any` は `Vector{Any}` として materialize する。
- 作業中に見つけた mixed cat の `Float64` widening / `String` conversion
  error は Issue #4651 として報告済みで、fixture
  `array_cat_string_type_preservation_4592` に regression coverage を追加した。

### Partition vector chunk view eltype preservation ✅ (Issues #4648/#4649)

- `partition(::Vector, n)` now yields `SubArray` view chunks for vector inputs,
  matching upstream Julia's allocation model more closely than the previous
  `[]` / `Vector{Any}` chunk fallback.
- `SubArray{T}` gained generic 1D view, trait, iteration, indexing, collect,
  parent, and parentindices methods, so narrow vector views such as
  `view(Int8[4, 5, 6], 1:2)` keep `SubArray{Int8}` metadata.
- `Vector{SubArray{T}}` collect allocation now uses the `_array_undef_from_dims`
  wrapper path for `SubArray{T}` element types.
- fixture `iteration_partition` を拡張し、Issues #4648/#4649 を固定した。

### Rest explicit Array state parity ✅ (Issue #4647)

- Legacy native Array iteration now matches upstream Julia's state convention:
  the yielded state is the next 1-based index, so `iterate(a, 2)` starts from
  the second element instead of the third.
- `Iterators.rest(array, state)` now materializes from the explicit upstream
  state without an extra skip, covering `collect(rest(Int8[1, 2, 3], 2)) ==
  Int8[2, 3]`.
- fixture `iteration_rest` を拡張し、Issue #4647 を固定した。

### Array{Any}/Array{Real} boxed numeric IndexStore preservation ✅ (Issue #4646)

- Direct `Array{Any}` / `Array{Real}` index assignment now preserves boxed
  narrow integer and `Float32` values instead of widening them through the
  scalar `F64` IndexStore path before Julia `setindex!` can apply
  `convert(T, v)`.
- The compiler skips pre-`IndexStore` `ToF64` coercion for boxed numeric array
  targets, and the VM routes numeric assignment to Pure Julia wrapper structs
  through the boxed value path.
- fixture `array_any_preserves_narrow_integer_4646` を追加し、Issue #4646 を
  固定した。

## 最新対応 (2026-05-26)

### generic similar(Array{T}, dims) tuple dispatch ✅ (Issues #4569/#4643)

- `similar(Array{T}, dims)` now works from `where T` helpers for tuple dims
  while preserving element type and shape for representative `Int64`,
  `Float64`, `Bool`, and `Complex{Float64}` arrays.
- Runtime `Array{T,length(dims)}` type construction now preserves the integer
  rank parameter and normalizes `Array{T,1}` / `Array{T,2}` to
  `Vector{T}` / `Matrix{T}`, so `typeof(similar(Array{T}, dims)) ===
  Array{T,length(dims)}` matches upstream Julia (Issue #4644).
- Runtime method search now treats concrete tuple runtime names such as
  `Tuple{Int64}` as matching a bare `::Tuple` parameter, so the
  dispatch-first `similar(::Type{Array{T}}, dims::Tuple)` path wins before
  the transitional builtin fallback.
- `similar` lowering now leaves `Any` dims uncoerced so an unannotated local
  or argument containing tuple dims reaches runtime dispatch instead of
  `DynamicToI64`.
- fixture `array_zeros_ones_fill_tuple_dims_4018` now covers both annotated
  `dims::Tuple` (#4569) and unannotated tuple dims (#4643).

### mixed String equality fallback ✅ (Issue #4642)

- Static `String`-vs-non-`String` `==` / `!=` now evaluates both operands and
  returns Julia's generic equality fallback result instead of coercing the
  non-String operand.
- Dynamic `Any` equality fallback now returns `false` / `true` for no-method
  mixed equality pairs.
- fixture `operators_mixed_string_equality_4642` を追加した。

### prefix dotted not broadcast syntax ✅ (Issue #4019)

- Julia prefix broadcast-not syntax `.!xs` now parses as a broadcast call and
  lowers through the existing Pure Julia broadcast materialization pipeline.
- `.!Bool[true, false]` now evaluates element-wise instead of failing with a
  parse error.
- The callable `!` function-value path exposed during validation was filed as
  Issue #4640 and fixed through the VM intrinsic fallback used by broadcast.
- fixture `broadcast_unary_dot_not_4626` を追加した。

### Vector{Any} tuple element destructuring ✅ (Issue #4019)

- Typed array constructor lowering now preserves tuple expressions as single
  elements for type-like targets, so `Any[(name, values)]` creates a
  one-element `Vector{Any}` instead of flattening the tuple into two elements.
- This fixes `for (name, values) in cases` over `Vector{Any}` broadcast probe
  cases where each element is a tuple.
- fixture `broadcast_vector_any_tuple_destructuring_4627` を追加した。

### runtime DataType typed array constructor ✅ (Issue #4018)

- Runtime `DataType` indexing now follows Julia's typed array constructor
  semantics for representative vector literals: `T[1, 2]`,
  `getindex(T, 3, 4)`, and abstract `Real[...]` / `Number[...]` construct
  `Vector{T}` instead of trying to index the `DataType` value itself, while
  preserving concrete stored values such as `1.5::Float64` and
  `Float32(2.5)`.
- The VM `IndexLoad` path now allocates a typed vector from the runtime element
  type when its target is `Value::DataType`.
- fixture `array_runtime_datatype_typed_array_constructor_4606` を追加し、
  Issues #4586/#4606/#4641 を固定した。

### typed Vector equality bridge ✅ (Issue #4639)

- `CallDynamicBinaryBoth` no-method fallback now handles legacy native
  Array-vs-Array `==` / `!=` through a scoped equality bridge.
- `Int16[1, 2] == Int16[1, 2]` and variable-bound `Vector{Int16}` equality now
  match upstream Julia during the #3908 migration.
- fixture `array_typed_vector_equality_4639` を追加し、#4606 fixture の
  workaround を direct `Vector{Int16}` equality に戻した。

### typed matrix literal lowering ✅ (Issues #4575/#4629)

- `Float32[1 2; 3 4]` / `Real[1 2.0; 3 4.0]` style typed matrix literals now
  lower successfully.
- Lowering reuses typed vector construction plus `reshape`, preserving
  column-major storage and the requested matrix element type.
- fixture `array_typed_matrix_literal_4575_4629` を追加し、#4628 broadcast
  fixture の typed matrix literal workaround を削除した。

### floating-point Dict/Set keys ✅ (Issue #4018)

- Rust-backed `Dict` and `Set` now accept `Float16` / `Float32` / `Float64`
  scalar keys instead of rejecting them as invalid dictionary keys.
- `DictKey` equality/hash now follows representative Julia `isequal` behavior
  for integer-compatible floating-point keys and keeps `-0.0` distinct from
  `0.0`.
- `Set(Float32[...])` now constructs successfully and supports membership with
  Julia's floating-point key semantics.
- fixture `collections_dict_set_float_keys_4638` を追加した。

### Dict Pair destructuring comprehension ✅ (Issue #4018)

- Array comprehensions now lower tuple destructuring bindings like
  `[k for (k, v) in d]`.
- Tuple destructuring comprehensions compile through the existing
  `iterate`-based loop path, so `Dict` Pair iteration no longer requires an
  indexable collection fallback.
- fixture `collections_dict_pair_destructuring_comprehension_4632` を追加した。

### narrow integer identity / membership ✅ (Issue #4637)

- `Int8` / `Int16` / `Int32` / `Int128` and unsigned narrow integer `===`
  now match upstream same-type identity semantics.
- `isequal` and `hash` canonicalize supported integer widths by numeric value,
  preserving Julia's `isequal(x, y) => hash(x) == hash(y)` invariant for
  representative narrow integer values.
- Tuple membership now uses numeric integer equality across supported widths,
  so `Int8(1) in (Int16(1), Int16(3))` matches upstream Julia.
- fixture `operators_narrow_integer_identity_membership_4637` を追加した。

### Dict narrow integer keys ✅ (Issue #4018)

- Rust-backed `Dict` now accepts narrow integer key values, including the
  `Dict(Int8(1) => Int16(2), Int8(3) => Int16(4))` path reported as Issue #4633.
- `keytype` / `valtype`, lookup, mutation, and `collect(keys(d))` preserve the
  representative `Int8` / `Int16` metadata used by upstream Julia.
- `DictKey` stores narrow integer key variants and compares/hashes integer keys
  by numeric value across supported integer widths.
- fixture `collections_dict_narrow_integer_keys_4633` を追加した。
- 検証中に見つけた narrow integer `===` / tuple `in` gap は Issue #4637
  として報告済み。

### Pair Type dispatch/reflection specificity ✅ (Issue #4018)

- `Type{Pair{K,V}}` methods now win over bare `Type{Pair}` methods for concrete
  Pair type objects in static dispatch and `which` reflection.
- `which` now shares the runtime Julia signature binding/scoring path for
  `Type{Pair{Int64,Int8}}` arguments, preserving upstream method choice.
- fixture `reflection_pair_type_parameter_dispatch_4636` を追加した。
- 作業中に見つけた direct static helper/reflection mismatch は Issue #4636
  として報告済みで、ローカル修正済み。

### Pair typed undef allocation ✅ (Issue #4018)

- `Array{Pair{Int64,Int8}}(undef, n)` and
  `similar(Array{Pair{String,Int16}}, dims)` now return upstream-matching
  `Vector{Pair{...}}` results.
- Runtime callable dispatch uses structured `Type{Pair{K,V}}` matching and
  scoring, and `Memory{Pair{K,V}}` constructors assemble the runtime DataType
  from bound type parameters.
- fixture `array_pair_typed_undef_allocation_4635` was added.
- The direct static helper/reflection mismatch filed as Issue #4636 is now
  fixed in the follow-up section above.

### Pair-valued pairs collect typed allocation ✅ (Issue #4018)

- `collect(pairs(::Vector{Int8}))` and `collect(pairs(::Tuple{Int8,Int8}))`
  now return `Vector{Pair{Int64, Int8}}`, matching upstream Julia.
- `pairs(...)` inference keeps the `Pairs` carrier for array-like collections,
  and public `collect(::Pairs)` uses the Pure Julia `_pairs_collect_dynamic`
  path before the remaining native range/generator bridge.
- fixture `collections_pairs_collect_type_preservation_4634` を追加した。
- 作業中に見つけた Pair-valued collect widening bug は Issue #4634 として

  として切り出し済み。

### generator expression collect typed allocation ✅ (Issue #4018)

- Comprehension-backed generator expressions now preserve representative narrow
  scalar source element types when materialized through `collect`.
- `collect(x for x in Int8[...])`, filtered `Int8` generators, same-typed
  `Int8` tuple generators, and `Float32` array generators allocate
  `Vector{Int8}` / `Vector{Float32}` results to match upstream Julia.
- fixture `generator_collect_narrow_type_preservation_4631` を追加した。
- 作業中に見つけた generator collect over `Int8` sources の `Vector{Float64}`
  widening bug は Issue #4631 として報告済み。

### mixed Vector set algebra allocation ✅ (Issue #4018)

- Generic `union` / `intersect` / `setdiff` / `symdiff` for mixed-element
  `Vector` inputs now allocate with `promote_type(eltype(a), eltype(b))`
  through `_array_undef_from_dims` instead of `[]`.
- Representative `Int8` + `Int16` results now return `Vector{Int16}` and
  `Int8` + `Float32` union returns `Vector{Float32}`, matching upstream Julia.
- fixture `collections_set_ops_mixed_type_preservation_4630` を追加した。
- 作業中に見つけた mixed Vector set operation `Vector{Any}` widening bug は
  Issue #4630 として報告済み。

### broadcast materialization type preservation ✅ (Issue #4019)

- `Broadcasted` materialization の result type selection を拡張し、representative
  `Float32` / small signed integer / unsigned integer / `String` result arrays が
  upstream Julia と同じ eltype を保持するようにした。
- same-eltype arithmetic broadcast は source element type を result allocation に
  使い、`Float32` division も `Float32` result を返す。
- fixture `broadcast_materialization_type_preservation_4628` を追加した。
- 作業中に見つけた broadcast materialization widening bug は Issue #4628、
  probe 中に見つけた `.!` parser gap は Issue #4626、`Vector{Any}` tuple
  destructuring gap は Issue #4627 として報告済み。

### typed subtractive reductions ✅ (Issue #4019)

- `reduce(-, ::Vector{T})` / `foldl(-, ::Vector{T})` /
  `foldr(-, ::Vector{T})` と `mapfoldl(identity, -, ::Vector{T})` /
  `mapfoldr(identity, -, ::Vector{T})` / `mapreduce(identity, -, ::Vector{T})`
  に typed Vector specializations を追加し、left/right fold order と
  representative result type を upstream Julia に合わせた。
- small signed / unsigned integer input は source element type、`Float32` input は
  source float type を保持する。unsigned `init` paths は upstream の wraparound
  result を返す。
- fixture `hof_reduction_minus_type_preservation_4625` を追加した。

### typed multiplicative reductions ✅ (Issue #4019)

  に typed Vector specializations を追加し、empty input の identity と
  representative non-empty result type を upstream Julia に合わせた。

  source element type、`Float32` / `Float64` input は source float type を保持する。
- Scalar `Bool * Bool` now preserves `Bool` through the compiler binary path
  instead of widening to `Int64` (Issue #4624).

  `UInt16` / `UInt32` / `UInt64` input は `Vector{UInt64}` に昇格し、
  `Float32` / `Float64` input は `similar(arr, length(arr))` により同型
  result を返す。`Bool` は `cumsum` を `Vector{Int64}`、`cumprod` を

  報告済み。

### unique and Vector set algebra similar fallback ✅ (Issue #4018)

- `base/set.jl` の `unique` / `unique(f, arr)` に、
  `Int8` / `Int16` / `Int32` / `UInt8` / `UInt16` / `UInt32` /
  `UInt64` / `Float32` / `Symbol` / `Any` の concrete Vector
  specializations を追加し、結果配列を `similar(arr, 0)` で確保するようにした。
- これにより `unique(Int8[1,2,1])`、`unique([:a,:b,:a])`、
  `unique(identity, Int16[1,2,1])` が上流 Julia と同じ
  `Vector{Int8}` / `Vector{Symbol}` / `Vector{Int16}` を返す。
- `union` / `intersect` / `setdiff` / `symdiff` の same-element Vector
  paths も `similar(a, 0)` allocation に移し、同型 Vector の result type が
  上流 Julia と同じ `Vector{T}` になるようにした。
- fixture は `Int8` union、`Int16` intersect、`Float32` setdiff、
  `Symbol` symdiff、homogeneous `Vector{Any}` union を `typeof` / `eltype`
  まで検証する。
- generic `arr::Vector` signature は current method dispatch では
  `Any` fallback と曖昧になるため採用せず、concrete element-type methods
  に限定した。
- 作業中に見つけた `Real[...]` / `Number[...]` typed literal の
  `DataType` indexing error は Issue #4586 として切り出し、
  runtime DataType typed-array constructor fixture に固定してローカル確認済み。
  heterogeneous `Vector{Any}` の mixed `isequal` error は Issue #4587
  として切り出し、`operators.jl` の String-vs-other `isequal` fallback で
  `unique(Any[1, "a", 1])` をローカル修正済み。
  raw mixed `==` / `!=` fallback の broader parity gap は Issue #4642 として
  報告し、ローカル修正済み。
- #4018 の Array wrapper allocation により露出した
  `in(::Any, ::Vector{Complex{Float64}})` の `StructRef` receiver rejection は
  Issue #4588 として切り出し、builtin `in` が wrapper `_mem` の logical
  elements を走査できるようにした。
- `Vector{Any}` equality が `operator(Vector{Any}, Vector{Any})` に落ちる
  gap は Issue #4589 として切り出し、現在は `Any[1,2] == Any[1,2]` と
  `union(Any[1,2], Any[2,3]) == Any[1,2,3]` をローカル確認済み。

### test-side Value::Array comment allowlist cleanup ✅ (Issue #3908)

- `subset_julia_vm/tests/test_mandelbrot_grid_comparison.rs` の説明コメントに
  残っていた literal `Value::Array` token を legacy native-array variant
  への言及に言い換え、テスト配下の `Value::Array` hits を 1 → 0 にした。
- `scripts/check_value_array_allowlist.sh` から test-side 例外を削除し、
  `subset_julia_vm/tests/` に新しい literal `Value::Array` が出た場合は
  監査で検出される状態にした。

### zeros/ones/fill tuple-dims similar(Array) allocation ✅ (Issue #4018)

- `fill(value, dims...)` の Pure Julia 実装を `_array_undef_from_dims`
  経由に統一し、concrete element type では直接
  `Array{T}(undef, ...)` を呼ばず `similar(Array{T}, dims)` で
  Memory-backed Array wrapper を確保する。
- `zeros` / `ones` の typed tuple-dims 経路も同じ helper を使い、
  `Int64` と `Complex{Float64}` の tuple-dims forms を concrete method
  として追加した。
- 4D tuple-dims の `fill` / `zeros` と `similar(Array{Real}, dims)` も
  fixture に追加し、high-rank shape と abstract numeric element type の
  storage-type allocation parity を確認した。
- runtime dispatch resolver が `Type{Array{T}}` を
  `Type{Array{Int64}}` などの concrete DataType 値に対して束縛できるようにし、
  generic `where T` helper からも `similar(Array{T}, dims)` を使えるようにした
  (Issue #4569)。
- `adjoint(::LinRange)` / `adjoint(::StepRangeLen)` の row-vector 確保も
  `_array_undef_from_dims(T, (1, n))` に寄せ、直接
  `Array{T}(undef, 1, n)` に戻らない形にした。
- shaped collect materialization の concrete element-type allocation も
  `iterators.jl` 側で `_array_undef_from_dims` 経由に寄せ、2D
  `collect_similar(::Array, ::Generator)` が shared Array helper dispatch
  を使う対象型を広げた。`Real` と `Any` も dedicated helper に寄せ、
  `Type{Any}` exact method が generic `Type{T}` より優先されるようにした
  (Issue #4574)。
- generic `_array_for_inner_shape(::Type{T}, dims)` の rank 別 direct
  `Array{T}(undef, ...)` fallback を削除し、全 rank を
  `_array_undef_from_dims(T, dims)` に統一した。`Type{Any}` の非 exact
  singleton match は `Type{T}` より弱くし、`Symbol` などの runtime type
  object が generic helper で `Any` allocation に落ちないようにした
  (Issue #4577)。
- compiler の `Array{T}(undef, dims...)` / tuple-dims lowering を
  `_array_undef_from_dims(T, dims_tuple)` call に寄せ、direct
  `AllocUndef*` instruction boundary を縮小した。callable runtime
  dispatch では `DataType` 値を `Type{T}` singleton として扱うため、
  generic `Array{T}(undef, (2,))` も Pure Julia helper dispatch に進む
  (Issue #4580)。
- Any-typed argument を含む `print` / `println` は builtin I/O path へ
  route し、static dispatch が `Nothing` singleton fallback を選んで
  compile-time coercion error になる regression を修正した (Issue #4580)。
- `ArrayPop` が Pure Julia Array wrapper (`StructRef`) を受けた場合、
  1D wrapper の `_mem` / `_size` を更新して末尾要素を返す path を追加した。
  `resize!` shrink と `copy!` の vector resize が `ArrayPop: expected Array
  or Set, got "StructRef"` で失敗する regression を修正した (Issue #4570)。
- 3D Array wrapper の colon slicing methods を追加し、
  `A[1, :, :]` / `A[:, 2, :]` / `A[:, :, 1]` / `A[:, :, :]` が
  `similar(a, dims)` allocation と scalar `getindex` / `setindex!` で
  materialize されるようにした (Issue #4571)。
- `BuiltinId::Similar` の cached-bytecode compatibility fallback は、
  Array / Memory だけでなく全 receiver type で `similar` / `Base.similar`
  method table を先に引き、見つからない場合のみ direct Rust allocation
  fallback に進むようにした。
- VM-native range collect bridge の `Vector{T}(undef, n)` allocation を
  `_array_undef_from_dims(T, (n,))` に寄せ、UnitRange / StepRange /
  LinRange / StepRangeLen の materialization が shared Array helper
  allocation を使うようにした。
- tuple element の Array wrapper が `setindex!` で backing `Memory` に
  書く path を `IndexStore` に追加し、`collect(enumerate(...))` の
  `Vector{Tuple{Int64,Int64}}` materialization regression を修正した
  (Issue #4578)。
- native collect compatibility fallback が Pure Julia Array wrapper
  `StructRef` を受けた場合、`_mem` / `_size` から fresh Array copy を
  materialize するようにし、nested HOF chain の
  `collect: unsupported iterator type Array{Int64}` regression を修正した
  (Issue #4579)。
- runtime dispatch の `Array{T}` pattern を次元未束縛 Array として扱い、
  `Vector{T}` / `Matrix{T}` / `Array{T,N}` 実引数を invariant element match
  で受けられるようにした。`collect(x::Any)` から
  `collect(::Array{Int64})` user method が選ばれ、`Array{Real}` は
  `Vector{Float64}` に誤 dispatch しない (Issue #4581)。
- parser が matrix row 内の `[:x :y]` を `(:x):y` range と誤読していた
  境界を修正し、`Matrix{Symbol}` literal と
  `collect_similar([:a], Generator(identity, Matrix{Symbol}))` を
  upstream と同じ shape/value で materialize できるようにした
  (Issue #4576)。
- #4579 の Array wrapper collect fallback 修正により、3D Array source の
  `collect_similar` も通るようになったため、Issue #4573 の再現を
  `generator_trait_collect_similar_4052` に追加した。
- fixture `array_zeros_ones_fill_tuple_dims_4018` を追加し、上流 Julia と
  同じ `Matrix{Int64}` / `Matrix{Complex{Float64}}` / 3D fill shape に加え、
  static/generic `Array{T}(undef, dims)` helper lowering を検証する。
- fixture `array_range_adjoint_similar_allocation_4018` を追加し、
  `StepRangeLen` の adjoint row allocation behavior を検証する。
- fixture `generator_trait_collect_similar_4052` を拡張し、Bool / Char /
  Symbol / String / Float32 / Complex{Float64} / Any / 3D Array source の
  shaped collect result を検証する。Float32 payload は `===` まで
  検証する。

### Float16/Float32/Bool identity parity ✅ (Issues #4582, #4583, #4584)

- `BuiltinId::Egal` に Float16 / Float32 の bit identity arm と Bool の
  value identity arm を追加し、narrow float / Bool の `===` を upstream
  Julia と合わせた。
- `isequal` の Float16 / Float32 arm と mixed narrow-float comparisons も
  Float64 と同じ NaN-aware signed-zero semantics に寄せ、
  `Float32(-0.0)` / `Float16(-0.0)` と `0.0` の区別を保存するようにした。
- fixture `types_float_identity_4582` を追加し、Issues #4582 / #4583 /
  #4584 の regression を検証する。

### Small integer Array allocation and sizeof parity ✅ (Issues #4018, #4585)

- `_array_undef_from_dims(::Type{Int8/Int16/Int32/UInt8/UInt16/UInt32/UInt64}, dims)`
  を追加し、small integer typed Array allocation を `Vector{Real}` ではなく
  `Vector{T}` として materialize する。
- `sizeof(::Array)` は Pure Julia Array wrapper の `_mem` / `_size` も
  payload size として評価し、Memory-backed wrapper arrays の byte count を
  upstream Julia と合わせる。
- `types_sizeof_basic` に small signed/unsigned integer vector の regression
  coverage を追加した。

### vm/exec/array_basic legacy_array_value_into delegation ✅ (Issue #3908)

- `vm/exec/array_basic.rs` の 4 つの helper のうち、
  `legacy_array_value_into(Value) -> Option<ArrayRef>` と
  `try_consume_array_value(Value) -> Result<ArrayRef, Value>` は array
  variant 上での挙動が同一 (`Option` vs `Result` の違いのみ)。

### typed array comprehension parsing/lowering ✅ (Issue #4462)

- Added parser support for `T[expr for var in iter]` typed comprehensions.
- Lowering now applies the requested type constructor to the comprehension body,
  matching Julia's element conversion behavior without adding VM intrinsics.
- Added parser coverage and the `comprehension_typed_array_4462` fixture.

### Symbol array comprehension element type preservation ✅ (Issue #4463)

- Array literal and comprehension inference now carries `Symbol` element types
  through compiler collection paths.
- Comprehension emission treats Symbol results as Any-backed scalar values
  instead of forcing a floating-point conversion.
- Added the `comprehension_symbol_array_4463` fixture.

### collect-backed vector fields compare with == ✅ (Issue #4446)

- Array-like `==` / `!=` involving statically `Any` operands now routes through
  the VM `isequal` bridge when either side is known array-like by value or
  Julia type.
- This preserves vector equality for values stored in struct fields after
  `collect(1:n)`.
- Added the `struct_field_collect_vector_eq_4446` fixture.

### Plots x/function series methods and include-aware package cache ✅ (Issue #4452)

- Added `plot`, `plot!`, `scatter`, and `scatter!` overloads for `(x,
  f::Function)` in bundled `Plots`, mapping `f` across `x` for the series y
  data.
- Package module cache hashes now include recursively loaded literal
  `include("...")` content, preventing stale cached Plots method tables after
  edits to included files.
- Added loader unit coverage and the `packages_plots_function_xy_4452` fixture.

### iteration.rs destructure helpers (round 2) ✅ (Issue #3908)

- Added a file-local
  `legacy_array_value_ref(&Value) -> Option<&ArrayRef>` helper in
  `vm/type_ops/iteration.rs`. Routed all eight remaining destructure-side
  `Value::Array` sites through it (continuing PR #4468 which routed the
  construction sites through `array_value`): the three matrix shape probes
  (`matrix_array_dims_2d`, `extract_matrix_row_1based`,
  `extract_matrix_column_1based`), the `_mem::Array` linear getter in
  `iterate_first_array_wrapper_fields`, the `iterate_first` / `iterate_next`
  / `collect_iterator` Array match arms, and the `collect_iterator_values`
  materialize-then-unwrap. `let-else` sites use
  `let Some(arr) = legacy_array_value_ref(matrix) else { ... }`; match arms
  use guarded `_ if legacy_array_value_ref(coll).is_some() => { ... }`
  patterns, all under existing `_ =>` fallback arms.
- Lowered the `subset_julia_vm/src/vm/type_ops/iteration.rs` allowlist
  ceiling from 9 to 4 in `scripts/check_value_array_allowlist.sh`
  (delta -5). The four remaining matches are the two helper bodies
  (`array_value` and `legacy_array_value_ref`) plus their doc comments.
- `iteration::`, `hof::`, `range::`, `generator::`, and `collections::`
  fixture tests continue to pass through the helper.

  String-indexing Array-of-indices arm, and the top-level slicing target
  unwrap) through a new file-local
  `legacy_array_value_ref(&Value) -> Option<&ArrayRef>` helper. The first
  three sites sit inside `match` blocks with wildcard fallbacks, so guarded
  `_ if legacy_array_value_ref(...).is_some() => { ... }` arms preserve
  exhaustiveness. The target unwrap switched to
  `if let Some(arr_ref) = legacy_array_value_ref(&target) { arr_ref.clone() }
  else { ... }` so the `getindex` dispatch fallback in the `else` branch
  still runs unchanged.
- Routed the three slicing result re-pushes (1D `slice_indices.len() == 1`,
  2D matrix slice, and the generic N-D fallback) through a new
  `array_value(ArrayValue) -> Value` helper, consolidating the
  `Value::Array(new_array_ref(result_arr))` construction.
- Lowered the file's `Value::Array` allowlist ceiling from 7 to 2 in
  `scripts/check_value_array_allowlist.sh` (reduction of 5). The two
  remaining matches are the helper bodies (`legacy_array_value_ref` and
  `array_value`).
- Existing array indexing / slicing / string slicing fixtures continue to
  pass through the routed dispatch.
