### Bool return-type annotation preserves Bool static dispatch ✅ (Issue #4376)

- `function f()::Bool; true; end; println(f())` が `1` を出力する（`true` ではなく）
  バグを修正。`using Primes; println(isprime(17))` が同様に `1` を出力していたのが、
  本問題の現れ。CLI / iOS / Web すべてで再現していた。
- 原因: `subset_julia_vm/src/compile/type_helpers.rs:220` で
  `JuliaType::Bool => ValueType::I64` と型消去していた。これにより `::Bool`
  戻り値アノテーション付きの関数が呼び出し側で静的に `I64` として扱われ、
  `compile/expr/builtin_io.rs` の `println` 経路が `PrintI64NoNewline` を発行。
  ランタイムでは `Value::Bool` が `Instr::ReturnI64` の `preserved_val` で
  保存されているので `typeof` は `Bool` を返すが、印字命令側で `pop_i64` され
  `1`/`0` に縮退していた。
- Fix: `JuliaType::Bool => ValueType::Bool` に変更。`ValueType::Bool` は
  既存の variant で、Bool リテラル (`utils.rs:193`) や比較演算 (`utils.rs:233`)
  の戻り型として使用済み。`compile/stmt.rs:232` の `ValueType::Bool =>
  Instr::ReturnI64` 経路はそのままなので、VM バイトコードは変化しない
  (narrow integer 群と同じ流儀)。
- Regression: `tests/fixtures/bool/return_type_annotation.jl`
  (`bool_return_type_annotation`)。`foo(x::Bool)` / `foo(x::Int64)` の
  multiple dispatch を経由して、Bool アノテーション付き戻り値が Bool 経路に
  乗ることを確認。
- 影響範囲: 全 fixture (124 chunks) と全 lib unit test (1883) が pass。

## 最新対応 (2026-05-23)

### Web build: bundled packages reachable via pipeline ✅ (Issue #4373)

- WebAssembly Playground (`subset_julia_vm_web`) で `using Primes; factor(10)`
  を実行すると `Runtime error: ErrorException: Unknown function: factor` で
  失敗していた問題を修正。CLI / iOS では同コードが成功していた。
- 原因: `subset_julia_vm_web/src/lib.rs::run_from_source_internal` が
  `Lowering::new(source).lower(...)` → `compile_core_program` を直接呼んでおり、
  `pipeline::parse_and_lower` が走らせる `PackageLoader::load_for_usings`
  (`@stdlib:@packages` を解決する経路) を素通りしていた。`compile_core_program`
  内の `stdlib_loader::load_stdlib_modules` は stdlib しか拾わないため、
  `subset_julia_vm/packages/` に同梱された Primes / Plots / Example が IR に
  マージされず、`factor` などの export が解決されないまま VM へ流れていた。
- Fix: WASM エントリポイントを `pipeline::parse_and_lower(source)` に
  切り替え。これにより CLI / iOS と同一の前処理 (prelude マージ → PackageLoader)
  を経由するようになり、同梱パッケージが Web からも利用可能に。
- Regression: `subset_julia_vm_web::tests::test_bundled_primes_factor` /
  `test_bundled_primes_isprime`。

### REPL: suppress struct text when plot SVG artifact attached ✅ (Issue #4369)

- `subset_julia_vm/src/ffi/repl_ffi.rs::repl_session_eval` now returns
  `CREPLResult.value = NULL` whenever `display_artifact.is_some()`, so the
  iOS REPL no longer prints the redundant textual struct form (e.g.
  `<struct ref>` or `Plots.Plot([StructRef(heap_idx=N)], :text)`) on top
  of the rendered chart.
- Non-plot results (`1 + 2` → `3`) still surface their textual value.
- Regression: `ffi::repl_ffi::tests::test_repl_eval_suppresses_value_text_when_plot_artifact_present`
  and `..._keeps_value_text_for_plain_results`.

### Editor tab renders SVG plot artifact ✅ (Issue #4366)

- `CExecutionResult` gains `artifact_mime` / `artifact_data` pointers.
  `compile_and_run_detailed` and `compile_and_run_streaming` now call
  `crate::plotting::try_value_to_artifact(value, vm.get_struct_heap())`
  and attach the SVG via `CExecutionResult::with_artifact`.
- Swift `VMBridge.CExecutionResult` mirrors the new fields; `ExecutionResult`
  carries `plotSVG: String?`, populated by `executeStreaming` / `execute`.
- `ContentView` (Editor tab) keeps `@State plotSVG` and renders
  `PlotPreviewView` (the existing WKWebView used by the REPL) inline above
  the text log when present. Cleared on `Run` / `Clear`.
- Regression: `ffi::detailed::tests::test_compile_and_run_detailed_attaches_plot_artifact`
  drives the raw FFI with `using Plots; plot(sin)` and asserts the artifact
  pointers are non-null and contain valid SVG. A negative test
  (`..._no_artifact_for_plain_value`) confirms the pointers stay null for
  non-plot return values.

### Plots: scatter shorthand ✅ (Issue #4367)

- `packages/Plots/src/types.jl::Series` gains a `seriestype` field (default
  `:line` via inner constructor for backward-compat with `Series(x, y, label)`).
- `packages/Plots/src/api.jl` adds `scatter(x, y)`, `scatter(y::Vector)`,
  `scatter(f::Function)` mirroring `plot` but tagging series with
  `:scatter`. Matches the shorthand in
  `extern/Plots.jl/PlotsBase/src/shorthands.jl` (`@shorthands scatter` ≡
  `plot(...; seriestype = :scatter)`).
- `Plots.jl` now exports `plot, scatter, Plot, Series` only — the
  non-upstream `text_plot` / `svg_plot` exports (and their backing files
  `text.jl`, `svg.jl`, `backends/GRBackend.jl`) are removed since they
  don't exist in upstream Plots.jl. The auto-display path is independent
  (Rust `src/plotting/svg.rs`).
- `src/plotting/svg.rs::extract_series` reads `Series.seriestype` from
  `s.values[3]` and renders `<circle>` markers when `:scatter`, otherwise
  the existing polyline `<path>` (line series).
- Regression: `test_repl_scatter_renders_circles` asserts the SVG for
  `scatter(sin)` contains `<circle` and no `<path>`. New fixture
  `packages_plots_scatter` covers the Julia surface.

### Plots.plot(f::Function) default xlims = (-5, 5) ✅ (Issue #4364)

- `subset_julia_vm/packages/Plots/src/api.jl::plot(f::Function)` now samples
  100 uniform points over `[-5.0, 5.0]` instead of the integer grid
  `1:100`, matching the upstream Plots.jl default
  (`extern/Plots.jl/RecipesPipeline/src/user_recipe.jl:219-233` falls back to
  `xmin, xmax = -5, 5` via `PlotUtils.tryrange` when no `xlims` is set).
- `plot(sin)` in the iOS REPL now renders a single smooth sin wave over
  `[-5, 5]` instead of ~15.9 high-frequency cycles sampled at integer
  arguments.
- Regression: `plots_function_sin.jl` asserts the x range hits the
  upstream endpoints and that `y[1] ≈ sin(-5)`, `y[end] ≈ sin(5)`.

### Plots auto-SVG artifact across qualified names ✅ (Issue #4361)

- `subset_julia_vm/src/plotting/svg.rs` now matches both the bare
  `Plot`/`Series` names and the module-qualified `Plots.Plot`/`Plots.Series`
  forms that `using Plots` produces in `StructInstance::struct_name`.
- The REPL auto-display path (`REPLSession::eval` →
  `try_value_to_artifact`) consequently attaches an `image/svg+xml`
  `display_artifact` for `plot(sin)` instead of letting the unresolved
  `Value::StructRef` leak to `format_value` and render as `<struct ref>` in
  the iOS REPL.
- Regression: `test_repl_plot_returns_svg_artifact` in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/repl/tests.rs` exercises
  `using Plots; plot(sin)` end-to-end and asserts the SVG artifact.

### Top-level docstring drop in lowering ✅ (Issue #4357)

- `lower_source_file` / `lower_module_definition` skip a top-level
  `StringLiteral` whose next non-comment sibling is a definition, so
  docstrings no longer become value-producing `main` statements.
- `using LinearAlgebra` (and other inputs whose user `main` block is empty,
  like bare `struct` definitions) now returns `nothing` in the REPL instead
  of leaking the asyncmap docstring from the tail of `Base`.
- Regression: `test_repl_using_returns_nothing` in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/repl/tests.rs`.

### String/Char multiplication Union vararg dispatch parity ✅ (Issues #3671/#4350)

- `Base.:*` now uses the upstream-shaped
  `Union{AbstractChar, AbstractString}` vararg method signature for
  string/char concatenation.
- `hasmethod(*, Tuple{String, Char, String})` and representative n-ary
  `String`/`Char` multiplication now match upstream Julia, including the
  existing slice-concat runtime dispatch path.

## 最新対応 (2026-05-22)

### isvalid dispatch-first routing ✅ (Issue #4352)

- `isvalid` is now classified as a dispatch-first public Base fallback and no
  longer has an early call-lowering route that bypasses Pure Julia methods.

### Peephole compare-jump fusion boundary guard ✅ (Issue #4351)

- Compare+jump fusion now respects branch-target boundaries, preserving
  short-circuit OR control flow and preventing stack underflow.

### String/Char multiplication dispatch parity ✅ (Issues #3671/#4350)

- Binary `String` / `Char` multiplication now reaches Pure Julia string
  concatenation dispatch even when operands come from slice indexing.

### Narrow integer fused slot preservation ✅ (Issue #4349)

- Fused VM slot arithmetic now preserves narrow signed/unsigned integer
  runtime values instead of requiring `I64` in the slot.
- `numeric_typed_param_int_widths` and the Rational Int32 recurrence path pass
  without disabling the fused VM fast path.

### Membership alias dispatch-first `in` delegation ✅ (Issue #3911)

- `∉`, `∋`, and `∌` now delegate to dispatch-first `in` at the call site when
  there is no specific user method for the alias itself.
- User `Base.in(::AliasNeedle3911, ::AliasBox3911)` extensions now win for
  `∈`/`∋`/`∉`/`∌` aliases while tuple membership still uses the retained VM
  fallback.

### Module struct DataType identity normalization ✅ (Issue #4348)

- `typeof(s) === MyStruct{Int64}` now succeeds when `s` is a
  module-qualified imported struct instance, matching upstream Julia for
  `module_struct_isa`.

### IOBuffer/empty Tuple show runtime dispatch ✅ (Issue #4347)

- `show(buf, ())` now reaches `show(::IO, ::Tuple)` through runtime typed
  dispatch, matching upstream Julia for the empty tuple display path.
- Runtime typed dispatch now considers ordinary subtype fallback such as
  `IOBuffer <: IO` and `Tuple{} <: Tuple`.

### Pair expression construction and display ✅ (Issue #4346)

- `:a => 1` now constructs a `Pair` struct when available and displays as
  `:a => 1`.

### gcdx integer recurrence ✅ (Issue #4345)

- `gcdx` keeps the integer recurrence integral by using `div(old_r, r)`.

### Runtime varargs specialization binding ✅ (Issue #4344)

- Runtime specialization now binds varargs collector parameters as `Tuple`.

### @kwdef default constructor fallback ✅ (Issue #4343)

- Exact field-layout mutable struct construction now supports `@kwdef`
  generated default constructor paths.

### iOS Random Simulation floor-name compatibility ✅ (Issue #4342)

- The iOS Random/Dice Simulation sample uses `integer_floor` instead of
  shadowing Base `floor`.
- `ios_samples_tests chunk_002` passes again.

### Complex function-value trig return typing ✅ (Issue #4341)

- `r = tan(z::Complex{Float64})` now keeps the Complex result on an Any/struct
  storage path instead of emitting `StoreF64`.
- Function-value intrinsic fallback for primitive math functions now declines
  Complex arguments so Pure Julia Complex overloads handle them.
- `complex_trig` passes again.

### Complex reshape element-type preservation ✅ (Issue #4340)

- `reshape(Vector{Complex{Float64}}(undef, 4), 2, 2)` now preserves
  `Matrix{Complex{Float64}}` / `Complex{Float64}` through the Pure Julia Array
  wrapper projection path.
- The iOS Mandelbrot 2D broadcast sample no longer writes Complex values into a
  destination reported as `Matrix{Float64}`.

### BigInt/BigFloat abstract numeric VM return preservation ✅ (Issue #4337)

- Preserved `BigInt` / `BigFloat` through constructor inference, abstract
  numeric parameter loads, dynamic binary dispatch, and caller result storage.
- `half_number(x::Number, y::Number) = x / y` now returns `BigFloat` for
  `big(6.0), big(2.0)`, matching upstream Julia.
- `sign(::BigInt)` now returns `BigInt`, closing the representative BigInt
  type-preservation fixture.

### Broadcast logical indexing inference ✅ (Issue #4338)

- Materialized broadcast comparisons now infer Boolean array results.
- Logical indexing with broadcast masks no longer enters the scalar Int64 index
  path when the mask is a Julia Array wrapper.

### Matrix rotation literal overload parity ✅ (Issue #4336)

- Added VM-supported Matrix overloads for `rotl90`, `rotr90`, and `rot180` in
  Pure Julia Base.
- Matrix literal rank inference can now expose those matrix-specific rotation
  routes instead of falling through missing method coverage.

### REPL Pure Julia Array wrapper persistence ✅ (Issue #4335)

- REPL persistence now converts Pure Julia `Array{T}` wrapper structs backed by
  Memory or native Array storage into shaped array literals for reinjection.
- This keeps `reshape` results addressable in later REPL evaluations.

### Reshape BuiltinOp reachability audit fix ✅ (Issue #4334)

- Restored `reshape` to the retained Base fallback reachability audit input
  list so `BuiltinOp::Reshape` is no longer reported as dead.
- The runtime route remains dispatch-first and still falls back to the VM
  reshape primitive only when no user/Pure Julia method matches.

### LinearAlgebra matrix literal direct dispatch parity ✅ (Issue #4020)

- `ArrayLiteral` type inference now uses lowering shape metadata to keep
  vectors as `Vector{T}` and matrix literals as `Matrix{T}`.
- Direct calls on matrix literal locals now select imported/user
  `LinearAlgebra` methods for `Matrix{Float64}` before the retained VM/native
  fallback, matching upstream Julia.
- Added `linalg_matrix_literal_direct_dispatch_4020` for `mul!`, `ldiv!`,
  `rdiv!`, `tr`, `opnorm`, and `diag`.

### LinearAlgebra backslash dispatch-first routing ✅ (Issue #4020)

- `A \ b` now uses runtime typed dispatch when user `Base.:\` extension
  methods exist, then falls back to the retained VM `Ldiv` kernel only when no
  runtime method matches.
- The representative `\(A::Matrix{Float64}, b::Vector{Float64})` user method
  now wins for direct calls and for `A::Any, b::Any` wrapper calls, matching
  upstream Julia.
- LinearAlgebra VM kernels now project the Pure Julia `Array` wrapper returned
  by `reshape` into a temporary `ArrayValue`, fixing the `rank(reshape(...))`
  path that reaches `svd`.
- Added `linalg_ldiv_dispatch_first_4020`.

### Membership operator runtime fallback dispatch parity ✅ (Issue #4276)

- `in(x, collection)` now uses runtime typed dispatch when user extension
  methods exist, then falls back to the retained VM membership path only when
  no runtime method matches.
- Binary membership aliases `∈`, `∉`, `∋`, and `∌` now lower to their public
  callable names instead of directly rewriting to `in` / `!in`, so user methods
  on those names can win like upstream Julia.
- This keeps `in(::Int64, ::Vector{Int64})` extensions from matching
  `Vector{Any}`, matching upstream Julia while preserving membership checks for
  `Any[...]`.
- Added `dispatch_in_user_method_4276` for direct `in`, operator `∈` / `∉` /
  `∋` / `∌`, and `Any`-typed receiver paths.

### Array `push!` runtime fallback dispatch parity ✅ (Issue #4276)

- `push!`, `pop!`, `pushfirst!`, `popfirst!`, `insert!`, and `deleteat!` now
  use runtime typed dispatch when user extension methods exist, then fall back
  to the retained VM array mutation path only when no runtime method matches.
- `pop!` and `popfirst!` keep the primitive fallback result shape internal:
  the modified array is discarded from the call result and only the popped value
  is returned.
- This keeps `Vector{Int64}` mutation extensions from matching `Vector{Any}`,
  matching upstream Julia while preserving in-place mutation for `Any[...]`.
- Extended `dispatch_collection_mutation_user_method_4276` to cover direct and
  `Any`-typed receiver calls for the `Vector{Any}` negative-dispatch case.

### LinearAlgebra matrix dispatch lattice/order parity ✅ (Issue #4020)

- `inv` now consults imported/user `LinearAlgebra.inv` methods before the
  retained VM kernel, matching upstream Julia for both `inv(A)` and
  `LinearAlgebra.inv(A)`.
- Module-qualified direct builtin routes for `svd`, `qr`, `eigen`, `eigvals`,
  `cholesky`, and `cond` now use method dispatch when user methods exist,
  avoiding Rust-kernel bypass for imported LinearAlgebra extensions.
- Added `linalg_direct_builtin_dispatch_first_4020`, covering imported user
  methods for the retained direct LinearAlgebra builtin routes.
- Fixed runtime array subtype parity so `Matrix{T}` no longer matches
  `AbstractVector` while `Array{T,1}` / `Array{T,2}` keep the expected
  `AbstractVector` / `AbstractMatrix` relationships.
- Preserved `AbstractVector` and `AbstractMatrix` in JuliaType parsing instead
  of erasing both to `AbstractArray`, which keeps method signatures distinct
  through runtime dispatch.
- Runtime binary dispatch candidates now include array-shaped stdlib
  `AbstractUser` methods, allowing `*(AbstractMatrix, AbstractMatrix)` to be
  selected for matrix-matrix products such as `C * nullspace(C)`.
- Loaded stdlib module functions now compile before user top-level methods, so
  user `Base.:*` methods written after `using LinearAlgebra` win over
  same-signature stdlib methods like upstream Julia.
- Runtime type names for homogeneous struct arrays now preserve the element
  struct name, allowing `Vector{Complex{Float64}}` methods to dispatch before
  generic array fallbacks.
- Added `linalg_matmul_matrix_matrix_abstract_dispatch_4020` and verified the
  full `linalg::` fixture category.

### Array map! vararg source dispatch ✅ (Issue #4019)

### VM call-frame stack boundary restoration ✅ (Issue #4317)

### Dict delete! user-method dispatch fallback parity ✅ (Issue #4276)

### Collection mutation user-method dispatch fallback parity ✅ (Issue #4276)

### Integer StepRange collect Base dispatch ✅ (Issue #4266)

### Numeric constructor arity MethodError parity ✅ (Issue #4316)

- Direct primitive numeric constructor calls with extra positional arguments now

- `Base.Generator(Float64, Int64[], [10, 20])` now preserves Julia's empty
  unsupported-call eltype as `Vector{Union{}}`.

### LinearAlgebra bounded Matrix dispatch parity ✅ (Issue #4020)

- `Matrix{<:Integer}` annotations lower to a bounded parametric Matrix type
  and keep that bound through compile-time and runtime dispatch scoring.
- MethodTable dispatch now lets the bounded Matrix method beat `Any` for
  `Matrix{Int64}`, while rejecting `Matrix{Float64}`.
- VM `CallDynamic` no longer uses same-family fallback for parametric misses,
  so runtime `Any` paths also respect the element bound.
- Added `linalg_det_lu_matrix_bound_dispatch_4020` and verified it against
  upstream Julia, direct sjulia, and the full `linalg::` fixture category.

## 最新対応 (2026-05-21)

### LinearAlgebra dispatch-first fallback reduction ✅ (Issue #4020)

- `det` and `lu` are now classified as `DispatchFirst` in the public Base route
  registry.
- User/Pure Julia methods for `det(::Array)` and `lu(::Array)` are selected
  before the retained Rust LinearAlgebra fallback for both unqualified calls
  and `LinearAlgebra.det` / `LinearAlgebra.lu`.
- Verified against upstream Julia, direct sjulia fixtures, the full `linalg::`
  fixture category, and iOS simulator builds.

### Diagonal `size(D, dim)` VM parity ✅ (Issue #4314)

- `Base.size(D::Diagonal, dim::Int)` now uses equivalent `if` / `elseif`
  control flow that avoids the VM's current short-circuit-condition bug.
- Added `linalg_size_diagonal_dim_4314` to pin `size(D, 1)` and `size(D, 2)`.
- Verified the targeted fixture, existing Diagonal fixture, full `linalg::`
  category, Rust iOS simulator target, and Xcode simulator app build.

### callable local callee dispatch ✅ (Issue #4313)

- Function-position local bindings now compile to `CallFunctionVariable`
  through the runtime callable-value path before any global method lookup.
- `Expr::FunctionRef` participates in legacy local type collection as
  `ValueType::Function`, so function-valued ternaries no longer inherit the
  integer fallback type.
- Verified with upstream Julia and the `hof::` fixture category, including
  `hof_edge_cases`.

### tuple equality numeric parity ✅ (Issue #4312)

- Tuple equality now delegates to recursive Julia-style value equality instead
  of comparing tuple element debug strings.
- Representative HOF tuple results now match upstream Julia when integer and
  floating-point elements compare equal.
- Verified with `memory_first_results.jl` and the full `hof::` fixture category.

### `resize!(Vector{Bool})` default preservation ✅ (Issue #4311)

- `resize!` growth for Bool and Int64 arrays now pushes branch-local defaults
  directly, avoiding a widened joined `default` binding.
- `resize!(Bool[], n)` no longer attempts to push `0.0` into a Bool array.
- Verified against upstream Julia and the full `array::` fixture category.

### VM direct call/frame fast path ✅ (Issue #4303)

- Added a fast path for inferred direct `Call` / `CallInbounds` bytecode when
  the callee has fixed positional parameters and does not need kwargs, varargs,
  or runtime type-parameter binding.
- The fast path avoids cloning `FunctionInfo`, allocating/reversing an argument
  vector, and cloning argument values while binding parameters into local slots.
- It still pushes a normal VM frame and return IP, preserving the interpreter
  return path, try/catch handler cleanup, recursion behavior, cancellation
  checks, and iOS app VM embedding compatibility.
- Added `benchmarks/vm_direct_calls.jl` for repeated small direct-call
  measurement. On the `50000`-call workload, sjulia VM median improved from
  `2.72s` to `2.61s`; profiler event `CallDirectFastHit` recorded `50002`
  hits.
- On `benchmarks/vm_mandelbrot.jl` (`120x80x60`), `CallDirectFastHit` recorded
  `9602` hits and sjulia VM median measured `2.82s`.
- Verified the iOS simulator app still builds after the VM call path change.

### VM dynamic binary primitive fast path ✅ (Issue #4306)

- Added a fast path inside `CallDynamicBinaryBoth` for the hot
  `Float64`/`Float64` and `Int64`/`Int64` primitive fallback cases.
- These primitive pairs already preempt shared resolver dispatch under the
  existing Julia-compatibility policy, so the VM now avoids type-name string
  construction, resolver setup, and candidate scanning before executing the
  primitive operation.
- Added profiling events for dynamic binary dispatch behavior:
  `BinaryBothPrimitiveFastHit`, `BinaryBothPrimitiveFastMiss`,
  `BinaryBothResolverLookup`, `BinaryBothResolverMatch`, and
  `BinaryBothResolverMiss`.
- On `benchmarks/vm_mandelbrot.jl` (`120x80x60`, `RUNS=5`), sjulia VM median
  improved to `2.87s`; `BinaryBothPrimitiveFastHit` recorded `498795` hits.
- Verified the iOS simulator app still builds after the VM dispatch changes.

### VM Any-path return/profiler diagnostics ✅ (Issue #4305)

- Return-type-annotated functions that compile their final `convert(T, value)`
  expression as `Any` can now still emit primitive return opcodes for declared
  primitive returns (`ReturnI64`, `ReturnF64`, `ReturnF32`, `ReturnF16`).
- This removes an avoidable boxed/`Any` return path without changing Julia's
  annotation semantics: the lowering still inserts `convert(T, value)`, and the
  VM typed return validates the converted stack value.
- The VM profiler now splits `CallDynamicBinaryBoth` by fallback intrinsic and
  candidate count, exposing remaining Any-path hot spots in Mandelbrot as
  `CallDynamicBinaryBoth::MulFloat/14` and `CallDynamicBinaryBoth::AddFloat/11`.
- The Mandelbrot wall time did not materially improve in this slice because the
  dominant remaining Any path is inside binary expression compilation, not the
  annotated return boundary.
- Verified the iOS simulator app still builds after the VM/compiler changes.

### typed VM numeric binary bytecode ✅ (Issue #4302)

- Primitive `Int64` / `Float64` binary operations with proven operand types now
  emit existing typed VM bytecode (`AddI64`, `SubI64`, `MulI64`, `ModI64`,
  `AddF64`, `SubF64`, `MulF64`, `DivF64`, and typed comparisons) instead of
  routing through `CallIntrinsic`.
- `Base.:+` / builtin-operator compilation uses the same typed-instruction
  mapping, while unsupported or semantic-sensitive operations such as integer
  division and dynamic modulo remain on the existing fallback paths.
- Direct and fused `Int64` arithmetic now uses wrapping semantics to match
  upstream Julia's unboxed `add_int` / `sub_int` / `mul_int` behavior.
- The VM profiler now splits remaining `CallIntrinsic` entries by intrinsic
  kind, making future hot spots easier to assign.
- Verified with VM Mandelbrot and local-slot benchmarks plus iOS simulator app
  build. On the small Mandelbrot workload, `CallIntrinsic` disappeared from
  the top instruction profile and hot arithmetic now appears as typed VM ops.

### typed VM local slot load/store fast paths ✅ (Issue #4304)

- Added slotized typed local instructions for inferred `Int64`, `Float64`, and
  `Bool` bindings: `LoadSlotI64` / `StoreSlotI64`, `LoadSlotF64` /
  `StoreSlotF64`, and `LoadSlotBool` / `StoreSlotBool`.
- `vm/slot.rs` now preserves typed numeric and Bool local loads/stores during
  slotization instead of rewriting all local access to generic `LoadSlot` /
  `StoreSlot`.
- Generic `LoadSlot` / `StoreSlot` remains the fallback for `Any`, unstable
  bindings, captured/generic values, and non-typed storage.
- Added `benchmarks/vm_local_slots.jl` to isolate scalar local load/store
  pressure and documented how to profile it with `SJULIA_VM_PROFILE=1`.
- Verified the iOS simulator app still builds after the VM instruction changes.

### iOS REPL plotSVG initializer build fix ✅ (Issue #4307)

  `REPLSessionManager`.
- Verified the SwiftUI app builds for the iOS simulator target with

### `Tuple{}` type-object equality parity ✅ (Issue #4300)

- Kept `Tuple{}` as the concrete empty tuple type (`TupleOf([])`) instead of
  canonicalizing it to the abstract `Tuple` type object.
- This makes `typeof(()) == Tuple{}` and `typeof(()) === Tuple{}` match
  upstream Julia while preserving bare `Tuple` as the abstract tuple family.
- Extended the #4268 value-parameter fixture with `Val{()}()` so empty tuple
  value parameters also check the corrected type-object equality path.

### Keyword default expression preservation ✅ (Issue #4297)

- Extended kwarg default evaluation to recognize simple quoted-symbol defaults
  lowered as `QuoteLiteral(SymbolNew("name"))`.
- `KwParamInfo.default` now stores `Value::Symbol(...)` and
  `KwParamInfo.ty` records `ValueType::Symbol` for defaults like
  `debuginfo=:default`.
- Bool kwarg defaults now store `Value::Bool` / `ValueType::Bool` instead of
  the older `Int64` representation.
- `KwParamInfo` now retains optional default IR, and omitted keyword binding
  evaluates supported default expressions left-to-right in the callee frame.
- Global-name default expressions fall back to the top-level frame at call time,
  so rebinding a global used by a keyword default is observed by later calls.
- Added `kwargs_symbol_default_4297`, covering omitted Symbol defaults after a
  preceding Bool keyword default and explicit Symbol overrides.
- Added `kwargs_default_expression_order_4297`, covering `x=1+2`,
  `b=a+1`, explicit earlier keyword values, explicit later overrides, and
  call-time global Symbol default lookup.
- Extended the supported default evaluator to simple zero-argument calls, so
  representative defaults such as `x=default_num()+1` and
  `debuginfo=default_sym()` now match upstream Julia.
- Extended the same bounded evaluator to simple positional-argument calls whose
  arguments are literal or already-bound default expressions, covering
  `x=default_arg(41)` and Symbol-preserving identity defaults.
- Extended bounded default evaluation to simple keyword calls, covering
  `x=default_kw(x=41)`, calls whose keyword argument references an earlier
  default, and Symbol-preserving keyword call defaults.
- Seeded the abstract-inference environment with keyword default types
  left-to-right, matching upstream `Base.infer_return_type(f, Tuple{})` for the
  same representative numeric and Symbol default-call cases.

### while-loop exit narrowing for loop-carried state ✅ (Issue #4267)

  `code_lowered`: `:default` is normalized to `:source`, `:source` / `:none`

  field access: `if x isa A; y = x; return y.n; end`.
- Added `type_inference_narrowed_alias_field_4270`, covering
  `Base.infer_return_type`, `Core.Compiler.return_type`, and runtime behavior.

### tfunc metadata completion and `abs_float` reflection ✅ (Issue #4275)

- Migrated production tfunc registrations away from the legacy

### union-split method return joins ✅ (Issue #4287)

- Matched upstream's regular method-match union splitting budget
  (`InferenceParams.max_union_splitting == 4`) separately from sjulia's

- Synchronized newly built `MethodSig`s into the shared `InferenceEngine`, so

### string array transformation type preservation ✅ (Issue #4278)

### heterogeneous generator collect typejoin ✅ (Issue #4279)

- Added generator/comprehension element typejoin handling for heterogeneous
  numeric tuple inputs and ternary generator bodies.
- `collect(x for x in (1, 2.0))`,
  `collect(x for x in (1, 2.0, Int8(3)))`, and

### invoke and invokelatest compatibility ✅ (Issue #4290)

- Added a world-age-free `Base.invokelatest(f, args...; kwargs...) =
  f(args...; kwargs...)` compatibility wrapper for the supported single-world
  runtime.
- Added function-variable keyword/splat call support so the wrapper forwards
  keyword arguments instead of falling back to callee defaults.
- Routed `Core.invokelatest(f, args...)` to the same supported primitive lookup
  as `Base.invokelatest`, covering representative `Core.invokelatest(+, 1, 2)`.
- Added compile-time `invoke(f, Tuple{...}, args...)` dispatch for statically
  named functions and statically known tuple signatures, selecting the method
  for the declared signature instead of the actual argument's most specific
  method.
- Routed `Core.invoke(f, Tuple{...}, args...)` to the same static invoke path.
- Expanded trailing `Tuple{Vararg{T}}` invoke signatures to the call arity, so
  declared-signature vararg dispatch matches upstream representative behavior.
- Added lowering for simple `@invoke f(x::T, ...)` expression/statement forms
  into the existing static `invoke(f, Tuple{T, ...}, x, ...)` path.
- Added static function-alias tracking so `g = f; invoke(g, Tuple{T}, x)`
  selects `f`'s method table with the declared signature.
- Added static DataType-value alias tracking so `sig = Tuple{T}; invoke(f, sig, x)`
  uses the aliased tuple signature for declared-signature dispatch.
- Added positional, vararg, keyword, and positional+keyword coverage in
  `reflection_invokelatest_basic_4290`.
- Added `@invokelatest f(args...; kwargs...)` lowering to the same
  world-age-free `invokelatest(f, args...; kwargs...)` wrapper used by the
  supported direct call surface.
- Added upstream `@invokelatest` property/index forms:
  `@invokelatest x.f`, `@invokelatest x.f = v`, `@invokelatest xs[i]`, and
  `@invokelatest xs[i] = v` now lower to `getproperty` / `setproperty!` /
  `getindex` / `setindex!` calls through `invokelatest`.
- Allowed supported `invoke(f, Tuple{...}, args...; kwargs...)` calls to use
  the declared-signature method selection path and then issue `CallWithKwargs`.
- Added runtime Function-value support for static-signature `invoke`, so
  `function apply(f, x); invoke(f, Tuple{Number}, x); end` selects the declared
  `Number` method even though `f` is a parameter value.
- Added runtime Tuple-signature support for non-keyword `invoke`, covering both
  `invoke(f, sig, x)` with a statically named function and `invoke(f, sig, x)`
  where `f` is a runtime Function value.
- Added keyword support for runtime Function-value `invoke` with both static and
  runtime Tuple signatures, reusing the normal keyword binding path after
  declared-signature method selection.
- Routed keyword-splat `invoke(...; kw...)` through the same invoke-specific
  declared-signature path, including static named, runtime Function value, and
  runtime Tuple-signature representative cases.
- Expanded `@invoke` compatibility so unannotated positional arguments use
  runtime `typeof(arg)` in the declared Tuple signature, and keyword /
  keyword-splat macro calls forward through the same `invoke` path.
- Added `@invoke` property/index forms from upstream `reflection.jl`:
  `getproperty`, `setproperty!`, `getindex`, and `setindex!` macro syntax now
  lower to declared-signature `invoke` calls.
- Added the upstream `@invoke 420::Integer % Unsigned` operator doctest slice:
  sjulia now lowers infix `%` macro input through the `rem` alias and supports
  the corresponding integer type-conversion remainder method.
- Added single-world compatibility wrappers for `Base.get_world_counter`,
  `Base.tls_world_age`, and `Base.invoke_in_world`, matching representative
  positional, vararg, and keyword call behavior while full world-age semantics
  remain unsupported.
- Added the representative upstream old-world boundary where
  `Base.invoke_in_world(UInt64(0), f, args...)` throws `MethodError` instead of
  silently calling the newest method.
- Accepted representative world-aware reflection calls in the single-world
  model: `hasmethod(...; world=...)`, `Base.return_types(...; world=...)`, and
  positional-world `Core.Compiler.return_type(..., world)`.
- Matched the upstream representative generated-function boundary where
  `hasmethod(f, Tuple{...}; world=typemax(UInt64))` returns `false` instead of
  silently using the current method table.
- Matched the corresponding keyword-name form:
  `hasmethod(f, Tuple{...}, (:kw,); world=typemax(UInt64))` raises the
  upstream generated-function reflection error.
- Added representative `@world` lowering for identifier and dotted global
  function bindings, evaluating the supplied world expression and returning a
  callable Function value in the current single-world runtime.
- Added parenthesized callable-expression lowering so upstream-style
  `(@world length Base.get_world_counter())(xs)` can call the macro result.

### hasmethod keyword-name filtering ✅ (Issue #4292)

- Extended `hasmethod(f, types)` to accept upstream-compatible

- Used existing `FunctionInfo.kwparams` metadata to distinguish accepted named

  keyword values.
- Preserved positional and keyword splat metadata through known functions,

### runtime Array function-value dispatch ✅ (Issue #4295)

- Fixed runtime string-based subtype checks used by `CallFunctionVariable` so
  `Vector{T}` / `Matrix{T}` / `Array{T,N}` arguments match `Array{T}` method
  signatures.
- This makes callable `getindex` paths such as `f = getindex; f([10, 20], 2)`
  and `Base.invokelatest(getindex, [10, 20], 2)` match upstream representative

### keyword-parameter arrow functions ✅ (Issue #4294)

- Added parser support for semicolon-separated keyword parameter lists in arrow
  function heads, including `(; y=1) -> ...` and `(x; y=1) -> ...`.
- Lowered arrow keyword defaults, `kwargs...`, and positional `args...` into

- Added `kwargs_splat_arrow_kwparams_4294`.

### Val and NTuple value-parameter binding ✅ (Issue #4268)

- Added compile-time marking for `NTuple{N,T}` length parameters so runtime
  method entry binding treats `N` as a value parameter.
- Added VM method argument binding for `NTuple{N,T}` tuple values, binding
  `N` from tuple length and `T` from homogeneous element types.
- Confirmed `Val{3}()` and `Val(3)` both bind `N == 3` and return an `Int64`
  value, matching upstream Julia.
- Extended `Val{N}` runtime method binding to ordinary Float64 value
  parameters, so `f(::Val{N}) where N = N` returns a `Float64` value for
  `Val{1.5}()`.
- Added fixture coverage for non-finite Float64 value parameters
  `Val{Inf}()`, `Val{-Inf}()`, and `Val{NaN}()`, which already bind as
  runtime `Float64` values through the same path.
- Extended the same binding path to simple Char value parameters, so
  `Val{'x'}()` binds `N` as a runtime `Char` value rather than a type object.
- The Char value-parameter binding now uses the same escaped character forms as
  character literals, covering representative `Val{'\n'}`, `Val{'\''}`, and
  `Val{'\\'}` cases, plus hex and Unicode escapes such as `Val{'\x41'}` and
  `Val{'\u03B1'}`.
- Added representative tuple value-parameter binding for `Val{(1, 2)}()`,
  empty/singleton tuple values, mixed `Bool`/`Symbol` tuple values, and nested
  tuple values, so `f(::Val{N}) where N = N` returns runtime `Tuple` values
  for these upstream-compatible cases.
- Extended static `Val` value-parameter handling to constructor-form numeric
  bits values such as `Val{UInt8(1)}()`, `Val{Int32(2)}()`, and
  `Val{Float32(1.5)}()`, preserving the original runtime value type when
  binding `N`.
- Added typed constructor elements inside tuple value parameters, covering
  `Val{(UInt8(1), Int32(2))}()`.
- Fixed `ntuple` index argument preservation so `ntuple(f, 3)` calls `f` with
  `Int64` indices, not widened `Float64` values.
- Allowed non-capturing arrow lambdas lowered as nested function references to
  drive `ntuple(i -> i, N)`, covering the upstream `Val{N}` size example.
- Routed `ntuple` calls with lowered arrow `LetBlock` callables or local
  callable variables through the runtime callable path, preserving closure
  captures for `ntuple(i -> i + a, 3)` and `f = i -> i + a; ntuple(f, 3)`.
- Added abstract-interpretation transfer for `ntuple(f, const_n)`, so the
  captured-arrow representative cases also report `Tuple{Int64, Int64, Int64}`
  through `Base.infer_return_type`.
- Added `types_value_param_binding_4268`.

### global binding reassignment widening ✅ (Issue #4285)

- Global type collection now widens a top-level binding to `Any` when the same
  non-const global is assigned incompatible storage types.
- Functions compiled against such globals now use runtime loads/dispatch instead
  of stale typed global loads.
- Single-assignment const globals remain precise for both runtime execution and
  `Base.infer_return_type` / `Base.return_types` in the representative case.
- Top-level `const` rebinding such as `const x = 1; x = 1.5` now raises an
  invalid-assignment `ErrorException` and preserves the original value.
- Added `type_inference_global_binding_invalidation_4285` and a unit test for
  mixed global reassignment widening.

### full @generated function syntax for type/value-parameter bodies ✅ (Issue #4284)

- Added lowering support for full-form `@generated function ... end`
  definitions and one-line `@generated f(...) = ...` definitions as
  compatibility wrappers.
- Representative generated bodies that directly return already-bound
  type/value parameters now work through the existing method binding path.
- Simple quoted generated bodies such as `:(x + 1)` and `return :(x * x)`
  are unquoted into normal function bodies during lowering, including
  one-line generated definitions.
- Preserved `Type{T}` return snapshots for direct generated returns when the
  supplied signature binds `T` to a concrete type. `Base.return_types`,
  `Base.infer_return_type`, and `Core.Compiler.return_type` now match upstream
  for `Tuple{Int64}`, while abstract signatures such as `Tuple{Integer}` fall
  back to `Any` like upstream generated-function reflection.
- Added `generated_full_syntax_type_params_4284`.

### inference metadata annotation compatibility slice ✅ (Issue #4286)

- Added parser support for module-qualified macro calls in the `Base.@macro ...`
  form and for macro arguments that are long-form function definitions.
- Added lowering pass-through for `@inline`, `@noinline`,
  `@nospecializeinfer`, and `@propagate_inbounds` as no-op compatibility
  wrappers around definitions or expressions.
- Added lowering pass-through for upstream inference metadata annotations
  `Base.@constprop :aggressive function ... end`, `Base.@constprop :none f(x)=...`,
  `Base.@assume_effects :foldable function ... end`,
  `Base.@assume_effects :terminates_locally f(x)=...`, metadata-only statement
  markers, and callsite `Base.@assume_effects :foldable f(x)`.
- Added a representative `@inbounds` / `@boundscheck` runtime slice:
  statement and expression `@inbounds` forms mark the wrapped call context, and
  `@boundscheck` blocks are skipped inside the callee frame for that context.
- Propagated the same `@inbounds` frame context through Lazy AoT
  `CallSpecializeInbounds` so specialized calls suppress lowered
  `@boundscheck` blocks consistently with direct calls.
- Covered long-form `@inline function ... end`, short-form `Base.@inline f(x)=...`,
  and nested `Base.@propagate_inbounds @inline f(x)=...` wrapper combinations.
- Added parser pass-through for parameter-position `@nospecialize x` and
  `@specialize(x)` annotations.
- Added statement-position metadata marker compatibility for
  `@nospecialize x y` and `@specialize`, and fixture coverage for callsite
  `@inline f(x)` / `@noinline (expr)` wrappers.
- Added metadata-only statement marker compatibility for upstream-accepted
  bare `@inline` / `@noinline` statements inside function bodies.
- Added explicit lowered IR retention for statement-position and wrapped-target metadata:
  `Stmt::Meta` now carries supported `@inline` / `@noinline` /
  `@nospecialize` / `@specialize` / `Base.@constprop` /
  `Base.@assume_effects` markers before the wrapped statement while VM/AoT
  execution treats them as no-op.
- Added the first metadata semantic-consumption slice: function-body `@inline` /
  `@noinline` `Stmt::Meta` markers are converted into
  `AotFunction.inline_policy`, and the AoT inliner now honors `@noinline`
  before size/score heuristics and lets non-recursive `@inline` callees cross
  the automatic size limit. `Stmt::Meta` is skipped during AoT statement
  conversion so metadata does not become a synthetic `nothing` statement.
- Moved wrapped top-level definition annotations such as
  `@inline function ... end` / `@noinline function ... end` from sibling
  `Stmt::Meta` blocks into the annotated function body, then hoisted those
  functions into `Program.functions`. This matches upstream `pushmeta!` shape
  closely enough for AoT `inline_policy` conversion to see wrapped definition
  metadata.
- Added a representative callsite inline/noinline semantic slice:
  expression-position `@inline f(x)` / `@noinline f(x)` now lower into retained
  `#__sjulia_inline__` / `#__sjulia_noinline__` wrappers. VM execution treats
  them as no-op wrappers, while AoT IR conversion maps direct static calls to
  per-call `CallStatic.inline_policy`; the AoT inliner uses that callsite policy
  ahead of definition policy and preserves upstream's innermost nested
  annotation precedence.
- Extended that callsite slice across wrapped expressions: `@inline (f(x) + g(x))`
  recursively marks direct static calls inside the AoT expression tree, while
  explicit inner policies such as `@noinline f(x)` keep innermost precedence.
  Outer callsite policy is not propagated into lambda bodies.
- Added `macros_inference_meta_noop_4286`, including a Julia-compatible
  `@boundscheck return 1` / `@inbounds caller()` elision case for direct and
  specialized calls, plus representative `@constprop` / `@assume_effects`
  definition and callsite annotations.

### reflection return type APIs for single-method cases ✅ (Issue #4288)

- Added `Base.return_types(f)` / `Base.return_types(f, types)` using existing
  `methods` reflection and VM `FunctionInfo.return_type` snapshots.
- Added `Base.infer_return_type(f)` / `Base.infer_return_type(f, types)` as a
  typejoin over the returned method snapshots.
- Added `Core.Compiler.return_type(f, Tuple{...})` as an alias to the same
  representative return-type reflection surface.
- Matched upstream's no-method concrete signature result:
  `return_types(...) == Any[]` and `infer_return_type(...) == Union{}`.
- Added minimal `Base.code_lowered` / `Base.code_typed` representative surfaces
  backed by method matches and return type snapshots.
- Added representative `CodeInfo.code` field access for both lowered and typed
  reflection results.
- Matched representative `code_typed` `interp` keyword behavior:
  `interp=nothing` is accepted, while non-interpreter values such as `interp=1`
  raise `Expected AbstractInterpreter`.
- Preserved parametric direct-parameter return snapshots such as
  `f(xs::Vector{Int64}) = xs`, so return reflection reports `Vector{Int64}`
  instead of the erased `Array` boundary.
- Matched upstream method filtering for concrete signature reflection: when
  querying `Tuple{Int64}`, only the most specific applicable method contributes
  to `methods` / `return_types`, while broader abstract queries can still return
  multiple methods.
- Fixed `Type{T}` return binding for `f(::Type{T}) where T = T`, avoiding the
  previous `Type{Type{Int64}}` over-wrap and matching upstream `Type{Int64}`.
- Added representative support for `Core.Compiler.return_type(Tuple{typeof(f), Args...})`
  by expanding signature tuples through `_methods_by_ftype`.
- Added a builtin tfunc reflection slice for `+ :: Tuple{Int64,Int64}`, so
  `Base.return_types`, `Base.infer_return_type`, and `Core.Compiler.return_type`
  report `Int64` for that representative primitive call.
- Extended the builtin reflection slice with representative `string(::Int64)`,
  `length(::Vector{Int64})`, and `getindex(::Vector{Int64}, ::Int64)` results,
  matching upstream return-type reflection for those Base builtin calls.
- Preserved `Vector{T}` reflection snapshots for production inference's
  representative `map` and generator `collect` paths, so `return_types`,
  `infer_return_type`, and `code_typed` report `Vector{Int64}` instead of the
  erased `Array` / `Any` boundary for those cases.
- Preserved anonymous-arrow tuple `map` reflection snapshots by resolving the
  nested callable stored in the lowered `LetBlock`, so `map(x -> x + 1,
  t::Tuple{Int64,Float64})` reports `Tuple{Int64,Float64}`.
- Added small Union argument splitting for reflection method lookup, so
  `Base.return_types(f, Tuple{Union{Int64,String}})` returns the branch method
  snapshots and `infer_return_type` / `Core.Compiler.return_type` preserve
  `Union{Int64,String}` instead of widening to `Any`.
- Preserved `JuliaType::Union` annotations in abstract inference input
  environments, allowing Union-annotated callers to use method-table union
  splitting and report `Union{...}` snapshots.
- Added conditional narrowing for ternary expressions, so `isa` guards over
  small Union parameters refine each branch before joining the result.
- Added `reflection_return_types_basic_4288` and
  `reflection_code_typed_lowered_basic_4288`.

### type-stability report inference provenance ✅ (Issue #4291)

### tuple map type preservation ✅ (Issue #4283)

### closure capture through representative HOF and Generator callables ✅ (Issue #4289)

- Kept local callables on runtime/general collection paths when building
  `map` / `Generator`-style collections, so nested functions preserve captured
  values instead of being lowered to bare function indexes.
- Confirmed `map(f, [1, 2, 3])` and `collect(Base.Generator(f, 1:3))` with
  `f(x) = x + a` match upstream representative `Vector{Int64}` behavior.

  as nested `FunctionDef` values, so `map(x -> x + a, [1, 2, 3])` preserves the
  captured `a` and returns `Vector{Int64}`.
- Reused the nested-arrow lowering path for assigned anonymous functions, so
  `f = x -> x + a; map(f, [1, 2, 3])` also preserves the captured value.
- Collected nested functions embedded in `Expr::ModuleCall` arguments, so direct
  anonymous generator construction `Base.Generator(x -> x + a, 1:3)` registers
  the closure before runtime collection.
- Added coverage for multi-iterator `Base.Generator(f, xs, ys)` and filtered
  generator expressions preserving captured values.
- Routed unfiltered local-callable generator expressions through runtime
  generators so non-empty `collect(f(x) for x in 1:3)` preserves
  `Vector{Int64}`.
- Extended abstract inference / reflection for the same unfiltered generator
  expression path, so `Base.return_types` and `Base.infer_return_type` report
  `Vector{Int64}` rather than `Vector{Any}`.
- Added first-class abstract closure values carrying captured value types.
  `make_adder(a)(x)`, `f = make_adder(offset); f(x)`, returned named nested
  functions, simple composed functions, and returned composed closures now
  report `Int64` through `Base.return_types` / `Base.infer_return_type` for the
  representative upstream-compatible cases.
- Captured local functions with fully typed parameters but free captured values
  are now retained in the reflection-time specialization function table, fixing
  `f(x::Int) = x + a; f(2)` to report `Int64` for the representative
  `Base.return_types` / `Base.infer_return_type` path.
- Reflection APIs now accept runtime closure values directly, so
  `Base.return_types(f, Tuple{Int64})` and `Base.code_typed(f, Tuple{Int64})`
  for `f = x -> x + a` use the captured environment and report `Int64`, matching
  upstream representative behavior.
- Added explicit unsupported diagnostics for upstream opaque closure entry
  points. `Base.Experimental.@opaque ...` now reports opaque closures as
  unsupported under Issue #4289 rather than generic `unknown macro @opaque`,
  and `Core.OpaqueClosure` reports the same unsupported feature rather than
  falling through to `Unknown module: Core`.
- Added a static callable-type alias bridge for Issue #4309. Top-level
  `T = typeof(f)` aliases for known callable values now let `(::T)(...)`
  methods participate in calls to `f`, matching the upstream representative
  closure object method case without relying on runtime JIT/world-age machinery.
- Added collect-style runtime typejoin for filtered local-callable
  generator/comprehension bodies, including all-filtered-out `Vector{Union{}}`.
- Added `closures_hof_capture_4289`.
- Added `closures_callable_closure_method_4309`.

## 最新対応 (2026-05-14)

### Full nextest timeout and reshape Complex storage ✅ (Issues #3972/#3973/#3974)

- Added a process-shared persistent Base cache under `target/sjulia_base_cache_<prelude-hash>.bin` so `cargo nextest` fixture processes no longer recompile Base independently.
- Added a process-shared lowered prelude `Program` cache under `target/sjulia_prelude_program_<prelude-hash>.bin` so fresh test processes do not repeatedly parse/lower Base before compilation.
- Batched generated fixture tests into per-category `chunk_NNN` tests of 16 fixtures each so a full nextest run does not launch one process per fixture while category-targeted workflows still work.
- Set the default nextest profile to 16 test threads and prioritized late heavy integration/iOS chunks so the full release command avoids both over-parallel Base cache restoration and end-of-run stragglers.
- Preserved explicit embedded cache precedence (`SJULIA_BASE_CACHE`) and existing version/hash validation, with stale persistent caches deleted and regenerated automatically.
- Added a lock-file path so the first process writes the cache and concurrent fixture processes wait/read instead of racing into duplicate Base compilations.
- Reconstruct `RuntimeCompileContext` when loading serialized Base cache so warm-cache Lazy AoT still specializes parametric Base methods without bloating the persistent cache payload; this fixes the warm-cache `rational_bigint_mixed_promotion_diagonal` runtime error from #3973.
- Fixed reshaped interleaved Complex mutation so `set_complex` writes through to shared parent storage, matching the storage-sharing expectation from upstream `julia/base/array.jl` reshape behavior and the broadcast materialization path in `julia/base/broadcast.jl`.
- Reduced diagnostic Mandelbrot/randn tests to checksum-style VM executions instead of repeated parse/lower/compile/output probes.
- Validation passed for first-writer/no-cache and warm-cache `generator::`, chunked `generator::` / `rational::`, cold/warm-cache `rational_bigint_mixed_promotion_diagonal`, Mandelbrot grid regressions, reshaped Complex parent-storage unit coverage, and full `timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --release` (`2557/2557 passed`, `1170.167s`).

A follow-up bug found during validation (#3882) fixed AST-like builtin `JuliaType` to `CoreType` projection for DataType flag predicates.
- Added dispatch-first public Base fallback cleanup for `push!`, `pop!`, and `delete!`: user/Pure Julia methods are tried first, while Rust `BuiltinOp` paths remain only as primitive container compatibility fallbacks.
- Fixed implementation bugs found during the work after creating `bug` Issues: `timedwait` `pollint` guard (#3876), covariant `Type{<:Abstract}` dispatch over user structs (#3877), Rational/Integer arithmetic and comparison drift (#3878/#3880), Rational BigInt promotion (#3879), generic `promote` target selection for Bool/Float/Complex/user rules (#3881), and AST-like DataType flag reflection (#3882).

### RuntimeTypeRegistry TypeVar metadata ✅ (Issue #3862)

- `RuntimeTypeObject` now exposes TypeVar `.name`, `.lb`, and `.ub` metadata, moving those reflection lookups out of local `builtins_reflection` pattern matches and into the shared runtime type-object read model.
- The change deliberately keeps `Value::DataType(JuliaType)` as the runtime projection and does not introduce object/layout identity. Current Pure Julia reflection only needs metadata lookup for this path.
- Unit coverage now fixes bounded and unbounded TypeVar metadata in `RuntimeTypeRegistry`, while existing reflection fixtures continue to cover `DataType.parameters`, `UnionAll.var/body`, and public TypeVar property access.
- 検証: `timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --lib vm::type_objects vm::builtins_reflection` 14/14 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --release --test fixture_tests reflection::` 23/23 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass。

### Base-qualified dispatch-first routing ✅ (Issue #3861)

- Added `is_method_dispatch_first_base_function()` as the public Base routing inventory for names that must try Julia method dispatch before Rust fallback routing.
- `Base.foo(...)` calls for migrated public names now forward into the ordinary `compile_call` path first, matching unqualified-call behavior. Rust `BuiltinOp` routes remain available as primitive value and cache-compatibility fallbacks after dispatch misses.
- Added `pure_julia/base_qualified_dispatch_first.jl` to verify `Base.length`, `Base.keys`, `Base.values`, and `Base.pairs` user methods are not shadowed by public-name builtin fallback routes.
- 検証: `julia subset_julia_vm/tests/fixtures/pure_julia/base_qualified_dispatch_first.jl` pass、`timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --lib compile::base_functions compile::expr::call` 3/3 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --release --test fixture_tests pure_julia:: dispatch:: dict:: sets::` 77/77 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass。

### CoreType-backed AoT lattice join ✅ (Issue #3860)

- AoT `StaticType` now has a lossy projection from `CoreType` plus `core_typejoin()`, so AoT merge-point joins can use `CoreType::typejoin()` for shapes that still have a backend/codegen representation.
- `TypeInferenceEngine::join_types` keeps the existing numeric promotion compatibility path, then delegates non-numeric structural joins to CoreType before falling back to a plain union. Equal-length tuples now join element-wise through the shared lattice operation.
- `StaticType` remains an AoT backend projection: abstract supertypes, `UnionAll`, `TypeVar`, value parameters, and unknown runtime type objects are not forced into `StaticType`.
- 検証: `timeout 1200 cargo test --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot --lib aot::inference::tests::test_unify_types` 1/1 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot aot::inference::tests::test_unify_types` 1/1 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --lib compile::lattice inference_core` 131/131 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --release --test fixture_tests type_inference:: type_preservation:: type_stability::` 72/72 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass。

### MethodTable structured signature ownership ✅ (Issue #3859)

- `MethodSig` now stores `core_signature: CoreType` as the structured `Tuple{...}` / `UnionAll` signature for newly registered methods, with legacy `params` / `type_params` retained as compatibility projections.
- `MethodTable::add_method` refreshes the structured signature and uses it as the primary duplicate-replacement identity, so methods with identical legacy params but different `where` bounds no longer replace each other.
- Compile-time MethodTable registration now creates and stores the structured signature before duplicate replacement. Dispatch scoring remains on the compatibility projection for this PR to preserve existing Channel/default-argument priority behavior while still passing through `CoreType::specificity()`.
- Tie-breaking now prefers the non-`UnionAll` wrapper projection when a generic constructor/helper and concrete wrapper tie, preserving existing `Channel(5)` dispatch behavior after structured signatures allow both methods to coexist.
- 検証: `timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --lib compile::method_table inference_core::type_core::tests::unionall_rhs_binds_typevars_with_bounds` 14/14 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --release --test fixture_tests dispatch:: where_tests:: tuple:: reflection::` 83/83 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass。

### CoreType UnionAll / TypeVar / Vararg semantic operations ✅ (Issue #3858)

- `CoreType::is_subtype_of` now handles right-hand `UnionAll` patterns with bounded `TypeVar` binding, repeated covariant `TypeVar` diagonal constraints, and tuple `Vararg` subtype checks for the migrated structured subset.
- `CoreType::type_intersect` now computes tuple intersections with trailing `Vararg`, preserving results such as `Tuple{Int64, Vararg{Int64}}`.
- `compile::method_table` upper-bound checks for method type variables now use CoreType directly, so dispatch validation for structured families such as `AbstractVector` no longer depends on a local `JuliaType::from_name` fallback. Legacy bound spellings like `T<:Integer` / `<:` are normalized before entering CoreType to preserve existing where-dispatch behavior.
- 検証: `timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --lib inference_core::type_core::tests::unionall_rhs_binds_typevars_with_bounds inference_core::type_core::tests::diagonal_typevar_tuple_patterns_require_concrete_reuse inference_core::type_core::tests::vararg_typevar_patterns_share_tuple_semantics inference_core::type_core::tests::type_intersection_handles_tuple_elements_and_typeof compile::method_table::tests::typevar_bound_checks_use_coretype_structured_families` 5/5 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --lib inference_core compile::method_table types::tests vm::type_ops::comparison` 145/145 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --release --test fixture_tests dispatch:: where_tests:: reflection:: types_tests::` 112/112 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass。

### CoreType semantic classifier ownership ✅ (Issue #3857)

- Built-in dispatch primitive / abstract numeric / integer-accepting abstract numeric classifiers now live on `CoreType`, so these Julia type semantics have one shared owner instead of being duplicated in `JuliaType`.
- `JuliaType::is_concrete_primitive`, `is_abstract_integer`, `is_abstract_numeric`, and `is_primitive` now project into `CoreType` and preserve the legacy dispatch boundaries through the shared classifier API.
- Unit coverage fixes the classifier boundary for primitive leaves, abstract numeric supertypes, and non-primitive negatives such as `AbstractString`, `Vector{Int64}`, `Nothing`, `Missing`, and `Symbol`.
- 検証: `timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --lib inference_core types::tests::test_specificity types::tests::test_is_concrete types::tests::test_subtype_structured_builtin_families_use_core_type` 42/42 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --lib inference_core types::tests compile::method_table` 127/127 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --release --test fixture_tests dispatch:: types_tests:: type_inference::` 141/141 pass、`timeout 1200 cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass。

### Milestone 17: type core / dispatch / reflection migration ✅ (Issues #3826-#3831)

- Shared `CoreType` is now the semantic bridge used by compiler-side type checks, VM runtime subtype/reflection paths, method-table specificity bridges, and AoT primitive numeric classification.
- `MethodSig::core_signature()` exposes method signatures as structured `Tuple{...}` / `UnionAll` shapes, and runtime typed/untyped dispatch paths now share core hierarchy/specificity facts for migrated cases.
- `RuntimeTypeRegistry` centralizes runtime type-object metadata for `DataType`, `UnionAll`, `TypeVar`, type parameters, and built-in field reflection without local braced-string parsing in reflection builtins.
- Public Base builtin routing is documented as method-dispatch-first, with Rust paths classified as primitive fallback, internal intrinsic, true runtime boundary, or cache compatibility handler. Recent Dict and iterator wrapper fixes keep Pure Julia parametric structs from being shadowed by legacy Rust-backed fallback routes.
- 検証: `timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --lib vm::type_objects vm::builtins_reflection inference_core` 50/50 pass、`reflection::` 23/23 pass、`dispatch::` 23/23 pass、`types_tests::` 57/57 pass、`pure_julia::` 26/26 pass、`type_inference:: type_preservation:: type_stability::` 72/72 pass、`tuple:: where_tests:: kwargs:: kwargs_splat:: varargs::` 66/66 pass、`packages::` 16/16 pass、`pair::` 2/2 pass。Full release fixture sweep は `timeout 1200 cargo nextest run --release` の 20 分制限で 2765/4652 tests 時点まで進み、観測された失敗は timeout による SIGTERM のみ。

## 最新対応 (2026-05-11)

### AoT: native call boundary classification ✅ (Issue #3723)

- `subset_julia_vm/src/aot/native_calls.rs` を追加し、`ccall`, `llvmcall`, `Core.Intrinsics.llvmcall` を AoT native-call boundary として分類。
- 現状は full Julia-compatible `ccall` を実装せず、unsupported `ccall` / `llvmcall` を AoT Core IR conversion で span 付き diagnostic として拒否する。これにより Rust/Cranelift codegen に ordinary call や placeholder として流れない。
- named pass verifier に脱出防止を追加し、手組み AoT IR の `CallStatic/CallDynamic { function: "ccall" | "llvmcall" | "*.ccall" | "*.llvmcall" }` も `InvalidIR` にする。
- future supported path は `AotNativeCallSupport::Supported { abi: AotCallAbi }` を使い、typed ABI data なしの ad-hoc native call 受理を禁止する設計にした。
- ドキュメント: [AOT_NATIVE_CALLS.md](./AOT_NATIVE_CALLS.md)
- 検証: `cargo test --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot --lib aot::native_calls` 4/4 pass、`cargo test --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot --lib test_program_to_aot_ir_rejects` 2/2 pass、`cargo test --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot --lib aot::pass_pipeline` 6/6 pass、`cargo nextest run --release --lib` 1676/1676 pass（ローカルに `timeout` が無いため unwrapped）。

### AoT: rooting and safepoint contract ✅ (Issue #3722)

- `subset_julia_vm/src/aot/rooting.rs` を追加し、runtime `Value` の ownership/rooting state を `Native`, `RuntimeOwned`, `RuntimeBorrowed`, `Rooted`, `Temporary` に分類。Rust backend の現状は dynamic `Value` を owned として扱う契約に固定した。
- runtime/helper call effect を `NonAllocating`, `AllocatingSafepoint`, `UnknownSafepoint` に分類し、dynamic dispatch や allocation-like builtin を safepoint として verifier が扱えるようにした。
- named pass verifier から `verify_aot_rooting_obligations` を実行し、borrowed/temporary runtime value が unrooted のまま safepoint をまたぐ constructed case を `AotError::InvalidIR` で拒否する回帰テストを追加。
- Cranelift backend は runtime `Value` / managed pointer support を満たすまで `Any`, `Unknown`, string/array/tuple/struct を unsupported として拒否し、raw `i64` placeholder 化を避ける。
- ドキュメント: [AOT_ROOTING_SAFETY.md](./AOT_ROOTING_SAFETY.md)
- 検証: `cargo test --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot --lib aot::rooting` 5/5 pass、`cargo test --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot --lib aot::pass_pipeline` 5/5 pass、`cargo test --release -p subset_julia_vm --features cranelift --lib aot::codegen::cranelift` 10/10 pass、`cargo nextest run --release --lib` 1676/1676 pass（ローカルに `timeout` が無いため unwrapped）。

### AoT: named pass diagnostics and verifiers ✅ (Issue #3721)

- `subset_julia_vm/src/aot/pass_pipeline.rs` を追加し、AoT compiler boundary を `AotPassStage` として centralize。stage list は `AfterLowering`, `AfterDCE`, `AfterInference`, `AfterAotIrConversion`, `AfterAbiLowering`, `AfterOptimization`, `BeforeBackendCodegen`。
- `AotPassDiagnostics` が stage ごとの `AotPassStats` (functions/statements/dynamic_calls/structs/globals) と optional dump を保持する。dump は CLI から `--dump-aot-stage=<name|all>` で出せる。
- `verify_aot_program(stage, program)` を追加し、malformed AoT IR を backend codegen より前で止める hook を用意。空の function/parameter/variable/call target/field name、array shape mismatch、index なし index expression を `AotError::InvalidIR` で報告する。
- `src/bin/aot.rs` の source/Core IR compile path は `AfterAotIrConversion`, `AfterOptimization`, `BeforeBackendCodegen` で verifier を実行し、指定 stage の pretty AoT IR dump を出力する。
- 回帰テスト: stage parser/dump selection、stats+dump recording、malformed array shape/call target verifier failure、CLI flag parse を追加。
- 検証: `cargo test --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot --lib aot::pass_pipeline` 5/5 pass、`cargo test --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot --bin aot` 4/4 pass、`cargo nextest run --release --lib` 1676/1676 pass（ローカルに `timeout` が無いため unwrapped）。

### AoT: generated runtime multidispatch dispatchers ✅ (Issue #3720)

- AoT Rust codegen の multidispatch dispatcher をコメント出力から実関数生成に変更。`method_table` は return type も保持し、同名 method 群ごとに `pub fn f(arg0: Value, ...) -> RuntimeResult<Value>` を emitted artifact として生成する。
- dispatcher arm は `Value` pattern (`I64`, `I32`, `F64`, `F32`, `Bool`, `Char`, `Str`, `Nothing`, `Any`) を specialized ABI に unbox し、`f_i64_i64(...)` などの mangled specialization を呼んで `Value::from(...)` で runtime value に戻す。unsupported param/return type の arm は生成せず、no-match は `RuntimeError::method_error`。
- `AotExpr::CallDynamic` は overloaded function の場合、引数を `Value` に box して生成 dispatcher へ routing。fully static call は引き続き exact method に direct call する。
- 回帰テスト: dispatcher 関数生成、static multidispatch call の direct specialization 維持、dynamic call の `Value` 引数 routing を追加。
- 検証: `cargo test --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot --lib aot::codegen::aot_codegen` 92/92 pass、`cargo nextest run --release --lib` 1676/1676 pass（ローカルに `timeout` が無いため unwrapped）。

### AoT: backend-neutral ABI value boundary ✅ (Issue #3719)

- `subset_julia_vm/src/aot/abi.rs` を追加し、AoT IR と backend/codegen の間に `AotAbiClass` / `AotAbiValue` / `AotCallAbi` を導入。値表現を `UnboxedScalar`, `NativeAggregate`, `NativePointer`, `RuntimeBoxed` に分類する backend-neutral な境界を固定した。
- 既存 Rust backend の型 spelling は互換維持のため `StaticType::to_rust_type()` と一致させつつ、`AotCodeGenerator::type_to_rust` は ABI layout 経由で型を取得するよう変更。`Any` / multi-variant `Union` は runtime `Value` boundary、single-variant `Union` は inner ABI class として扱う。
- `AotFunction::call_abi()` を追加し、CodeInstance-like specialization (#3718) の後続で各関数 specialization の params/return ABI を参照できるようにした。
- 回帰テスト: primitive scalar, native heap value, struct aggregate, single/multi `Union`, `Any`, call ABI の native/runtime boxed 判定を追加。
- 検証: `cargo test --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot --lib aot::abi` 8/8 pass、`cargo test --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot --lib call_abi` 2/2 pass、`cargo test --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot --lib aot::codegen::aot_codegen` 89/89 pass、`cargo nextest run --release --lib` 1676/1676 pass（ローカルに `timeout` が無いため unwrapped）。

### AoT: CodeInstance-like specialization units ✅ (Issue #3718)

- `subset_julia_vm/src/aot/specialization.rs` を追加し、`CodeInstanceKey` / `CodeInstance` / `SpecializationQueue` を AoT 共通の特殊化単位として導入。関数名 + 引数型 tuple、source IR、推論済み signature / return type、dependency edge、emitted artifact slot、state を 1 箇所で保持できるようにした。
- `TypeInferenceEngine` の `call_sites: HashMap<String, Vec<Vec<StaticType>>>` を `SpecializationQueue` に置き換え、root call-site と関数本体内の nested call を同じ queue に enqueue。関数本体を走査するときは active owner を立て、`outer(Int64) -> inner(Int64)` のような依存 edge を記録する。
- 既存の call-site specialization 挙動は `observed_args_for(function)` 経由で維持しつつ、final analyze pass で source `Function` と `FunctionSignature` / return type を該当 CodeInstance に attach する。
- 回帰テスト: queue dedupe / dependency enqueue / display の unit test と、nested call の CodeInstance dependency を検証する inference test を追加。
- 検証: `cargo nextest run --release --lib` 1676/1676 pass（ローカルに `timeout` が無いため unwrapped）。`aot` feature 下の新規/関連 test は `cargo test --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot --lib code_instance`, `call_site_array`, `dependency_edges`, `display_uses`, `mandelbrot_escape` で pass。`cargo nextest run --release -p subset_julia_vm --features aot --lib` 全体は既存 `aot::analyze::tests::test_convert_function_flattens_let_block_assign_expr` で fail。

### Lowering: statement `_with_ctx` 重複 sweep ✅ (Issue #3639)

- `subset_julia_vm/src/lowering/stmt/` の statement lowering 主要ペアを `Option<&LambdaContext>` の共通実装へ統合。`assignment`, `for`, `if`, `try`, `while`, statement/block entrypoint, `return`, `global`, `local` の context 版と非 context 版で同じロジックを二重保持しない構造にした。
- public API と既存 call sites の互換性を保つため `*_with_ctx` wrapper は残し、wrapper から共通実装に `Some(lambda_ctx)` を渡す。非 context 版は `None` を渡す。
- `if @generated ... else ... end` の既存 semantics 差分は維持。通常 lowering は Phase 3 の quote unquote を試し、lambda context 版は従来通り fallback branch 実行のみ。
- 差分は pure refactor。`cargo check --release -p subset_julia_vm` pass（ローカルに `timeout` が無いため unwrapped）。

### Lowering: `lower_const_statement` / `_with_ctx` 重複解消 pilot ✅ (Issue #3639)

- `subset_julia_vm/src/lowering/stmt/mod.rs` の `lower_const_statement` / `lower_const_statement_with_ctx` / `lower_const_statement_impl` の 3 関数を `lower_const_statement(walker, node, lambda_ctx: Option<&LambdaContext>)` 一本に統合。`_impl` ヘルパは廃止、呼び出し側 (`lower_stmt`, `lower_stmt_with_ctx`) は `None` / `Some(lambda_ctx)` を渡す形に更新。
- Issue #3639 が指摘する 30 ペアの先行 pilot として最小スコープで着地。pure refactor のため挙動は不変。残り 29 ペアは別 PR で sweep 予定。
- 検証: `cargo nextest run --release --test fixture_tests constants::` 9/9 pass、`cargo nextest run --lib` 1676/1676 pass、`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean。

## 最新対応 (2026-05-10)

### Prevention: 128-bit / Float16 type-drift の体系的監査 ✅ (Issue #3699)

- **Type-preservation matrix** フィクスチャ 6 本を `subset_julia_vm/tests/fixtures/type_preservation/` に追加。`{+, -, *, /, ÷, %, ==, <, <=, >, >=}` × `{Int128, UInt128, Float16}` × `{same-type, mixed-with-Int64, mixed-with-Float64}` × `{inline-from-constructor, variable-bound}`。Issue 本文の指定通り inline / variable-bound の両形式を併記しており、`UInt128 == UInt128` の i64::MAX 超 (Issue #3696 の元バグ) を含む。
- マトリクスが捕捉した実バグを修正: `vm/dynamic_ops/mod.rs::dynamic_div` に F16/F16 ほか F16 系 9 アームを追加 (`dynamic_mod` の F16 アームと完全対称)。これにより `div(::Float16, ::Float16)` (= `floor(::Float16 / ::Float16)`) が runtime fallback で `Cannot divide F16 and F16` を出さず Float16 を保つ。
- **静的解析スクリプト** `scripts/check_div_specializations.sh` を新設。`base/int.jl` の `function div(x::TN, y::TN)` を Int8/16/32/64/128, UInt8/16/32/64/128 の 10 種すべてについて確認。`.github/workflows/ci.yml` の `code-audits` ジョブに登録 (shellcheck + run step)。bash 3.2 互換、`docs/vm/CODE_AUDITS.md` Audit Policies bullet 追加。
- **ドキュメント**: `docs/vm/TYPE_PRESERVATION.md` の Part 3 に **4 層モデル** (L1 inference → L2 early-route → L3 method-table → L4 runtime fallback) と各 primitive × 各層の責務テーブルを追加。**Option A vs Option B** (`WidePrimitiveOp` instruction) の設計選択を文書末尾に記録。`docs/vm/CHECKLISTS.md` に "New Primitive Type / New Operator Method" チェックリストを追加。
- 検証: `cargo nextest run --release --test fixture_tests type_preservation::` 6/6 pass、`numeric::` 17/17 pass、`promotion::` / `arithmetic::` / `types::` 57/57 pass、`cargo nextest run --lib` clean、`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean、`bash scripts/check_div_specializations.sh` / `check_audit_scripts_bash3_compat.sh` / `check_fixture_test_names.sh` / shellcheck すべて pass。

### Set algebra Pure Julia migration ✅ (Issue #3724)

- `union`/`intersect`/`setdiff`/`symdiff`/`issubset`/`isdisjoint`/`issetequal` および mutating 変種 (`union!` ほか) について、Set/Vector/mixed Set+Vector 形の Pure Julia method を `subset_julia_vm/src/julia/base/set.jl` に集約。Vector 経路は線形検索 (`_vec_contains`) で `isequal` ベースのため Float64 など DictKey 非対応要素もカバー。
- `BuiltinId::Set{Union,Intersect,Setdiff,Symdiff,Issubset,Isdisjoint,Issetequal}` と `SetUnionMut`/`SetIntersectMut`/`SetSetdiffMut`/`SetSymdiffMut` を enum・`from_name`・`name` から削除し、`vm/builtins_sets/set_ops.rs` のハンドラを撤去。`shared.rs` の未使用ヘルパも削除。
- `compile_builtin_set` (`compile/expr/builtin_set.rs`) と `compile_builtin_call` の短絡呼び出しを撤去。`is_base_function` / inventory test からも該当名を除去したため Set 代数呼び出しは必ず method dispatch を経由する。
- `_set_push!`, `_set_delete!`, `_set_in`, `_set_empty!`, `_set_length` 等の内部 intrinsic は維持。`SetNew`/`SetPush`/`SetDelete`/`SetIn`/`SetEmpty` の public-name route も既存の Pure Julia wrapper 経由で維持。
